# Introduction

> Source route: /manual/getting-started/introduction
> Source file: manual/getting-started/introduction.md

DataVo is an embedded database engine written in C# for `.NET 10`. It runs directly inside your application process with no external server, no native DLLs, and full Native AOT compatibility — combining SQL, LSM storage, columnar indexes, vector search, and live reactive views in one library.

```csharp
using DataVo.Core;
using DataVo.Core.StorageEngine.Config;

using var db = new DataVoContext(new DataVoConfig { StorageMode = StorageMode.InMemory });
db.Execute("CREATE DATABASE Demo");
db.Execute("USE Demo");
db.Execute("CREATE TABLE players (Id INT PRIMARY KEY, Name VARCHAR(80), Score INT)");
db.Execute("INSERT INTO players (Id, Name, Score) VALUES (1, 'Ada', 950)");

var result = db.Execute("SELECT Name, Score FROM players WHERE Id = 1")[0];
Console.WriteLine($"{result.Data[0]["Name"]}: {result.Data[0]["Score"]}");
```

## Choose Your Path

<div class="path-grid">
  <a class="path-card" href="./quickstart">
    <strong>Embedded .NET Engine</strong>
    Start with in-memory or crash-safe LSM storage and run SQL in 60 seconds.
  </a>
  <a class="path-card" href="../client-interfaces/source-generators">
    <strong>Roslyn Native AOT</strong>
    Compile typed LINQ and <code>[DataVoQuery]</code> methods at build time with zero reflection.
  </a>
  <a class="path-card" href="../fundamentals/reactive-views">
    <strong>Live Z-Set Reactive Views</strong>
    Maintain SQL and LINQ views incrementally with pull-drain delta notifications.
  </a>
  <a class="path-card" href="../fundamentals/datavo-sync">
    <strong>DataVo-Sync</strong>
    Offline-first bidirectional PostgreSQL synchronization (commercial add-on).
  </a>
</div>

## Architecture Overview

Every client interface — `DataVoContext`, compiled LINQ, ADO.NET, Dapper, and the EF Core bridge — routes into the same parser, typed query planner, and storage engines.

<div class="sketch-diagram">
  <img class="light-only" src="/manual/fig-01-architecture-light.svg" alt="DataVo architecture showing client interfaces, SQL parser, typed fast-path planner, and InMemory and LSM storage engines" />
  <img class="dark-only" src="/manual/fig-01-architecture-dark.svg" alt="DataVo architecture showing client interfaces, SQL parser, typed fast-path planner, and InMemory and LSM storage engines" />
</div>

### Storage Engines

| Mode | Backing Engine | Best For |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `StorageMode.InMemory` | Packed contiguous row buffers (`FlatRowStore`) | Ephemeral caches, tests, simulations, game state |
| `StorageMode.Lsm` | Commit log (WAL), arena MemTables, memory-mapped SSTables, 4,096-row columnar segments | Production embedded persistence with `LsmStrictFsync = true` |
| `StorageMode.Disk` | Legacy paged file engine | Reading existing v0.1/v0.2 data only; prefer `Lsm` for new work |

### Typed Fast Paths & Vector Search

Queries are first offered to **typed execution paths** (single-table scans, integer-key hash joins, columnar aggregates, index-driven joins, and filtered vector search) that read cells straight from stored bytes without building per-row dictionaries. If a query shape is outside the fast paths, it falls back seamlessly to the general evaluator with identical semantics.

`VECTOR(n)` columns are first-class relational columns backed by SIMD-accelerated `FLAT` (exact) or `HNSW` (approximate graph with cost-based exact fallback) indexes, keeping embeddings and metadata in one transaction log.

## Packages at a Glance

| Package | Purpose | Native AOT |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DataVo.Core` | Embedded engine, `DataVoContext`, storage engines, vector & reactive APIs | Yes |
| `DataVo.Generators` | Roslyn source generator for `[DataVoTable]`, `[DataVoQuery]`, and compiled LINQ | Yes |
| `DataVo.Data` | Standard ADO.NET provider (`DataVoConnection`, `DataVoCommand`, `DataVoDataReader`) + Dapper | Yes |
| `DataVo.EntityFrameworkCore` | Experimental EF Core bridge (`UseDataVo(...)`); not a standalone provider | No |

## Where DataVo Fits — and Where It Doesn't

- **Strong fit:** Local-first `.NET 10` apps, game tooling, simulations, and retrieval workloads that combine relational filtering with vector search. On warm caches, v0.4 outperforms SQLite on key lookups, low-cardinality `GROUP BY`, integer-key joins, columnar aggregates, and filtered vector search.
- **Not a fit:** Client/server deployments, multi-process writes to one directory (`datavo.lock` enforces single-process ownership), stored procedures/triggers, or serializable predicate locking. For whole-table analytics over tens of millions of rows, DuckDB remains orders of magnitude faster.
- **Need multi-device PostgreSQL sync?** [DataVo-Sync](/manual/fundamentals/datavo-sync) is a separate commercial add-on providing offline-first bidirectional sync over WebSocket/HTTP with wire v2 + Brotli.

## See Also

- [Installation & Packages](/manual/getting-started/installation) — NuGet packages (`0.4.0-rc.1`) and `.NET 10` requirements.

# Installation & Packages

> Source route: /manual/getting-started/installation
> Source file: manual/getting-started/installation.md

DataVo ships as four NuGet packages on `nuget.org`, with `DataVo.Core` as the foundation. The current release is **0.4.0-rc.1 (release candidate)**, so pass `--prerelease` when installing.

```bash
dotnet add package DataVo.Core --prerelease
dotnet add package DataVo.Generators --prerelease
dotnet add package DataVo.Data --prerelease
dotnet add package DataVo.EntityFrameworkCore --prerelease
```

## Package Reference

| Package | Install When You Need | Includes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DataVo.Core` | Embedded SQL, typed tables, vector search, reactive views | `DataVoContext`, `InMemory`/`Lsm`/`Disk` engines, HNSW/FLAT/columnar indexes |
| `DataVo.Generators` | Build-time compiled LINQ and `[DataVoQuery]` methods | Roslyn source generator & interceptors (build-time only, no runtime dependency) |
| `DataVo.Data` | Standard ADO.NET or Dapper micro-ORM | `DataVoConnection`, `DataVoCommand`, `DataVoDataReader`, `DataVoTransaction`, `DataVoParameter` |
| `DataVo.EntityFrameworkCore` | Experimental EF Core `DbContext` bridge | `UseDataVo(...)`, `EnsureDataVoCreated()`, `DataVoVectorDbFunctions` |

## Recommended Combinations

| Workload | Packages to Add |
| --- | --- |
| Embedded SQL & `DataVoTable<T>` | `DataVo.Core` |
| Zero-allocation compiled LINQ & AOT | `DataVo.Core` + `DataVo.Generators` |
| ADO.NET or Dapper | `DataVo.Data` *(transitively brings `DataVo.Core`)* |
| Existing EF Core models | `DataVo.EntityFrameworkCore` *(transitively brings `DataVo.Core`)* |

## Requirements

- **`.NET 10` (`net10.0`):** Published packages target `net10.0`. Multi-target packages (`net8.0`, `net9.0`, `net10.0`, `netstandard2.1`) are planned for v0.5; see [Status & Roadmap](/manual/getting-started/roadmap#unity-evaluation-status) for Unity evaluation details.
- **Native AOT:** `DataVo.Core`, `DataVo.Data`, and `DataVo.Generators` build with trim and AOT analyzers (`IL2026`, `IL3050`) as errors. `DataVo.EntityFrameworkCore` is excluded from Native AOT.
- **C# Interceptors:** `DataVo.Generators` ships MSBuild `.props` that automatically register `DataVo.Generated` in `InterceptorsNamespaces`.
- **Building from source:** Run `dotnet pack DataVo.sln -c Release` to produce local `.nupkg` files in `artifacts/packages`.

## Verify Your Installation

```csharp
using DataVo.Core;
using DataVo.Core.StorageEngine.Config;

using var db = new DataVoContext(new DataVoConfig { StorageMode = StorageMode.InMemory });
db.Execute("CREATE DATABASE Smoke");
db.Execute("USE Smoke");
db.Execute("CREATE TABLE players (Id INT PRIMARY KEY, Name VARCHAR(80))");
db.Execute("INSERT INTO players (Id, Name) VALUES (1, 'Ada')");

Console.WriteLine(db.Execute("SELECT Id, Name FROM players")[0].Data.Count); // 1
```

# Quickstart

> Source route: /manual/getting-started/quickstart
> Source file: manual/getting-started/quickstart.md

Get a working DataVo database running in a `.NET 10` console app in under a minute. You will start with `StorageMode.InMemory` for zero-setup iteration, then switch to crash-safe `StorageMode.Lsm` with a two-line config change.

```csharp
using DataVo.Core;
using DataVo.Core.StorageEngine.Config;

using var db = new DataVoContext(new DataVoConfig { StorageMode = StorageMode.InMemory });

db.Execute("CREATE DATABASE GameDb");
db.Execute("USE GameDb");

db.Execute("""
    CREATE TABLE players (
        Id INT PRIMARY KEY,
        Name VARCHAR(80),
        Score INT,
        Region VARCHAR(32)
    );
    """);

db.Execute("INSERT INTO players (Id, Name, Score, Region) VALUES (1, 'Ada', 980, 'EU')");
db.Execute("INSERT INTO players (Id, Name, Score, Region) VALUES (2, 'Grace', 1120, 'US')");

var result = db.Execute("SELECT Id, Name, Score FROM players WHERE Score >= 900 ORDER BY Score DESC LIMIT 10")[0];
foreach (var row in result.Data)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{row["Id"]}: {row["Name"]} ({row["Score"]})");
}
```

## 1. Create a Project and Install `DataVo.Core`

```bash
dotnet new console -n DataVoQuickstart
cd DataVoQuickstart
dotnet add package DataVo.Core --prerelease
```

## 2. Open a `DataVoContext`

Construct a `DataVoContext` with a `DataVoConfig`. Always dispose the context with `using` so background flushes and file locks release cleanly.

```csharp
using DataVo.Core;
using DataVo.Core.StorageEngine.Config;

using var db = new DataVoContext(new DataVoConfig
{
    StorageMode = StorageMode.InMemory
});
```

## 3. Create a Database and Table

DataVo hosts multiple logical databases inside one context. Create a database, select it with `USE`, and define your table schema.

```csharp
db.Execute("CREATE DATABASE GameDb");
db.Execute("USE GameDb");

db.Execute("""
    CREATE TABLE players (
        Id INT PRIMARY KEY,
        Name VARCHAR(80),
        Score INT,
        Region VARCHAR(32)
    );
    """);
```

## 4. Insert and Query with Parameters

Use prepared statements (`db.Prepare`) when running the same query repeatedly to avoid re-parsing SQL and to bind parameters safely.

```csharp
var insert = db.Prepare(
    "INSERT INTO players (Id, Name, Score, Region) VALUES (@id, @name, @score, @region)");

insert.Execute(
    new DataVoQueryParameter("id", 1),
    new DataVoQueryParameter("name", "Ada"),
    new DataVoQueryParameter("score", 980),
    new DataVoQueryParameter("region", "EU"));

var topPlayers = db.Prepare("SELECT Id, Name, Score FROM players WHERE Score >= @min ORDER BY Score DESC");
var result = topPlayers.Execute(new DataVoQueryParameter("min", 900))[0];

foreach (var row in result.Data)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{row["Id"]}: {row["Name"]} ({row["Score"]})");
}
```

## 5. Persist Data with LSM Storage

Switch from `StorageMode.InMemory` to `StorageMode.Lsm` to persist tables to disk with a crash-safe write-ahead log (`LsmStrictFsync = true` by default).

```csharp
using var db = new DataVoContext(new DataVoConfig
{
    StorageMode = StorageMode.Lsm,
    DiskStoragePath = "./datavo_lsm_data",
    LsmStrictFsync = true
});
```

::: info DataVo Extension
Add `DataVo.Generators` and annotate a C# `Player` class with `[DataVoTable("players")]` to query `db.Table<Player>()` with compile-time LINQ and zero per-row allocations.
:::

## See Also

- [Choosing an Interface](/manual/getting-started/choosing-an-interface) — Compare SQL, Compiled LINQ, ADO.NET, Dapper, and EF Core.
- [Storage Modes](/manual/fundamentals/storage-modes) — Understand `InMemory`, `Lsm`, and `Disk` trade-offs.
- [DataVoContext API](/manual/client-interfaces/datavo-context-api) — Full reference for prepared statements, typed writes, and streaming.
- [Vector Search](/manual/fundamentals/vector-search) — Store `VECTOR(n)` embeddings alongside relational columns.

# Choosing an Interface

> Source route: /manual/getting-started/choosing-an-interface
> Source file: manual/getting-started/choosing-an-interface.md

DataVo exposes five ways to query the same embedded engine. They differ in ergonomics and per-call allocation overhead — not in storage modes, durability, or index support — and you can freely mix them in the same process.

## Decision Matrix

| Interface | Packages | Best For | Per-Call Overhead | Native AOT |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Compiled LINQ](/manual/client-interfaces/compiled-linq) | `DataVo.Core` + `DataVo.Generators` | Hot paths: point lookups, filtered scans, aggregates, projections | Lowest — reads stored bytes directly; zero-alloc aggregates | Yes |
| [`DataVoContext`](/manual/client-interfaces/datavo-context-api) | `DataVo.Core` | Ad-hoc SQL, DDL, prepared statements, vector search, reactive views | Low with `db.Prepare(...)`; materializes dictionaries on general path | Yes |
| [ADO.NET](/manual/client-interfaces/ado-net) | `DataVo.Data` | Libraries expecting `DbConnection`, `DbCommand`, `DbDataReader` | Same engine behind standard `System.Data.Common` wrappers | Yes |
| [Dapper](/manual/client-interfaces/dapper) | `DataVo.Data` + `Dapper` | Plain SQL mapped to POCOs with familiar micro-ORM APIs | ADO.NET overhead plus Dapper row mapping | Per Dapper |
| [EF Core Bridge](/manual/client-interfaces/entity-framework) | `DataVo.EntityFrameworkCore` | Existing EF Core `DbContext` models (experimental preview) | Highest — EF Core infrastructure sits above DataVo | No |

**Rule of thumb:** start with `DataVoContext` for DDL and general SQL, move hot-path reads and aggregates to **Compiled LINQ**, use **ADO.NET / Dapper** when integrating existing SQL codebases, and use the **EF Core bridge** only when you already depend on EF Core.

## How Every Interface Connects

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  App["Your .NET 10 App"]
  App --> LINQ["Compiled LINQ (DataVo.Generators)"]
  App --> Ctx["DataVoContext (DataVo.Core)"]
  App --> Ado["ADO.NET (DataVo.Data)"]
  App --> EF["EF Core Bridge (DataVo.EntityFrameworkCore)"]
  Dapper["Dapper"] --> Ado
  LINQ --> Core["DataVo.Core Engine"]
  Ctx --> Core
  Ado --> Core
  EF --> Core
  Core --> Storage["InMemory | LSM | Disk (legacy)"]
```

## The Same Query, Five Ways

Counting players with `Score >= 1000` in the `players` table:

**1. `DataVoContext` (SQL)**

```csharp
var result = db.Execute("SELECT COUNT(*) AS Total FROM players WHERE Score >= 1000")[0];
object? total = result.Data[0]["Total"];
```

**2. Compiled LINQ (`DataVo.Generators`)**

```csharp
int total = db.Table<Player>().Where(1000, static (p, min) => p.Score >= min).Count();
```

**3. ADO.NET (`DataVo.Data`)**

```csharp
using var cmd = connection.CreateCommand();
cmd.CommandText = "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM players WHERE Score >= @min";
cmd.Parameters.AddWithValue("@min", 1000);
object? total = cmd.ExecuteScalar();
```

**4. Dapper**

```csharp
int total = connection.ExecuteScalar<int>(
    "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM players WHERE Score >= @min",
    new { min = 1000 });
```

**5. Entity Framework Core Bridge**

```csharp
List<Player> matches = efContext.QueryFromDataVo<Player>(q =>
    q.Where(static p => p.Score >= 1000));
int total = matches.Count;
```

::: info DataVo Extension
Compiled LINQ reads the `Score` cell directly from packed row buffers without allocating `Player` instances. See [Compiled Scan Kernels](/manual/internals/compiled-scan-kernels) for how the generated code works.
:::

## See Also

- [DataVoContext API](/manual/client-interfaces/datavo-context-api) — Primary SQL, prepared statement, and batch write API.
- [Roslyn Source Generators](/manual/client-interfaces/source-generators) — `[DataVoTable]`, `[DataVoQuery]`, and build-time codegen.
- [Compiled LINQ](/manual/client-interfaces/compiled-linq) — Supported LINQ operators and interceptor setup.

# Status & Roadmap

> Source route: /manual/getting-started/roadmap
> Source file: manual/getting-started/roadmap.md

The current release on NuGet is **0.4.0-rc.1 (release candidate, 17 November 2026)**, shipping both the **v0.3** and **v0.4** milestones on `.NET 10`. This page defines the release-candidate contract, subsystem status, architectural boundaries, and what is planned for **v0.5**.

## Release Candidate Contract

- **Supported shape:** One `.NET 10` process owns a database directory (enforced via `datavo.lock`) or an in-memory database, executing SQL or compiled LINQ through `DataVoContext`, ADO.NET, or the EF Core bridge.
- **Durability:** Under `StorageMode.Lsm` with `LsmStrictFsync = true` (default), acknowledged commits are flushed to stable storage. With `LsmStrictFsync = false`, writes hand off to the OS page cache. See [LSM & Durability](/manual/fundamentals/lsm-and-durability).
- **Isolation:** Explicit transactions provide MVCC snapshot isolation with read-your-own-writes and first-committer-wins conflict detection, but not serializable predicate locking (write skew is possible). See [Transactions & MVCC](/manual/fundamentals/transactions-and-mvcc).
- **On-disk format:** v0.4 writes SSTable format version 8 and still reads versions 2, 4, and 6, but does not yet carry a long-term cross-version compatibility guarantee. Keep an export or seed script for critical data.
- **SQL `DATE` contract:** SQL `DATE` materializes as `DataVo.Core.DataVoDate` in row APIs (`CellValue.AsDate()`, compiled `GetDate`), with explicit `FromDateOnly` / `ToDateOnly` / `AsDateOnly` / `GetDateOnly` adapters for `System.DateOnly`.

## Subsystem Status

| Subsystem | Status | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DataVoContext` & SQL dialect | Release candidate | DataVo's own dialect; see [SQL Compatibility](/manual/sql/compatibility) |
| `InMemory` & `Lsm` storage | Release candidate | Active engines; `Disk` (paged) is legacy |
| Transactions & MVCC | Release candidate | Snapshot isolation, savepoints, atomic `COMMIT` |
| Vector search (`HNSW`, `FLAT`) | Release candidate | Cosine (`<=>`) and L2 (`<->`), cost-based exact fallback |
| Columnar indexes & SSTable segments | Release candidate | In-memory buffers + persisted 4,096-row zone-mapped segments |
| Live Reactive Views (Z-set IVM) | Release candidate | Pull-drain subscriptions via `Subscribe` / `SubscribeZeroAlloc` |
| `DataVo.Generators` & Native AOT | Release candidate | Trim/AOT analyzers (`IL2026`, `IL3050`) enforced as errors |
| `DataVo.Data` (ADO.NET & Dapper) | Release candidate | Standard `System.Data.Common` types; no `DbProviderFactory` |
| `DataVo.EntityFrameworkCore` | Preview bridge | Query/DML bridge only; no migrations, excluded from AOT |
| `DataVo.Browser` (WebAssembly) | Experimental | Powers the docs playground; not published on npm |
| `DataVo-Sync` (PostgreSQL sync) | Commercial add-on | Separate proprietary product; see [DataVo-Sync](/manual/fundamentals/datavo-sync) |

## Explicit Boundaries

| Out of Scope / Boundary | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Multi-process directory access | Rejected by `datavo.lock`; multiple contexts in one process share one engine |
| Serializable isolation / phantom locks | No range or predicate locks |
| Network server / wire protocol | Embedded only (`DataVo.Server` PG wire bridge is planned, unscheduled) |
| Stored procedures, triggers, UDFs | Keep procedural logic in C# |
| Replication / high availability | Embedded engine; use [DataVo-Sync](/manual/fundamentals/datavo-sync) for PG sync |

## Milestone History & v0.5 Plan

### v0.2 — Embedded Engine Baseline
- LSM storage with WAL, arena MemTables, background SSTable flushes/compaction, and clustered `INT`/`GUID` primary keys.
- Native AOT compliance (`IL2026`/`IL3050` as errors), zero-alloc `RowRef` scans, `VECTOR(n)` with `HNSW`/`FLAT`, and NuGet packaging.

### v0.3 — Columnar Indexes & Compact Rows *(shipped in `0.4.0-rc.1`)*
- `[Columnar]` / `USING COLUMNAR` indexes with SIMD-accelerated single-table aggregates.
- Packed `FlatRowStore` in-memory layout (49.2 B/row in benchmarks, 52.1 ns PK lookup).

### v0.4 — Columnar SSTables, Correctness & Typed Execution *(published as `0.4.0-rc.1`)*
- **Out-of-core columnar SSTables (format v8):** 4,096-row segments with NULL/NaN masks, min/max zone maps, and incremental shadow/delete vectors.
- **Oracle-verified correctness:** Fixed 5 cross-engine oracle bugs (`B1`–`B5`), `WHERE ... HAVING` without `GROUP BY`, `BIT` predicate binding, and culture-invariant `DOUBLE` lookups.
- **Typed execution:** `OR`/`LIKE` fast paths, integer-key hash joins, index-driven joins, dense bit-set anti-joins, unboxed `GROUP BY`, UTF-8 byte matching, and in-place top-k.
- **Vector search:** HNSW diversity heuristic on by default (100% recall@10 on clustered data), cost-based exact scan fallback, SQL `WITH (...)` HNSW parameters, and pre-optimized SIMD kernels.

### v0.5 — Native Interop & Client Ergonomics *(planned)*
- **Track A (Native Interop):** Native AOT C ABI (`dv_open`, `dv_exec`, `dv_prepare`) for C/Python/Rust/Go, zero-copy Apache Arrow C Data Interface export from columnar buffers/SSTables, and a reference Python binding.
- **Track B (Client Applications):**
  - *Done:* Build-time compiled `OrderBy`/`ThenBy`, `Skip`/`Take`, `Select` projections, and single-table `ExecuteUpdate`/`ExecuteDelete` in `DataVo.Generators`.
  - *Planned:* 2D geographic WGS84 points with haversine distance and spatial indexing, plus multi-target NuGet packages (`net8.0`, `net9.0`, `net10.0`, `netstandard2.1`).

## Unity Evaluation Status {#unity-evaluation-status}

Unity is an **evaluation target**, not a supported runtime. The public `DataVo.Core` package ships `net10.0` only; `DataVoEnablePortableTarget=true` produces an experimental local `netstandard2.1` candidate.

::: details Unity Evaluation Matrix (Unity 6000.5.4f1)
| Target / Boundary | Status | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unity 6000.5.4f1 Editor (macOS) | Narrow smoke pass | EditMode smoke suite passes on local portable candidate |
| macOS IL2CPP Player | Narrow smoke pass | Medium-stripping Player builds and passes type-binding + Disk/LSM reopen smoke |
| Windows x64 IL2CPP | Unverified | Requires separate Player proof |
| Direct Burst calls | Unsupported by design | Managed engine types cannot run inside Burst jobs |
:::

## See Also

- [Limits & Unsupported Features](/manual/reference/limits) — Exact engine limits and unsupported SQL/API features.
- [DataVo vs SQLite](/manual/performance/datavo-vs-sqlite) — v0.4 benchmark findings and correctness notes.
- [LSM & Durability](/manual/fundamentals/lsm-and-durability) — WAL fsync modes and crash recovery guarantees.

# Storage Modes

> Source route: /manual/fundamentals/storage-modes
> Source file: manual/fundamentals/storage-modes.md

`StorageMode` selects where DataVo stores table rows and how writes survive process restarts. Pick `InMemory` for ephemeral workloads and tests, or `Lsm` for durable on-disk persistence.

```csharp
using DataVo.Core;
using DataVo.Core.StorageEngine.Config;

// Ephemeral in-memory database (default)
using var db = new DataVoContext(new DataVoConfig
{
    StorageMode = StorageMode.InMemory
});

// Durable log-structured database on disk
using var persisted = new DataVoContext(new DataVoConfig
{
    StorageMode = StorageMode.Lsm,
    DiskStoragePath = "./datavo_lsm_data",
    LsmStrictFsync = true
});
```

## Comparing Storage Modes

| Mode | Durability & Memory | Write Path | Best For |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `StorageMode.InMemory` | Ephemeral; packed chunks in RAM | Direct append into `FlatRowStore` + hash/sorted PK map | Unit tests, caches, game state, low-latency ephemeral datasets |
| `StorageMode.Lsm` | Durable (`commit.wal` + `.sst`); memory-mapped reads | Commit log -> 32 MB MemTable -> background SSTable flush & compaction | Production embedded persistence, write-heavy and local-first apps |
| `StorageMode.Disk` *(Legacy)* | File-backed with optional WAL | Page/file append; **not crash-safe for `UPDATE`** | Reading existing legacy directories only |
| `StorageMode.Wasm` *(Experimental)* | Browser/OPFS via `WasmStorageEngine` (falls back to in-memory) | Delegated to injected WASM engine | Interactive browser playground (`DataVo.Browser`); not on npm |
| `StorageMode.Custom` | Defined by your `IStorageEngine` | Delegated to `CustomStorageEngine` | Custom storage adapters, encryption wrappers, or test mocks |

## `InMemory` and `FlatRowStore`

`StorageMode.InMemory` is the default when you omit `StorageMode`. Internally, it is backed by `FlatRowStore`, a packed chunked row store that lays out fixed-width cells in contiguous memory buffers instead of allocating one CLR object per row. Integer primary keys use an in-memory hash map for point lookups and maintain a sorted key copy on demand for range scans.

> `FlatRowStore` is an internal engine component, not a `StorageMode` enum value. Always configure `StorageMode.InMemory`.

## `Lsm` vs Legacy `Disk`

Use `StorageMode.Lsm` for all new persistent applications. It provides single-record crash atomicity, clustered `INT`/`GUID` primary keys, memory-mapped SSTables, persistent secondary indexes, and out-of-core columnar segments. See [LSM & Durability](/manual/fundamentals/lsm-and-durability) for tuning `LsmStrictFsync` and recovery behavior.

`StorageMode.Disk` is kept solely so older data directories remain readable. It receives no new durability work and performs `UPDATE` as two separate durable steps (write new row, tombstone old row), which means a crash between steps can lose the updated row.

## `Wasm` and `Custom` Backends

Both modes accept an `IStorageEngine` instance on `DataVoConfig`:

```csharp
using var customDb = new DataVoContext(new DataVoConfig
{
    StorageMode = StorageMode.Custom,
    CustomStorageEngine = myEngine
});
```

For `StorageMode.Wasm`, set `WasmStorageEngine` to an OPFS-backed or browser storage implementation; if left `null`, DataVo falls back to an in-memory backend.

## Directory Sharing and Locking

For `Lsm` and `Disk`, DataVo serves one engine per directory per process:

- **Within one process:** Multiple `DataVoContext` instances and ADO.NET connections targeting the same `DiskStoragePath` share a single engine until the last handle is disposed. Their configurations must match, or the second open throws `DatabaseInUseException`.
- **Across processes:** DataVo holds a `datavo.lock` file while the directory is open. Opening the same directory from a second process throws `DatabaseInUseException`.

## See Also

- [LSM & Durability](/manual/fundamentals/lsm-and-durability) — WAL commit atomicity, strict vs. relaxed fsync, and SSTable layout
- [Configuration Reference](/manual/reference/configuration) — Complete list of `DataVoConfig` properties and defaults
- [Transactions & MVCC](/manual/fundamentals/transactions-and-mvcc) — Snapshot isolation and concurrency across storage modes

---

# LSM & Durability

> Source route: /manual/fundamentals/lsm-and-durability
> Source file: manual/fundamentals/lsm-and-durability.md

`StorageMode.Lsm` is DataVo's durable storage engine, built on a log-structured merge tree with a single directory-wide commit log (`commit.wal`), arena-backed MemTables, and memory-mapped immutable SSTables.

```csharp
using DataVo.Core;
using DataVo.Core.StorageEngine.Config;

using var db = new DataVoContext(new DataVoConfig
{
    StorageMode = StorageMode.Lsm,
    DiskStoragePath = "./datavo_lsm_data",
    LsmStrictFsync = true,          // default: wait for stable storage on commit
    ClusteredPrimaryKeys = true     // default: store single INT/GUID PK tables clustered
});

db.Execute("CREATE DATABASE App; USE App;");
db.Execute("CREATE TABLE players (id INT PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR, score INT)");
db.Execute("INSERT INTO players (id, name, score) VALUES (1, 'Ada', 250)");
```

## Write Path and SSTables

Every statement (or explicit `COMMIT`) appends one checksummed record to `commit.wal`, then applies mutations to each table's arena-backed active MemTable. When a MemTable reaches 32 MB, DataVo freezes it, swaps in a fresh MemTable, and flushes the frozen generation on a background thread into an immutable `.sst` file.

<div class="sketch-diagram">
  <img class="light-only" src="/manual/fig-02-lsm-write-path-light.svg" alt="LSM write path from commit.wal to MemTable, background SSTable flush, manifest edit, and compaction" />
  <img class="dark-only" src="/manual/fig-02-lsm-write-path-dark.svg" alt="LSM write path from commit.wal to MemTable, background SSTable flush, manifest edit, and compaction" />
</div>

Each SSTable is written sequentially to a temporary file, fsynced, atomically renamed, and published in one manifest edit before older `commit.wal` records are pruned:

- **4 KiB data blocks + Bloom filters:** Sorted entries with a sparse block index and per-file blocked Bloom filter let point lookups skip absent files and touch at most one block on a hit.
- **Memory-mapped reads (`LsmReadMode`):** `LsmReadMode.Auto` (default) memory-maps `.sst` files on 64-bit platforms so reads hit the OS page cache with no syscall per lookup. Use `LsmReadMode.PositionalRead` to force standard file reads.
- **Out-of-core columnar segments (v8):** Tables with a `USING COLUMNAR` (`[Columnar]`) index store 4,096-row columnar chunks, NULL/NaN masks, tombstone runs, and per-chunk min/max zone maps inside each `.sst` file.

## Durability Settings & `IoSchedulerMode`

| Setting | Default | Behavior | When to Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `LsmStrictFsync = true` | Yes | Forces `commit.wal` to stable storage before acknowledging writes; concurrent commits share fsyncs | Production data that must survive power loss or OS crash |
| `LsmStrictFsync = false` | No | Acknowledges after OS-buffered WAL append; recent writes can be lost on power/kernel failure | Caches, rebuildable data, and throughput ceiling benchmarks |
| `ClusteredPrimaryKeys` | `true` | Stores single `INT` or `GUID` PK tables directly under their key (no separate PK index) | Keep `true` for fast PK seeks and range scans (set at `CREATE TABLE`) |
| `IoSchedulerMode` | `Off` | Controls legacy `Disk` I/O scheduling (`Off`, `PoolingOnly`, or reserved `GroupCommit`) | Only relevant for legacy `StorageMode.Disk` (`Lsm` uses its own commit log) |

> When reporting or comparing write throughput, always pair the number with its durability setting—for example, `LSM Strict` vs. `LSM Relaxed`.

## Crash Atomicity and Visibility

In `StorageMode.Lsm`, every auto-commit statement and every explicit transaction `COMMIT` is written to `commit.wal` as a **single checksummed record**:

- **All-or-nothing recovery:** On startup after a crash, recovery replays each complete record atomically and ignores any truncated tail. Multi-row `UPDATE`s and multi-table transactions are never half-applied.
- **Durable visibility:** Row changes, secondary index updates, and reactive notifications become visible to other sessions only after the commit record is durable. Write locks are held until publish, and any failed statement writes no record and leaves no partial state.

## Reopening a Directory

Closing and reopening a `DataVoContext` on the same `DiskStoragePath` restores the catalog (`Catalog.xml`), SSTables, commit log, and transaction-ID watermark:

```csharp
var config = new DataVoConfig
{
    StorageMode = StorageMode.Lsm,
    DiskStoragePath = "./datavo_lsm_data"
};

using (var db = new DataVoContext(config))
{
    db.Execute("CREATE DATABASE App; USE App;");
    db.Execute("CREATE TABLE players (id INT PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR)");
    db.Execute("INSERT INTO players VALUES (1, 'Ada')");
}

using var reopened = new DataVoContext(config);
reopened.Execute("USE App");
var row = reopened.Execute("SELECT name FROM players WHERE id = 1")[0].Data[0]; // "Ada"
```

### Index Recovery on Open

| Index Type | Behavior on Reopen |
| --- | --- |
| **Clustered PK** (`INT`/`GUID`) | Stored directly as the SSTable row key; zero rebuild |
| **B-tree secondary indexes** | Stored as keyed SSTables under `.idx` and updated in the same commit record; zero rebuild |
| **`USING COLUMNAR`** | Stored inside `.sst` (v8 segments); only the unflushed tail stays in memory; zero rebuild |
| **`USING HNSW`** | Loads snapshot written on clean close and catches up from `commit.wal`; rebuilds if missing, corrupt, or >50% changed |
| **`USING FLAT`** | Rebuilt sequentially from table rows on open |

Like `Disk` mode, an LSM directory is owned by one process at a time via `datavo.lock`, while multiple contexts inside the same process share one engine (requiring identical settings). Note that prior to v1.0, the on-disk LSM format does not guarantee cross-version binary compatibility.

## See Also

- [Storage Modes](/manual/fundamentals/storage-modes) — Compare `InMemory`, `Lsm`, `Disk`, `Wasm`, and `Custom`
- [Transactions & MVCC](/manual/fundamentals/transactions-and-mvcc) — Snapshot isolation and atomic multi-statement commits
- [Configuration Reference](/manual/reference/configuration) — Full `DataVoConfig` reference

# Transactions & MVCC

> Source route: /manual/fundamentals/transactions-and-mvcc
> Source file: manual/fundamentals/transactions-and-mvcc.md

DataVo provides multi-version concurrency control (MVCC) with **snapshot isolation**. Readers see a consistent point-in-time view without blocking writers, while explicit transactions buffer writes and commit atomically with first-committer-wins conflict detection.

```csharp
using DataVo.Core;
using DataVo.Core.StorageEngine.Config;

using var db = new DataVoContext(new DataVoConfig
{
    StorageMode = StorageMode.Lsm,
    DiskStoragePath = "./datavo_lsm_data"
});

db.Execute("CREATE DATABASE App; USE App;");
db.Execute("CREATE TABLE players (id INT PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR, score INT)");

db.Execute("BEGIN TRANSACTION");
db.Execute("INSERT INTO players (id, name, score) VALUES (1, 'Ada', 100)");
db.Execute("UPDATE players SET score = 150 WHERE id = 1");
db.Execute("COMMIT");
```

> **`DataVoContext` uses SQL statements for transactions.** There is no `db.BeginTransaction()` method on `DataVoContext`—issue `BEGIN` / `COMMIT` / `ROLLBACK` via `db.Execute(...)`. If you need a `DbTransaction` object, use `DataVoConnection.BeginTransaction()` in [ADO.NET](/manual/client-interfaces/ado-net).

## Session-Bound Transactions & Savepoints

Transactions belong to a session. When running concurrent workflows against a shared `DataVoContext`, pass an explicit `Guid sessionId` to keep each transaction isolated:

```csharp
Guid sessionId = Guid.NewGuid();

db.Execute("BEGIN", sessionId);
db.Execute("INSERT INTO players (id, name, score) VALUES (2, 'Lin', 90)", sessionId);
db.Execute("SAVEPOINT before_bonus", sessionId);
db.Execute("UPDATE players SET score = 999 WHERE id = 2", sessionId);
db.Execute("ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT before_bonus", sessionId); // reverts bonus only
db.Execute("RELEASE SAVEPOINT before_bonus", sessionId);
db.Execute("COMMIT", sessionId);                             // commits score = 90
```

`ROLLBACK` discards all buffered changes for that session. `SAVEPOINT <name>`, `ROLLBACK TO [SAVEPOINT] <name>`, and `RELEASE [SAVEPOINT] <name>` rewind or discard nested buffered changes without aborting the outer transaction.

## MVCC Snapshot Isolation

When a transaction executes `BEGIN`, DataVo captures a **snapshot ordered by commit**, not by transaction start time:

- A transaction sees only commits that **finished** before its `BEGIN` (waiting up to `LockAcquireTimeoutMs` for any in-flight publish to complete).
- Auto-commit statements still running when `BEGIN` starts remain invisible even if they finish a moment later.
- Old row versions are retained automatically while any active snapshot needs them and reclaimed once no open snapshot can observe them.

<div class="sketch-diagram">
  <img class="light-only" src="/manual/fig-03-mvcc-snapshot-light.svg" alt="MVCC snapshot isolation showing Session B reading its BEGIN snapshot while Session A commits a newer version" />
  <img class="dark-only" src="/manual/fig-03-mvcc-snapshot-dark.svg" alt="MVCC snapshot isolation showing Session B reading its BEGIN snapshot while Session A commits a newer version" />
</div>

```sql
-- Session A                                -- Session B
BEGIN;                                      BEGIN;
UPDATE players SET score = 200 WHERE id = 1;
COMMIT;
                                            -- Still sees score = 150 (A committed after B began)
                                            SELECT score FROM players WHERE id = 1;
                                            COMMIT;
```

## Read-Your-Own-Writes

Every statement inside an open transaction (`SELECT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, joins, subqueries, index lookups, and compiled LINQ `ExecuteUpdate`) reads through the transaction's snapshot **plus its own uncommitted writes**:

```sql
BEGIN;
INSERT INTO players (id, name, score) VALUES (3, 'Grace', 50);
UPDATE players SET score = 120 WHERE name = 'Grace';  -- sees buffered insert
DELETE FROM players WHERE score = 120 AND id = 3;     -- removes buffered row
COMMIT;                                               -- net no-op for id = 3
```

Multiple updates to the same row coalesce into a single pending version, and key checks account for keys inserted or deleted earlier in the same transaction.

## Write Conflicts & Atomic Commit

DataVo enforces **first-committer-wins**:

- If two transactions modify the same row, the first to commit succeeds. The second fails with a conflict error—either during `UPDATE`/`DELETE` if the other commit already finished, or at `COMMIT`. A failed `COMMIT` ends the transaction; retry from `BEGIN`.
- At `COMMIT`, DataVo re-validates primary keys, `UNIQUE` constraints, and foreign keys against concurrent commits. Swapping key values between rows in the same transaction is supported because old rows are removed before new ones are written.
- On `Lsm`, the entire `COMMIT` is written as one atomic batch and discarded on failure. On `InMemory`, applied steps are journaled and undone on failure.

## Isolation Guarantees

| Anomaly | Prevented? | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dirty reads | Yes | Uncommitted writes are private to the session |
| Non-repeatable reads | Yes | Snapshot pinned at `BEGIN` |
| Lost updates | Yes | First-committer-wins detects concurrent row writes |
| Read skew | Yes | Multi-row reads observe one consistent commit watermark |
| Write skew | **No** | Snapshot isolation is not serializable; guard cross-row invariants by updating a shared row |

## ADO.NET Transactions

When using `DataVo.Data` (or Dapper), use standard `DataVoConnection.BeginTransaction()`:

```csharp
using DataVo.Data;

using var conn = new DataVoConnection("StorageMode=Lsm;DataSource=./datavo_lsm_data");
conn.Open();

using var tx = conn.BeginTransaction();
using var cmd = conn.CreateCommand();
cmd.Transaction = tx;
cmd.CommandText = "UPDATE players SET score = 300 WHERE id = 1";
cmd.ExecuteNonQuery();
tx.Commit();
```

## See Also

- [SQL Transaction Statements](/manual/sql/statements/transactions) — Exact syntax for `BEGIN`, `COMMIT`, `ROLLBACK`, and `SAVEPOINT`
- [LSM & Durability](/manual/fundamentals/lsm-and-durability) — Crash atomicity and strict fsync guarantees
- [ADO.NET Provider](/manual/client-interfaces/ado-net) — `DataVoConnection` and `DataVoTransaction` usage

# Vector Search

> Source route: /manual/fundamentals/vector-search
> Source file: manual/fundamentals/vector-search.md

DataVo stores dense float embeddings directly alongside relational columns in `VECTOR(n)` columns and queries them with `<=>` (Cosine) and `<->` (L2 / Euclidean) distance operators. Embeddings live in the same table, index lifecycle, and transaction log as your application metadata.

```csharp
using DataVo.Core;
using DataVo.Core.StorageEngine.Config;

using var db = new DataVoContext(new DataVoConfig { StorageMode = StorageMode.InMemory });
db.Execute("CREATE DATABASE Docs; USE Docs;");

db.Execute("""
CREATE TABLE documents (
    id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    title VARCHAR,
    category VARCHAR,
    embedding VECTOR(3)
);
""");

db.Execute("INSERT INTO documents VALUES (1, 'Intro', 'guide', '[1, 0, 0]')");
db.Execute("INSERT INTO documents VALUES (2, 'LSM',   'guide', '[0.9, 0.1, 0]')");
db.Execute("INSERT INTO documents VALUES (3, 'Sync',  'cloud', '[0, 1, 0]')");
db.Execute("CREATE INDEX idx_docs_emb ON documents (embedding) USING FLAT");

var top = db.Execute("""
SELECT id, title, embedding <=> '[1, 0, 0]' AS distance
FROM documents
ORDER BY distance ASC
LIMIT 2;
""")[0];
```

*(The snippet uses `VECTOR(3)` for readability; production schemas use `VECTOR(384)`, `VECTOR(1536)`, etc.)*

::: info DataVo Extension
`VECTOR(n)` (along with aliases `VEC2`, `VEC3`, `VEC4`, `FLOAT[n]`, and `REAL[n]`), the `<=>` and `<->` distance operators, and `USING HNSW` / `USING FLAT` index clauses are DataVo SQL extensions beyond standard ANSI SQL.
:::

## Distance Operators

DataVo ranks closer vectors by **smaller** distance values, so nearest-neighbor queries order ascending (`ORDER BY distance ASC`) with a `LIMIT`:

| Operator | Metric | Typical Use Case |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<=>` | Cosine distance | Text and semantic embeddings where vector direction matters more than magnitude |
| `<->` | L2 (Euclidean) distance | Geometric spaces where absolute coordinate distance matters |

## Choosing a Vector Index: `FLAT` vs `HNSW`

Create an index on the `VECTOR(n)` column to accelerate similarity search:

```sql
-- Exact SIMD scan (100% recall, ideal for tests and smaller tables)
CREATE INDEX idx_docs_flat ON documents (embedding) USING FLAT;

-- Approximate nearest-neighbor graph (fast on large tables)
CREATE INDEX idx_docs_hnsw ON documents (embedding)
USING HNSW WITH (
    metric = 'cosine',
    m = 24,
    ef_construction = 128,
    ef_search = 96,
    enable_diversity_heuristic = true
);
```

All `WITH (...)` options are optional and ignore case and underscores (`ef_construction` and `EfConstruction` are identical):

| Option | Default | Range | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `metric` | `cosine` | `cosine`, `euclidean` (`l2`) | Distance metric ranked by the index (also supported on `FLAT`) |
| `m` | `16` | `2..128` | Max neighbor links per graph layer (`2 * m` on layer 0) |
| `ef_construction` | `64` | `1..4096` | Candidate beam width during index build |
| `ef_search` | `64` | `1..4096` | Minimum candidate beam width at query time |
| `enable_diversity_heuristic` | `true` | `true`, `false` | Preserves inter-cluster links; keep `true` for clustered text embeddings |

Options are persisted in the catalog and reused if the graph is rebuilt after a crash or reopen. Passing an unknown option, an out-of-range value, or an HNSW option on a `FLAT`/B-tree index raises an error.

## Filtered & Joined Vector Search

Combine vector ranking with `WHERE` predicates, distance thresholds, or `JOIN`s:

```sql
SELECT id, title, embedding <=> '[1, 0, 0]' AS distance
FROM documents
WHERE category = 'guide' AND embedding <=> '[1, 0, 0]' < 0.25
ORDER BY distance ASC
LIMIT 10;
```

DataVo guarantees the requested `LIMIT` whenever enough matching rows exist:

1. **Adaptive candidate expansion:** DataVo requests `~LIMIT / selectivity` candidates from the vector index, tests scalar or joined filters on stored rows, and expands the candidate count if too few rows pass.
2. **Exact-scan cost routing:** When a selective filter widens the HNSW beam past the break-even point (~9% of vectors at 384D, ~20% at 1,536D), HNSW automatically switches to an exact SIMD scan—improving both latency and recall. (Set `HNSWIndex.EnableExactScanCostRouting = false` in C# to disable.)
3. **Exact table-scan fallback:** If expansion still finds fewer than `LIMIT` passing rows, DataVo filters the table first and ranks only the surviving rows against the index's stored vectors.

## C# Direct Vector Search (`SearchNearest`)

When you already have a `float[]`, `ReadOnlySpan<float>`, or vector string in C# and want to query a named index without building SQL text, call `db.SearchNearest(...)`:

```csharp
ReadOnlySpan<float> query = [1f, 0f, 0f];
List<Dictionary<string, object?>> hits = db.SearchNearest(
    tableName: "documents",
    indexName: "idx_docs_flat",
    queryVector: query,
    topK: 5);
```

::: details API Reference
```csharp
public List<Dictionary<string, object?>> SearchNearest(
    string tableName, string indexName, float[] queryVector, int topK = 10);

public List<Dictionary<string, object?>> SearchNearest(
    string tableName, string indexName, ReadOnlySpan<float> queryVector, int topK = 10);

public List<Dictionary<string, object?>> SearchNearest(
    string tableName, string indexName, string queryVector, int topK = 10);
```
:::

## See Also

- [SQL Indexes (`CREATE INDEX`)](/manual/sql/statements/indexes) — Full DDL syntax for `BTREE`, `HNSW`, `FLAT`, and `COLUMNAR` indexes
- [SQL Data Types](/manual/sql/data-types) — `VECTOR(n)` column declarations and literal syntax
- [LSM & Durability](/manual/fundamentals/lsm-and-durability) — How HNSW snapshots and FLAT indexes recover on reopen

# Streaming Queries

> Source route: /manual/fundamentals/streaming-queries
> Source file: manual/fundamentals/streaming-queries.md

By default, `db.Execute("SELECT ...")` buffers the entire result set into `List<Dictionary<string, object?>>` before returning. When scanning large tables or stopping early on a match, use DataVo's pull-based streaming APIs to process rows incrementally in 1,024-row pages—or with zero heap allocations.

```csharp
using DataVo.Core;
using DataVo.Core.StorageEngine.Config;

using var db = new DataVoContext(new DataVoConfig { StorageMode = StorageMode.InMemory });
db.Execute("CREATE DATABASE Game; USE Game;");
db.Execute("CREATE TABLE players (id INT PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR, score INT)");

// Lazily fetches 1,024-row pages; stops scanning storage immediately on break
foreach (DataVoRow row in db.StreamQuery(
    "SELECT id, name, score FROM players WHERE score >= @min",
    ("min", 900)))
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{row["name"]}: {row["score"]}");
    if ((int)row["id"]! == targetId)
        break; // triggers yield break — remaining pages are never read
}
```

## Comparing Execution Modes

<div class="sketch-diagram">
  <img class="light-only" src="/manual/fig-07-streaming-modes-light.svg" alt="Comparison of Execute buffered results, StreamQuery 1024-row yield pages, and zero-allocation StreamRef RowRef spans" />
  <img class="dark-only" src="/manual/fig-07-streaming-modes-dark.svg" alt="Comparison of Execute buffered results, StreamQuery 1024-row yield pages, and zero-allocation StreamRef RowRef spans" />
</div>

| API | Element Type | Memory & Allocation | Best For |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `db.Execute(sql)` | `List<Dictionary<string, object?>>` | Buffers full result set | Small results, DDL/DML, scripts |
| `db.StreamQuery(sql, ...)` | `IEnumerable<DataVoRow>` | 1,024-row pages (`yield return`); owns cell array per row | Large SQL scans, `.Take(n)`, early `break` |
| `db.Table<T>().Where(...)` | `IEnumerable<T>` | 1,024-row pages (`yield return`); one POCO per row | Native AOT compiled domain queries without `.ToList()` |
| `db.StreamRef("T")` / `table.StreamRef()` | `RowRef` (`readonly ref struct`) | **0 B** per row after warmup | 60/120 FPS simulation loops and GC-free aggregators |

## Paged SQL Streaming (`db.StreamQuery`)

For eligible single-table `SELECT` queries, `StreamQuery` fetches 1,024-row pages lazily and yields each `DataVoRow`:

- **Early exit & `LIMIT`:** With `LIMIT k [OFFSET n]`, each batch caps its fetch size to `Math.Min(1024, remaining + skip)` and exits via `yield break` once `k` rows are emitted.
- **Owned rows:** Each `DataVoRow` owns its decoded values (`row["Column"]` or `row[ordinal]`), so you can safely store rows beyond the loop iteration.
- **Per-page locking:** During pure paged streaming, DataVo acquires and releases the read scope **per 1,024-row page**, so a slow consumer never stalls concurrent writers.

`StreamQuery` automatically falls back to materializing first—and still streams the resulting rows lazily—when a query uses `JOIN`, `GROUP BY`, `HAVING`, `ORDER BY`, `DISTINCT`, CTEs, `RANK()`, indexed equality probes, or runs inside an explicit `BEGIN` transaction (which needs a single snapshot).

## Compiled `DataVoTable<T>` Streaming

Enumerating a source-generated `[DataVoTable]` query without calling `.ToList()` streams 1,024-row pages of strongly-typed entities:

```csharp
foreach (Player p in db.Table<Player>().Where(100, static (p, min) => p.Score >= min))
{
    ProcessPlayer(p);
}

foreach (Player nearby in db.Table<Player>().WithinRadius(origin, radius: 25f))
{
    RenderNearby(nearby);
}
```

Only call `.ToList()` when you intentionally need every matching object buffered at once.

## Zero-Allocation Scans (`StreamRef`)

::: info DataVo Extension
`StreamRef` (`RowRefStream` yielding stack-only `RowRef` spans) is a DataVo .NET-native extension designed for zero-GC hot loops.
:::

When allocating even one `DataVoRow` or POCO per row is too expensive, stream raw page views with `StreamRef`:

```csharp
RowRefStream stream = db.Table<Player>().StreamRef();
int scoreCol = stream.GetOrdinal("Score");

long total = 0;
foreach (RowRef row in stream)
{
    if (!row.IsNull(scoreCol))
        total += row.GetInt32(scoreCol);
}
```

`RowRef` is a `readonly ref struct` backed by a reusable page buffer, allocating **0 bytes** on the managed heap after warmup. Because the buffer is overwritten on the next page, `RowRef` cannot be stored past its loop iteration or captured across `await`.

::: details API Reference
```csharp
// DataVoContext
public IEnumerable<DataVoRow> StreamQuery(string query, params DataVoQueryParameter[] parameters);
public IEnumerable<DataVoRow> StreamQuery(string query, Guid sessionId);
public RowRefStream StreamRef(string tableName);

// DataVoTable<T>
public RowRefStream StreamRef();
```
:::

## See Also

- [Zero-Allocation Row Model](/manual/internals/zero-allocation-rows) — Memory layout and typed accessors of `RowRef`
- [Live Reactive Views](/manual/fundamentals/reactive-views) — Receive incremental deltas instead of rescanning tables
- [Roslyn Source Generators](/manual/client-interfaces/source-generators) — Compile-time predicates on `DataVoTable<T>`

# Live Reactive Views

> Source route: /manual/fundamentals/reactive-views
> Source file: manual/fundamentals/reactive-views.md

Live Reactive Views let you register a standing SQL or compiled LINQ query and receive exact **incremental deltas** (`Added`, `Removed`, `Updated`) whenever underlying tables change—without polling or rescanning. Powered by **Z-set Incremental View Maintenance (IVM)** inspired by DBSP, every committed write emits signed tuple weights (`+1` insert, `-1` delete, `(-1, +1)` update) that update only affected keys or groups.

```csharp
using DataVo.Core;
using DataVo.Core.StorageEngine.Config;

using var db = new DataVoContext(new DataVoConfig { StorageMode = StorageMode.InMemory });
db.Execute("CREATE DATABASE Game; USE Game;");
db.Execute("CREATE TABLE players (id INT PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR, region VARCHAR, score INT)");

using IDisposable sub = db.Subscribe(
    "SELECT region, COUNT(*) AS players, SUM(score) AS total FROM players GROUP BY region",
    change =>
    {
        foreach (var row in change.Added)
            Console.WriteLine($"+ {row["region"]}: total={row["total"]}");
        foreach (var row in change.Updated)
            Console.WriteLine($"~ {row["region"]}: total={row["total"]}");
    });

db.Execute("INSERT INTO players VALUES (1, 'Ada', 'EU', 120), (2, 'Lin', 'EU', 80)");
db.DispatchPendingNotifications(); // invokes callback on the calling thread
```

::: info DataVo Extension
Live Reactive Views (`Subscribe`, `SubscribeZeroAlloc`, `SubscribeInto`, and `DispatchPendingNotifications`) are a DataVo .NET-native IVM extension. Subscriptions return `IDisposable` directly—there is no separate `LiveView` wrapper class.
:::

## Choosing a Subscription API

| API | Input | Payload | Steady-State Allocation | Best For |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `db.Subscribe(sql, cb)` | Raw SQL | `QueryChange` (dictionaries) | Per-delta lists & dicts | Ad-hoc SQL (`JOIN`, `GROUP BY`, `UNION`, subqueries, `WITH RECURSIVE`) |
| `db.Subscribe(prepared, cb, params)` | `DataVoPreparedStatement` | `QueryChange` or `QueryChangeRef` | Skips SQL parsing | Multi-tenant / per-room subscriptions sharing one template |
| `db.SubscribeZeroAlloc(sql, cb)` | Raw SQL / prepared | `in QueryChangeRef` (`RowRef` spans) | Zero row/dict boxing | High-frequency SQL aggregates, Top-K, joins, recursive CTEs |
| `query.Subscribe(cb)` | Compiled `DataVoTable<T>` LINQ | `QueryChange<T>` | Typed models (AOT-safe) | Strongly-typed app services and UI state without SQL strings |
| `query.SubscribeInto(dest, onUpdated)` | Compiled LINQ + `Memory<T>` | Writes `dest.Span[0..count]` in place | **0 bytes** on dispatch | Real-time game HUDs, leaderboards, and frame-tick render loops |

## Pull-Drain Delivery Model

Notifications are **pulled**, never pushed from background threads or timers:

1. Committed writes append row deltas to an internal buffer (zero overhead when no subscriptions are active).
2. Nothing fires until your application calls `db.DispatchPendingNotifications()`.
3. `DispatchPendingNotifications()` evaluates net deltas for affected views and invokes callbacks **on the calling thread**, skipping empty deltas.

<div class="sketch-diagram">
  <img class="light-only" src="/manual/fig-04-zset-ivm-pull-light.svg" alt="Pull-drain Z-set IVM pipeline from committed writes to change buffer to DispatchPendingNotifications on the caller thread" />
  <img class="dark-only" src="/manual/fig-04-zset-ivm-pull-dark.svg" alt="Pull-drain Z-set IVM pipeline from committed writes to change buffer to DispatchPendingNotifications on the caller thread" />
</div>

Key operational guarantees:
- **Transaction-safe:** Rolled-back transactions emit zero notifications.
- **Reentrancy-deferred:** Writes issued inside a callback are buffered for the *next* `DispatchPendingNotifications()` call.
- **No baseline redelivery:** Subscribing seeds internal state from existing rows silently; only subsequent commits trigger callbacks.

## Zero-Allocation Buffered Windows (`SubscribeInto`)

For 60/120 FPS HUDs and leaderboards, project directly into a caller-owned `Memory<HudSlot>` with **0 bytes allocated** per dispatch:

```csharp
public struct HudSlot
{
    public int Id;
    public int Score;
}

var hudSlots = new HudSlot[3];
int liveCount = 0;

using IDisposable hudSub = db.Table<Player>()
    .Where(100, static (p, min) => p.Score >= min)
    .OrderByDescending(static p => p.Score)
    .Take(3)
    .Select(static p => new HudSlot { Id = p.Id, Score = p.Score })
    .SubscribeInto(hudSlots.AsMemory(), count => liveCount = count);

db.Insert(new Player { Id = 1, Score = 150 });
db.Insert(new Player { Id = 2, Score = 320 });
db.DispatchPendingNotifications(); // 0 B allocated; hudSlots[0..liveCount] updated in place
```

## Enter / Leave / Stay Semantics

| Mutation | Before Matches | After Matches | Emitted Delta |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `INSERT` | — | Yes | `Added` |
| `DELETE` | Yes | — | `Removed` |
| `UPDATE` | Yes | No | `Removed` |
| `UPDATE` | No | Yes | `Added` |
| `UPDATE` | Yes | Yes | `Updated` (paired with `UpdatedBefore`) |

## Supported IVM Operators

Unsupported query shapes fail fast during `Subscribe` / `SubscribeZeroAlloc` with `NotSupportedException` and zero side effects.

| Query Shape | `Subscribe` | `SubscribeZeroAlloc` | Requirements / Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Aggregates** (`GROUP BY`, `COUNT`/`SUM`/`AVG`/`MIN`/`MAX`) | Yes | Yes | Single table; O(1) for `COUNT`/`SUM`/`AVG`; no `HAVING` or CTEs |
| **Top-K** (`ORDER BY ... LIMIT k [OFFSET n]`) | Yes | Yes | Single table with a **primary key** |
| **Two-table equi-join** (`INNER`/`LEFT`/`RIGHT`/`FULL`) | Yes | Yes | Keyed DBSP arrangements; optional post-join `WHERE` |
| **Three-table VIP exposure** (`Orders × Accounts × Markets` + `GROUP BY`) | Yes | Yes | Specialized incremental 3-table exposure pipeline |
| **Recursive CTE** (`WITH RECURSIVE ... UNION ALL`) | Yes | Yes | Linear reachability over a table with a **primary key** |
| **Linear filter** (`SELECT ... [WHERE ...]`) | Yes | No | Single table; `=`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`, `LIKE`, `IS [NOT] NULL`, `AND`/`OR` |
| **`SELECT DISTINCT`** | Yes | No | Single-table distinct multiplicity map |
| **`UNION` / `UNION ALL`** | Yes | No | Two single-table branches; no branch joins/aggregates or final `ORDER BY`/`LIMIT` |
| **Subqueries** (`IN`, `NOT IN`, `EXISTS`, `NOT EXISTS`) | Yes | No | Uncorrelated or single-key equality correlation; outer table needs a **primary key** |

Window functions (`RANK() OVER`), `HAVING`, arbitrary 3+ table joins, self-joins, and correlated scalar-aggregate subqueries are not supported in reactive views.

::: details API Reference
```csharp
// DataVoContext SQL & Prepared Subscriptions
IDisposable Subscribe(string sql, Action<QueryChange> onChanged);
IDisposable Subscribe(DataVoPreparedStatement statement, Action<QueryChange> onChanged);
IDisposable Subscribe(DataVoPreparedStatement statement, Action<QueryChange> onChanged, params DataVoQueryParameter[] parameters);
IDisposable Subscribe(DataVoPreparedStatement statement, Action<QueryChange> onChanged, ReadOnlySpan<DataVoQueryParameter> parameters);
IDisposable Subscribe(DataVoPreparedStatement statement, Action<QueryChange> onChanged, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, object?> parameters);

IDisposable SubscribeZeroAlloc(string sql, QueryDeltaHandler onChanged);
IDisposable SubscribeZeroAlloc(DataVoPreparedStatement statement, QueryDeltaHandler onChanged);
IDisposable SubscribeZeroAlloc(DataVoPreparedStatement statement, QueryDeltaHandler onChanged, params DataVoQueryParameter[] parameters);
IDisposable SubscribeZeroAlloc(DataVoPreparedStatement statement, QueryDeltaHandler onChanged, ReadOnlySpan<DataVoQueryParameter> parameters);
IDisposable SubscribeZeroAlloc(DataVoPreparedStatement statement, QueryDeltaHandler onChanged, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, object?> parameters);

void DispatchPendingNotifications();
void SetMaxReactiveSubscriptions(int max);

// DataVoTable<T> & Composed LINQ Queries
IDisposable Subscribe(Action<QueryChange<T>> onChanged);
IDisposable SubscribeInto(Memory<TProjection> destination, Action<int> onUpdated);
```

`QueryChange` and `QueryChange<T>` expose `Added`, `Removed`, `Updated`, `UpdatedBefore`, and `IsEmpty`. `QueryChangeRef` (`readonly ref struct` passed to `QueryDeltaHandler`) exposes `Schema`, `RowSet` properties (`Added`, `Removed`, `Updated`, `UpdatedBefore`), `IsEmpty`, and `Materialize()`.
:::

# DataVo Sync

> Source route: /manual/fundamentals/datavo-sync
> Source file: manual/fundamentals/datavo-sync.md

**DataVo Sync** is a separate, proprietary **commercial add-on** for teams that need offline-first, bidirectional synchronization between embedded DataVo databases and a central **PostgreSQL** server.

> **Not included in `DataVo.Core`:** The open-source MIT-licensed `DataVo.Core` NuGet package and repository contain the standalone embedded database engine only. DataVo Sync is licensed and distributed separately.

## How It Works

DataVo Sync connects PostgreSQL logical replication (`pgoutput`) to embedded DataVo clients over WebSocket and HTTP, keeping local reads microsecond-fast while synchronizing mutations automatically when online:

- **Wire v2 + Brotli framing:** Compact binary delta frames averaging **45.5 B/row** over the wire.
- **Z-set delta compaction:** Coalesces redundant intermediate mutations before transmission so offline bursts converge cleanly.
- **Per-column conflict resolution:** Resolves concurrent offline edits at column granularity rather than overwriting whole rows.
- **Crash-recoverable write-back:** Local offline writes are persisted and replayed safely to PostgreSQL upon reconnection.

## Verified Benchmark Highlights

Measured in end-to-end Linux x64 CI benchmarks (20 November 2026, PostgreSQL 17.12, 2 vCPU VM):

| Metric | DataVo Sync | Comparison Baseline |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **100k warm initial sync** | **605 ms** (`InMemory`) · **706–726 ms** (`Lsm`) | 702–909 ms (SQLite/JSON) · 1,167 ms (ElectricSQL `1.8.1`) |
| **Wire footprint** | **45.5 B/row** (wire v2 + Brotli) | 362.7 B/row ElectricSQL (**8.0× smaller**) |
| **Client allocations (100k sync)** | **36.4–49.1 MB** | 251.4 MB ElectricSQL (**5.1–6.9× lower**) |
| **Concurrent scaling** | **1,000 WebSocket clients** (`12,754 rows/s`) | Single 2-vCPU VM |
| **Local read & convergence** | **4.06–5.19 µs** point lookups · **81–243 ms** offline-burst convergence | Across PostgreSQL and peers |

## When to Use DataVo Sync

- **Local-first .NET desktop, mobile, or edge apps** that must stay fully responsive offline and sync with an existing PostgreSQL backend.
- **Multi-client collaborative tools** that combine local SQL/LINQ queries and [Live Reactive Views](/manual/fundamentals/reactive-views) with shared server state.
- **High-density client fleets** where wire bandwidth, client GC overhead, and initial hydration time directly affect hosting cost.

## Licensing & Early Access

For commercial licensing, evaluation builds, or architecture inquiries, reach out to `@ArintonAkos` on GitHub.

## See Also

- [LSM & Durability](/manual/fundamentals/lsm-and-durability) — Local crash-safe persistence used by offline DataVo clients
- [Live Reactive Views](/manual/fundamentals/reactive-views) — Real-time UI updates driven by local and synced changes
- [Benchmarks](/manual/performance/benchmarks) — Embedded engine performance benchmarks

# DataVoContext API

> Source route: /manual/client-interfaces/datavo-context-api
> Source file: manual/client-interfaces/datavo-context-api.md

`DataVoContext` is DataVo's primary embedded C# entry point. It owns the in-process storage engine, default session, and configuration with no server, socket, or connection pool to manage.

```csharp
using DataVo.Core;
using DataVo.Core.Contracts.Results;
using DataVo.Core.StorageEngine.Config;

using var db = new DataVoContext(new DataVoConfig
{
    StorageMode = StorageMode.InMemory
});

db.Execute("CREATE DATABASE game; USE game;");
db.Execute("CREATE TABLE players (id INT PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(80), score INT)");
db.Execute("INSERT INTO players (id, name, score) VALUES (1, 'Ada', 1200)");

QueryResult result = db.Execute("SELECT id, name, score FROM players WHERE id = 1")[0];
Console.WriteLine($"{result.Data[0]["name"]}: {result.Data[0]["score"]}");
```

## Executing SQL & Sessions

`Execute(string sql)` accepts one or more semicolon-separated SQL statements and returns a `List<QueryResult>`. Each `QueryResult` exposes `Fields`, `Data` (row dictionaries), `Messages`, `IsError`, and `ErrorCode`.

Transactions and `USE <database>` bindings are scoped to a session. Pass an explicit `Guid sessionId` to `Execute` when you need independent transaction scopes on the same context:

```csharp
Guid workerSession = Guid.NewGuid();
db.Execute("USE game", workerSession);
db.Execute("BEGIN TRANSACTION", workerSession);
db.Execute("UPDATE players SET score = 1500 WHERE id = 1", workerSession);
db.Execute("COMMIT", workerSession);
```

`DataVoContext` has no `BeginTransaction()` C# method; manage transactions with SQL (`BEGIN`, `COMMIT`, `ROLLBACK`, `SAVEPOINT`). See [Transactions & MVCC](/manual/fundamentals/transactions-and-mvcc).

## Prepared Statements

Use `db.Prepare(sql)` to parse and plan a parameterized SQL statement once and execute it repeatedly. Placeholders support `@param`, `$param`, and `:param` prefixes.

```csharp
DataVoPreparedStatement findPlayer = db.Prepare(
    "SELECT id, name, score FROM players WHERE score >= @min");

QueryResult rows = findPlayer.Execute(new DataVoQueryParameter("min", 1000));
```

For hot loops that read results immediately without retaining `QueryResult` across calls, `ExecuteBorrowed(...)` reuses pooled internal result buffers to reduce allocations.

## Typed, Bulk, and Atomic Batch Writes

When ingesting many rows or writing from strongly-typed models, bypass SQL parsing with direct write methods:

| Method | Best For | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Insert<T>(table, entity)` | Single POCO insert | Maps public properties to catalog columns (cached per schema version). |
| `BulkInsert(table, rows)` | Dictionary batches | All-or-nothing insert of `IEnumerable<IReadOnlyDictionary<string, object?>>`. |
| `InsertTyped` / `InsertTypedBatch` | Zero-boxing pipelines | Accepts `ReactiveRowSchema` and `ReadOnlySpan<CellValue>`. |
| `ApplyBatch(DataVoWriteBatch)` | Multi-table atomic mutations | Combines `Upsert`, `Update`, and `Delete` in one commit (`InMemory` and `Lsm` only). |

```csharp
var batch = new DataVoWriteBatch();
batch.Upsert(playersLayout, 1, "Ada", 1500);
batch.Delete(playersLayout, 2, null, null);
DataVoBatchResult stats = db.ApplyBatch(batch);
```

## Snapshots, Auth & Change Capture

- **Snapshots:** Capture and restore point-in-time engine state for the current session with `DataVoSnapshot snap = db.CreateSnapshot()` and `db.RestoreSnapshot(snap)` — useful for deterministic test resets or branching simulation state.
- **Session Auth:** When `EnableAuthorization = true`, switch the active principal per session with `db.Login(username, password)` and `db.Logout()`. See [Admin & Security SQL](/manual/sql/statements/admin-and-security).
- **Change Capture:** `db.Changes` exposes the engine's `ChangeCapture` stream, which feeds reactive subscriptions and custom CDC consumers.

For lazy streaming (`StreamQuery`), zero-allocation scanning (`StreamRef`), and live reactive views (`Subscribe`, `SubscribeZeroAlloc`), see [Streaming Queries](/manual/fundamentals/streaming-queries) and [Reactive Views](/manual/fundamentals/reactive-views).

::: details API Reference

```csharp
// SQL & Prepared Statements
public List<QueryResult> Execute(string query);
public List<QueryResult> Execute(string query, Guid sessionId);
public DataVoPreparedStatement Prepare(string sql);
public DataVoPreparedStatement Prepare(string sql, Guid sessionId);

// Prepared Statement Execution (DataVoPreparedStatement)
public QueryResult Execute(params DataVoQueryParameter[] parameters);
public QueryResult Execute(ReadOnlySpan<DataVoQueryParameter> parameters, Guid sessionId);
public QueryResult ExecuteBorrowed(params DataVoQueryParameter[] parameters);
public QueryResult ExecuteBorrowed(ReadOnlySpan<DataVoQueryParameter> parameters, Guid sessionId);

// Typed & Batch Writes
public RowKey Insert<T>(string tableName, T entity);
public IReadOnlyList<RowKey> BulkInsert(string tableName, IEnumerable<IReadOnlyDictionary<string, object?>> rows);
public RowKey InsertTyped(string tableName, ReactiveRowSchema columns, ReadOnlySpan<CellValue> row);
public IReadOnlyList<RowKey> InsertTypedBatch(string tableName, ReactiveRowSchema columns, IReadOnlyList<CellValue[]> rows);
public DataVoBatchResult ApplyBatch(DataVoWriteBatch batch);
public DataVoBatchResult ApplyBatch(DataVoWriteBatch batch, Guid sessionId);

// Snapshots, Auth & CDC
public DataVoSnapshot CreateSnapshot();
public void RestoreSnapshot(DataVoSnapshot snapshot);
public bool Login(string username, string password);
public bool Login(string username, string password, Guid sessionId);
public void Logout();
public void Logout(Guid sessionId);
public ChangeCapture Changes { get; }
```

:::

# Roslyn Source Generators

> Source route: /manual/client-interfaces/source-generators
> Source file: manual/client-interfaces/source-generators.md

`DataVo.Generators` generates table helpers, strongly-typed row mappers, and pre-compiled SQL methods at build time. Because all code is emitted by Roslyn and depends only on `DataVo.Core`, it eliminates runtime reflection and is 100% compatible with Native AOT.

```csharp
using System.Numerics;
using DataVo.Core;
using DataVo.Core.Annotations;
using DataVo.Core.StorageEngine.Config;

[DataVoTable("players")]
public sealed class Player
{
    [PrimaryKey] public int Id { get; set; }
    public string Name { get; set; } = "";
    [Indexed] public int Score { get; set; }
    [Columnar] public string Region { get; set; } = "";
    [SpatialIndex] public Vector3 Position { get; set; }
}

using var db = new DataVoContext(new DataVoConfig { StorageMode = StorageMode.InMemory });
db.Execute("CREATE DATABASE game; USE game;");

db.EnsurePlayerTable();
db.Insert(new Player { Id = 1, Name = "Ada", Score = 1200, Region = "EU", Position = new(10, 0, 5) });
Player? ada = db.GetPlayerById(1);
```

## Table Annotations & Generated Helpers

Annotating a model with `[DataVoTable("table_name")]` generates zero-reflection extension methods on `DataVoContext`:

| Attribute | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `[DataVoTable("players")]` | Binds the class to a table and generates `EnsurePlayerTable()`, `GetPlayerById(key)`, `Insert(player)`, and `Update(player)`. |
| `[PrimaryKey]` | Marks the primary key column used by `Get<Model>ById` and `Update`. |
| `[Indexed]` | Causes `Ensure<Model>Table()` to create a secondary B-Tree index (or HNSW index on `Vector3`). |
| `[Columnar]` | Adds the column to the table's columnar index (`cx_<table>`) for fast analytical aggregations (`int`, `long`, `float`, `double`, `bool`, and date columns). |
| `[SpatialIndex]` | Creates a Euclidean HNSW index (`sx_<table>_<column>`) on a `System.Numerics.Vector3` property for 3D spatial queries. |

Calling `db.EnsurePlayerTable()` creates the table and all annotated indexes if they do not exist. On compilers without module initializers (such as Unity), call `Ensure<Model>Table()` before accessing `db.Table<Player>()`.

## Compile-Time SQL with `[DataVoQuery]`

For fixed-shape SQL statements called on hot paths, annotate a `static partial` method with `[DataVoQuery]`. The generator validates parameter names at compile time and emits direct execution and projection mapping code.

```csharp
using DataVo.Core;
using DataVo.Core.CompiledQueries;

public sealed record PlayerSummary(int Id, string Name, int Score);

public static partial class PlayerQueries
{
    [DataVoQuery("SELECT id, name, score FROM players WHERE id = @id")]
    public static partial PlayerSummary? GetSummary(DataVoContext db, int id);

    [DataVoQuery("INSERT INTO players (id, name, score) VALUES (@id, @name, @score)")]
    public static partial IReadOnlyList<long> InsertPlayer(DataVoContext db, int id, string name, int score);

    [DataVoQuery("UPDATE players SET score = @score WHERE id = @id")]
    public static partial int UpdateScore(DataVoContext db, int id, int score);
}
```

Rules for `[DataVoQuery]` methods:
- The first parameter must be `DataVoContext`.
- Every SQL placeholder (`@id`, `@score`) must match a subsequent C# parameter name.
- Use `[DataVoQuery]` for stable point lookups, inserts, and narrow updates; use runtime SQL for dynamic queries, joins, or vector search.

### SQL `DATE` Projections

Generated models map SQL `DATE` columns to `DataVo.Core.DataVoDate` (and `DataVoDate?`) across all target frameworks. On modern .NET (`net10.0`), `System.DateOnly` and `System.DateOnly?` are also supported as explicit adapters.

## Schema Manifest Validation

To let the generator validate column names and pre-resolve single-column index hints at build time, include your DDL file as an `AdditionalFiles` entry with `DataVoSchemaManifest="true"`:

```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <AdditionalFiles Include="datavo.schema.sql" DataVoSchemaManifest="true" />
</ItemGroup>
```

```sql
CREATE TABLE players (
    id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(80),
    score INT
);

CREATE INDEX ix_players_score ON players (score);
```

# Compiled LINQ & Spatial Queries

> Source route: /manual/client-interfaces/compiled-linq
> Source file: manual/client-interfaces/compiled-linq.md

`DataVoTable<T>` lets you query `[DataVoTable]` models with C# lambdas that Roslyn compiles into prepared queries and zero-allocation storage scans at build time. No expression trees are constructed and no reflection runs at runtime, making compiled LINQ safe for Native AOT and 60/120 FPS game loops.

```csharp
using DataVo.Core;
using DataVo.Core.StorageEngine.Config;

using var db = new DataVoContext(new DataVoConfig { StorageMode = StorageMode.InMemory });
db.Execute("CREATE DATABASE game; USE game;");
db.EnsurePlayerTable();

DataVoTable<Player> players = db.Table<Player>();

// Pass values as state with a static lambda: zero closure allocation
Player? top = players.FirstOrDefault(1, static (p, id) => p.Id == id);
List<Player> leaderboard = players
    .Where(500, static (p, min) => p.Score >= min)
    .OrderByDescending(static p => p.Score)
    .Take(10)
    .ToList();
```

::: info DataVo Extension
Compile-time LINQ interceptors, in-storage zero-allocation aggregates, and 3D spatial index queries (`WithinRadius`, `WithinBoundingBox`, `NearestNeighbors`) are `.NET`-native DataVo extensions powered by `DataVo.Generators`.
:::

## Enabling Interceptors

Installing the `DataVo.Generators` NuGet package enables C# 12 interceptors automatically. If you reference the generator via a project reference, add the generated namespace to your `.csproj`:

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <InterceptorsNamespaces>$(InterceptorsNamespaces);DataVo.Generated</InterceptorsNamespaces>
</PropertyGroup>
```

On compilers without interceptors (such as Unity), the same code compiles and returns identical results via fallback scans; use generated `Get<Model>ById` methods or prepared statements on hot paths.

## Supported LINQ Operators

| Operator | Compiled Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `Where` | Translates `==`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`, `&&`, `\|\|`, boolean flags, and `null` checks. Uses PK/B-Tree indexes when available; streams in 1,024-row pages otherwise. |
| `FirstOrDefault`, `SingleOrDefault` | PK equality on `Lsm` reads a single row (0 B on miss). |
| `Count`, `Any`, `Sum`, `Min`, `Max` | Compiles directly into the storage scan (or `[Columnar]` index) for numeric/bool/date/Guid columns — **0 B allocated** once warm. |
| `OrderBy`, `OrderByDescending`, `ThenBy`, `ThenByDescending` | Emits `ORDER BY`; combined with `Take`, retains only top-K rows during the scan. |
| `Skip`, `Take` | Emits `OFFSET @offset LIMIT @limit` following `Enumerable` clamping semantics. |
| `Select` | Projects only the referenced columns (`SELECT name, score ...`) without instantiating full models. |
| `ExecuteDelete`, `ExecuteUpdate` | Emits single atomic `DELETE` or `UPDATE` statements (`Set`, `SetNull`, and `+`, `-`, `*` column arithmetic). |

### Zero-Allocation Aggregates & Bulk Updates

```csharp
// 0 B allocated on warm InMemory and Lsm tables (accelerated further if Score is [Columnar])
int elites = players.Where(1000, static (p, min) => p.Score >= min).Count();
long totalScore = players.Where(1000, static (p, min) => p.Score >= min).Sum(static p => p.Score);

// Atomic server-side bulk update
int boosted = players
    .Where(500, static (p, min) => p.Score >= min)
    .ExecuteUpdate(100, static (set, bonus) => set.Set(p => p.Score, p => p.Score + bonus));
```

### Build Diagnostics

Queries that cannot be compiled still return accurate results via an in-memory fallback (except `ExecuteUpdate`, which has no fallback) and emit a build diagnostic:

| Code | Severity | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DATAVOL001` | Warning | Lambda captures a local or instance member; pass it as state with a `static` lambda. |
| `DATAVOL002` | Warning | Predicate uses an unsupported construct (method call, arithmetic, or cross-column comparison). |
| `DATAVOL003` | Warning | `InterceptorsNamespaces` does not include `DataVo.Generated`. |
| `DATAVOL004` | Warning | `OrderBy`/`ThenBy` key or `Select` projection falls back to in-memory execution. |
| `DATAVOL005` | Error | `ExecuteUpdate` cannot be compiled (captured variable, PK assignment, or unsupported expression). |

## 3D Spatial Queries

Any `System.Numerics.Vector3` property on a `[DataVoTable]` model is stored as `VECTOR(3)` and can be queried spatially:

```csharp
using System.Numerics;

var origin = new Vector3(0f, 0f, 0f);

// Stream players inside a 50-unit sphere (surface inclusive)
foreach (Player p in players.WithinRadius(origin, radius: 50f)) { }

// Stream players inside an axis-aligned bounding box
List<Player> inZone = players.WithinBoundingBox(new(-10, -10, -10), new(10, 10, 10)).ToList();

// 5 closest players (uses [SpatialIndex] Euclidean HNSW; pass exact: true for exact scan)
IReadOnlyList<Player> nearest = players.NearestNeighbors(origin, k: 5);
```

- `WithinRadius` and `WithinBoundingBox` test stored coordinates in double precision before allocating models, so non-matching rows allocate nothing.
- `NearestNeighbors` uses the `[SpatialIndex]` Euclidean HNSW index (`sx_<table>_<column>`) when present, or falls back to an exact streaming scan when `exact: true`, unindexed, or inside a transaction.
- When a model has multiple `Vector3` properties, pass `column: "PropertyName"`. Nullable `Vector3?` rows with `null` never match.

## Reactive Subscriptions

Composed `DataVoTable<T>` queries (`Where`, `OrderBy`/`ThenBy`, `Skip`, `Take`, `Select`) integrate directly with DataVo's Z-set incremental view engine:

- **`.Subscribe(Action<QueryChange<T>> onChanged)`** delivers strongly-typed `Added`, `Removed`, `Updated`, and `UpdatedBefore` deltas when `db.DispatchPendingNotifications()` drains committed writes.
- **`.SubscribeInto(Memory<T> destination, Action<int> onUpdated)`** writes the live window directly into a caller-owned buffer with **0 B** heap allocations per drain for compiled `.Select(...)` struct projections:

```csharp
public struct HudSlot { public int Id; public int Score; }

var hud = new HudSlot[3];
using var sub = players
    .Where(100, static (p, min) => p.Score >= min)
    .OrderByDescending(static p => p.Score)
    .Take(3)
    .Select(static p => new HudSlot { Id = p.Id, Score = p.Score })
    .SubscribeInto(hud.AsMemory(), count => RenderHud(hud.AsSpan(0, count)));
```

- [Reactive Views](/manual/fundamentals/reactive-views) — Pull-drain Z-set IVM model and choosing a subscription API
