# Native AOT Deployment

> Source route: /manual/client-interfaces/native-aot
> Source file: manual/client-interfaces/native-aot.md

`DataVo.Core`, `DataVo.Data`, and `DataVo.Generators` are engineered for `.NET 10` Native AOT. Trim and AOT analyzers are enabled across the core and ADO.NET assemblies with `IL2026` and `IL3050` treated as build errors and verified on every change.

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
  <PublishAot>true</PublishAot>
  <InvariantGlobalization>true</InvariantGlobalization>
</PropertyGroup>
```

```bash
dotnet publish -c Release -r osx-arm64
```

## Package AOT Compatibility

| Package / Feature | Native AOT Status | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DataVo.Core` | **Verified** | Runtime SQL parser/executor, LSM/InMemory storage, `StreamQuery`, `StreamRef`, `Subscribe`, and `SubscribeZeroAlloc` use zero reflection. |
| `DataVo.Data` | **Verified** | `DataVoConnection`, `DataVoCommand`, `DataVoDataReader`, and `DataVoTransaction` are trim- and AOT-clean. |
| `DataVo.Generators` | **Verified** | `[DataVoTable]`, `[DataVoQuery]`, compiled LINQ interceptors, and `.SubscribeInto()` emit static C# at build time. |
| `DataVo.EntityFrameworkCore` | **Excluded** | Depends on EF Core's runtime infrastructure and is not covered by the Native AOT guarantee. |

## Writing AOT-Safe DataVo Code

- **Use `DataVo.Generators` for typed queries:** Prefer `[DataVoTable]` compiled LINQ and `[DataVoQuery]` over reflection-based mappers.
- **Avoid reflection-based micro-ORMs unless AOT-enabled:** `DataVo.Data` itself is AOT-clean, but third-party libraries layered on top (such as unconfigured Dapper reflection paths) govern their own AOT compatibility.
- **Use zero-allocation streaming on hot paths:** `StreamRef()` and `SubscribeZeroAlloc()` operate on `ReadOnlySpan<byte>` and `RowRef` structs with zero reflection and zero managed heap allocations.
- **Keep `DataVoContext.Insert<T>` types preserved:** `Insert<T>` carries `[DynamicallyAccessedMembers]` annotations so the trimmer preserves public properties and parameterless constructors, or use source-generated `db.Insert(player)` for zero-reflection writes.

## Verification

The repository validates AOT cleanliness with `scripts/check-aot-baseline.sh`, which publishes an AOT smoke application exercising `DataVo.Core`, `DataVo.Data`, and `DataVo.Generators` under `PublishAot=true`.

## See Also

- [Roslyn Source Generators](/manual/client-interfaces/source-generators) — Compile-time helpers and `[DataVoQuery]`
- [Compiled LINQ & Spatial Queries](/manual/client-interfaces/compiled-linq) — Zero-reflection LINQ interceptors
- [Zero-Allocation Rows](/manual/internals/zero-allocation-rows) — `RowRef` and `StreamRef` internals

# ADO.NET Provider (`DataVo.Data`)

> Source route: /manual/client-interfaces/ado-net
> Source file: manual/client-interfaces/ado-net.md

`DataVo.Data` implements the standard `System.Data.Common` abstractions (`DbConnection`, `DbCommand`, `DbDataReader`, `DbTransaction`, `DbParameter`) over the in-process DataVo engine. Any library targeting `IDbConnection` — including [Dapper](/manual/client-interfaces/dapper) — works without custom adapters.

```csharp
using DataVo.Data;

using var conn = new DataVoConnection("StorageMode=Lsm;DataSource=./game-data");
conn.Open();

using var cmd = conn.CreateCommand();
cmd.CommandText = "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS players (id INT PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(80), score INT)";
cmd.ExecuteNonQuery();

cmd.CommandText = "INSERT INTO players (id, name, score) VALUES (@id, @name, @score)";
cmd.Parameters.AddWithValue("@id", 1);
cmd.Parameters.AddWithValue("@name", "Ada");
cmd.Parameters.AddWithValue("@score", 1200);
cmd.ExecuteNonQuery();
```

## Connection Strings & Lifecycle

Use `DataVoConnectionStringBuilder` or a semicolon-delimited string with three supported keys:

| Key | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `StorageMode` | `InMemory` | `InMemory`, `Lsm`, or `Disk` (legacy). |
| `DataSource` | `"datavo"` | Database name (and storage directory path for `Lsm`/`Disk`). |
| `WalEnabled` | `true` (`Disk`) | Enables WAL in legacy `Disk` mode. |

When `conn.Open()` runs, it initializes the embedded engine, executes `CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS` for the `DataSource` database name, and selects it with `USE`. `Close()` rolls back any uncommitted transaction and releases the session.

## Provider Types

| `System.Data.Common` Base | DataVo Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DbConnection` | `DataVoConnection` | In-process engine handle; no network socket or connection pool. |
| `DbCommand` | `DataVoCommand` | Text commands with `@param` placeholders and `Prepare()`. |
| `DbDataReader` | `DataVoDataReader` | Forward-only reader over materialized command results. |
| `DbTransaction` | `DataVoTransaction` | Supports `Commit()`, `Rollback()`, and savepoints (`Save`, `Rollback(name)`, `Release`). |
| `DbParameter` | `DataVoParameter` | Supports `Parameters.AddWithValue("@name", value)`. |
| `DbConnectionStringBuilder` | `DataVoConnectionStringBuilder` | Strongly-typed builder for `StorageMode`, `DataSource`, and `WalEnabled`. |
| `Exception` | `DataVoException` | Exposes `ErrorCode`, `Line`, and `Column`. |

`DataVo.Data` does **not** ship a `DbProviderFactory`.

## Transactions & Prepared Commands

```csharp
using var tx = conn.BeginTransaction();

using var update = conn.CreateCommand();
update.CommandText = "UPDATE players SET score = @score WHERE id = @id";
update.Parameters.AddWithValue("@score", 1500);
update.Parameters.AddWithValue("@id", 1);
update.Prepare();
update.ExecuteNonQuery();

tx.Save("checkpoint1");
tx.Rollback("checkpoint1");
tx.Commit();
```

Calling `Prepare()` (or using parameterized commands) routes execution through DataVo's prepared-statement cache so repeated executions skip SQL parsing.

## Behavior Notes

- **Materialized reader:** `ExecuteReader()` executes the statement and walks materialized rows; for zero-allocation streaming, use `DataVoContext.StreamRef()` or compiled LINQ.
- **Metadata before `Read()`:** `GetName` and `GetFieldType` are available before the first `Read()` call. Column types are inferred from the first non-null value (`object` if all values are null).
- **Synchronous async wrappers:** `ExecuteReaderAsync` and other async methods complete synchronously on the calling thread because storage is in-process.
- **Timeouts and cancellation:** `Cancel()` is a no-op and `CommandTimeout` does not abort running statements; lock waits are bounded by `LockAcquireTimeoutMs`.
- **Single-process directory ownership:** Multiple `DataVoConnection` instances in the same process share one engine for a given directory; a second process opening the same directory fails with `DV7001_DATABASE_IN_USE`.

## See Also

- [Dapper](/manual/client-interfaces/dapper) — Using Dapper over `DataVoConnection`
- [Error Handling](/manual/reference/error-handling) — `DataVoException` and `DV*` error codes
- [Native AOT Deployment](/manual/client-interfaces/native-aot) — Trim and AOT compatibility for `DataVo.Data`

# Dapper

> Source route: /manual/client-interfaces/dapper
> Source file: manual/client-interfaces/dapper.md

Dapper works out of the box with DataVo via `DataVo.Data`. Because `DataVoConnection` implements `DbConnection`, Dapper's `IDbConnection` extension methods require no DataVo-specific adapter package.

```csharp
using Dapper;
using DataVo.Data;

using var conn = new DataVoConnection("StorageMode=InMemory;DataSource=game");
conn.Open();

conn.Execute("CREATE TABLE players (id INT PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(80), score INT)");
conn.Execute(
    "INSERT INTO players (id, name, score) VALUES (@Id, @Name, @Score)",
    new { Id = 1, Name = "Ada", Score = 1200 });

List<Player> top = conn
    .Query<Player>("SELECT id, name, score FROM players WHERE score >= @min", new { min = 500 })
    .ToList();

int total = conn.ExecuteScalar<int>("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM players");
```

Install both packages:

```bash
dotnet add package DataVo.Data --prerelease
dotnet add package Dapper
```

## Transactions & Parameterized Queries

Pass an `IDbTransaction` from `conn.BeginTransaction()` directly to Dapper's `Execute` and `Query` calls. Named parameters (`@Id`, `@min`) bind through `DataVoCommand`'s prepared-statement pipeline.

```csharp
using var tx = conn.BeginTransaction();

conn.Execute(
    "UPDATE players SET score = score + @bonus WHERE id = @id",
    new { bonus = 250, id = 1 },
    tx);

tx.Commit(); // or tx.Rollback()
```

### Verified Dapper Surface

Tested against `DataVoConnection` with Dapper `2.1.35`:

| Dapper Call | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `Execute` with anonymous-object parameters | Returns exact rows-affected count. |
| `Query<T>` / `QuerySingleOrDefault<T>` | Maps columns to POCO properties by name. |
| `ExecuteScalar<T>` | Returns the first column of the first row. |
| `QueryAsync<T>` | Completes synchronously (in-process engine). |
| `Execute` with `IDbTransaction` | Full `Commit()` / `Rollback()` participation. |

Features outside this verified set (such as multi-mapping, `QueryMultiple`, or list parameter expansion) pass through standard ADO.NET; validate them against your schema before relying on them.

## Dapper vs. Compiled LINQ

| Aspect | Dapper | [Compiled LINQ](/manual/client-interfaces/compiled-linq) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Query style | Raw SQL strings | Compile-time-checked C# lambdas |
| Row mapping | Reflection-based (per Dapper) | Source-generated, zero reflection |
| Heap allocations | Per-row POCO + Dapper overhead | **0 B** warm aggregates & buffered views |
| Native AOT | Governed by Dapper AOT support | Full Native AOT support |
| Best fit | Joins, ad-hoc SQL, existing Dapper code | Hot-path lookups, filtered aggregates, game loops |

Both interfaces can share the same underlying database: use Dapper for flexible SQL and compiled LINQ for hot paths.

## See Also

- [ADO.NET Provider (DataVo.Data)](/manual/client-interfaces/ado-net) — Connection strings, savepoints, and reader behavior
- [Compiled LINQ & Spatial Queries](/manual/client-interfaces/compiled-linq) — Zero-reflection compile-time queries
- [Choosing an Interface](/manual/getting-started/choosing-an-interface) — Compare all DataVo client APIs

# Entity Framework Core

> Source route: /manual/client-interfaces/entity-framework
> Source file: manual/client-interfaces/entity-framework.md

::: warning Experimental Preview — Excluded from Native AOT
`DataVo.EntityFrameworkCore` is an **experimental integration bridge**, not a standalone migration-capable EF Core provider. It relies on a host EF provider (such as `UseInMemoryDatabase`) for EF infrastructure services and is **excluded from DataVo's Native AOT guarantee**. For production or AOT workloads, use [`DataVoContext`](/manual/client-interfaces/datavo-context-api), [Compiled LINQ](/manual/client-interfaces/compiled-linq), or [ADO.NET / Dapper](/manual/client-interfaces/ado-net).
:::

`DataVo.EntityFrameworkCore` lets EF Core users evaluate DataVo-backed persistence and DataVo-native queries while keeping familiar `DbContext` and `DbSet<T>` models.

```csharp
using DataVo.EntityFrameworkCore;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;

var options = new DbContextOptionsBuilder<GameDbContext>()
    .UseInMemoryDatabase("datavo-ef-host")
    .UseDataVo(dataVo => dataVo
        .UseInMemoryStorage()
        .WithDataSource("game"))
    .Options;

using var ctx = new GameDbContext(options);
ctx.EnsureDataVoCreated();

ctx.Players.Add(new Player { Id = 1, Name = "Ada", Score = 1200, Region = "EU" });
ctx.SaveChanges();

List<Player> top = ctx.QueryFromDataVo<Player>(q => q
    .Where(static p => p.Score >= 1000)
    .OrderByDescending(static p => p.Score)
    .Take(10));
```

## Configuring `DataVoDbContext`

Derive from `DataVoDbContext` to access `LoadFromDataVo`, `QueryFromDataVo`, `QueryFromDataVoAsync`, and `ExplainQueryFromDataVo`:

```csharp
public sealed class GameDbContext : DataVoDbContext
{
    public GameDbContext(DbContextOptions<GameDbContext> options) : base(options) { }

    public DbSet<Player> Players => Set<Player>();

    protected override void OnModelCreating(ModelBuilder modelBuilder)
    {
        modelBuilder.Entity<Player>(entity =>
        {
            entity.ToTable("players");
            entity.HasKey(static p => p.Id);
            entity.Property(static p => p.Name).HasMaxLength(80);
        });
    }
}
```

- **`UseDataVo(...)`** attaches DataVo storage options (or a DataVo connection string) to `DbContextOptionsBuilder`.
- **`EnsureDataVoCreated()`** initializes the mapped tables in DataVo (available on both `DbContext` and `DatabaseFacade`).
- **`LoadFromDataVo()`** synchronizes EF's change tracker from DataVo when rows were written by another context or directly through `DataVoContext`.
- **`ExplainQueryFromDataVo<T>(...)`** inspects whether a LINQ expression fits the supported DataVo-native translation subset before running it.

## Vector Query Preview Shims

Inside `QueryFromDataVo`, `DataVoVectorDbFunctions` exposes preview shims (`CosineDistance` and `L2Distance`) that translate to DataVo's `<=>` and `<->` SQL vector operators:

```csharp
float[] queryVector = [1f, 0f, 0f];

List<Document> nearest = ctx.QueryFromDataVo<Document>(q => q
    .Where(d => DataVoVectorDbFunctions.CosineDistance(EF.Functions, d.Embedding, queryVector) < 0.3)
    .OrderBy(d => DataVoVectorDbFunctions.CosineDistance(EF.Functions, d.Embedding, queryVector))
    .Take(5));
```

Note that `COSINE_DISTANCE()` and `L2_DISTANCE()` exist only as EF Core preview shims, not as core DataVo SQL scalar functions.

## Current Limitations

| Area | Status |
| --- | --- |
| `DbSet` CRUD (`Add`, `SaveChanges`, `LoadFromDataVo`) | Supported for mapped scalar CLR properties |
| `QueryFromDataVo` / `QueryFromDataVoAsync` | Supported for bounded `Where`, `OrderBy`/`ThenBy`, `Skip`, `Take`, `Select` |
| Vector distance shims (`CosineDistance`, `L2Distance`) | Preview translation inside `QueryFromDataVo` |
| EF Migrations (`dotnet ef migrations`), shadow properties, complex joins, `GroupBy` | **Not supported** (unsupported patterns throw `DataVoEfException`) |
| Native AOT (`PublishAot=true`) | **Not supported** |

## See Also

- [Compiled LINQ & Spatial Queries](/manual/client-interfaces/compiled-linq) — AOT-safe, zero-reflection LINQ alternative
- [Error Handling](/manual/reference/error-handling) — `DataVoEfException` and engine error codes
- [Native AOT Deployment](/manual/client-interfaces/native-aot) — Why `DataVo.EntityFrameworkCore` is excluded from AOT

# SQL Compatibility

> Source route: /manual/sql/compatibility
> Source file: manual/sql/compatibility.md

DataVo SQL is a compact embedded-engine dialect designed for predictable, zero-allocation execution in .NET. It covers standard relational CRUD, joins, aggregates, transactions, and vector search without emulating PostgreSQL or SQLite system catalogs.

```sql
CREATE TABLE documents (
    id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    title VARCHAR(200),
    category VARCHAR(80),
    embedding VECTOR(384)
);

SELECT id, title, embedding <=> '[0.1, 0.2, ...]' AS distance
FROM documents
WHERE category = 'guide'
ORDER BY distance ASC
LIMIT 5;
```

## Dialect Matrix (DataVo v0.4 vs. SQLite & PostgreSQL)

| Feature | DataVo v0.4 | SQLite / PostgreSQL Difference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CREATE` / `DROP` (`DATABASE`, `TABLE`, `INDEX`) | Supported | Uses `DROP INDEX name ON table`; supports `USING BTREE`, `HNSW`, `FLAT`, `COLUMNAR`. |
| `ALTER TABLE` | Limited | Supports `ADD COLUMN`, `DROP COLUMN`, `MODIFY COLUMN`; rejects key, FK, or indexed column changes. |
| `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, `VACUUM` | Supported | No `MERGE`, `UPSERT` (`ON CONFLICT`), `RETURNING`, or PostgreSQL `COPY`. |
| Transactions & Savepoints | Supported | Snapshot isolation via `BEGIN`, `COMMIT`, `ROLLBACK`, `SAVEPOINT`, `ROLLBACK TO`, `RELEASE`; not serializable. |
| `SELECT`, `WHERE`, `ORDER BY`, `LIMIT`, `OFFSET` | Supported | `SELECT DISTINCT` runs on the general evaluator; `ORDER BY ... LIMIT k` uses bounded top-k on typed paths. |
| Joins (`INNER`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `FULL`, `CROSS`) | Supported | `INNER`/`LEFT` on integer keys use typed hash joins; `RIGHT`/`FULL`/`CROSS` and text/`GUID` keys use the general path. |
| Aggregates, `GROUP BY`, `HAVING` | Supported | `COUNT`, `SUM`, `AVG`, `MIN`, `MAX` (including `DISTINCT`); `HAVING` works with or without `GROUP BY`. |
| Subqueries & CTEs | Supported | `IN (SELECT ...)`, `EXISTS`, `NOT EXISTS`; non-recursive `WITH` CTEs (`WITH RECURSIVE` is reactive-only). |
| Set Operations | Partial | `UNION` and `UNION ALL` supported; `INTERSECT` and `EXCEPT` are not supported. |
| Window Functions | Limited | `RANK() OVER ([PARTITION BY ...] ORDER BY ...)` only; no `ROW_NUMBER`, `DENSE_RANK`, `LAG`, `LEAD`, or frames. |
| Scalar Functions & Expressions | Limited | `LOWER`, `UPPER`, arithmetic `+ - * /`; no `CASE WHEN`, `COALESCE`, `CAST`, `PRAGMA`, or date/math functions. |
| Vector Search (`VECTOR(n)`, `<->`, `<=>`) | Supported | Native DataVo extension (similar to `pgvector`, without `<#>` inner-product). |
| Views, Triggers, Procedures, UDFs | Not supported | Use [Live Reactive Views](/manual/fundamentals/reactive-views) (`Subscribe`) for continuous queries in C#. |
| System Catalogs (`pg_class`, `sqlite_master`) | Not supported | Use `SHOW DATABASES`, `SHOW TABLES`, `DESCRIBE <table>`, and `EXPLAIN`. |
| RBAC Security Commands | Supported | `CREATE USER`/`ROLE`, `GRANT`, `REVOKE`, `LOGIN`, `LOGOUT`, `SHOW USERS`/`ROLES`/`GRANTS` (not PostgreSQL roles). |

## Execution Paths & Performance Notes

Every construct marked **Supported** returns identical results across storage modes, but execution speed varies by path:

- **Typed fast paths:** Single-table filters, aggregates, `BETWEEN` on clustered primary keys, and `INNER`/`LEFT` joins on integer equality keys read stored rows directly with minimal allocations.
- **General evaluator:** `SELECT DISTINCT`, `RIGHT`/`FULL`/`CROSS` joins, joins on `VARCHAR` or `GUID` keys, cross-table `OR` predicates, CTEs, window functions, and queries inside explicit transactions materialize row dictionaries and are slower on large tables.

## Key Type Differences

- **`FLOAT` is 32-bit** (`System.Single`), unlike SQLite `REAL` or SQL Server `FLOAT` (64-bit). Use `DOUBLE` for 64-bit floating-point values.
- **`VARCHAR` comparisons are ordinal** (UTF-8 byte/code-point order), not collation-aware or case-insensitive.
- **No silent type fallbacks:** Unsupported types such as `DECIMAL`, `NUMERIC`, `DATETIME`, and `TIMESTAMP` throw an explicit `ParserException` instead of silently storing text.

## See Also
- [Data Types](/manual/sql/data-types) — Supported SQL types, .NET CLR mappings, and unsupported type errors
- [Query Planner](/manual/internals/query-planner) — How DataVo chooses between typed fast paths and the general evaluator
- [Functions & Operators](/manual/sql/functions) — Complete list of aggregates, window functions, scalar functions, and operators

---

# Data Types

> Source route: /manual/sql/data-types
> Source file: manual/sql/data-types.md

Every column in a DataVo table has a strict schema type. DataVo stores each accepted type natively and rejects unsupported SQL types with an explicit `ParserException` rather than silently falling back to text.

```sql
CREATE TABLE documents (
    id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    external_id GUID,
    title VARCHAR(200),
    published_on DATE,
    rating DOUBLE,
    is_public BIT,
    embedding VECTOR(384)
);
```

## Supported SQL Types

| Canonical Type | Accepted Aliases | .NET CLR Type | Storage & Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `INT` | `INTEGER`, `SMALLINT`, `TINYINT`, `MEDIUMINT` | `int` (`Int32`) | 32-bit signed integer. Single `INT` primary key is clustered on `Lsm`. |
| `BIGINT` | — | `long` (`Int64`) | 64-bit signed integer. Also used as the return type of `COUNT(...)`. |
| `FLOAT` | `REAL` | `float` (`Single`) | 32-bit IEEE 754 float (not 64-bit like SQLite `REAL`). |
| `DOUBLE` | `DOUBLE PRECISION` | `double` (`Double`) | 64-bit IEEE 754 double. |
| `BIT` | `BOOL`, `BOOLEAN` | `bool` (`Boolean`) | Accepts `TRUE`/`FALSE` (any case); `1`/`0` and `'true'`/`'false'` are also parsed. |
| `DATE` | — | `DataVoDate` | Calendar date stored as a 32-bit day count since `0001-01-01`. |
| `GUID` | `UUID`, `UNIQUEIDENTIFIER` | `Guid` | 128-bit UUID. Single `GUID` primary key is clustered on `Lsm`. |
| `VARCHAR(n)` | `NVARCHAR`, `CHAR`, `NCHAR`, `TEXT`, `STRING` | `string` | UTF-8 variable-length text. Comparisons and sorting are ordinal (case-sensitive). |
| `VECTOR(n)` | `VEC2`, `VEC3`, `VEC4`, `FLOAT[n]`, `REAL[n]` | `float[]` | Fixed-dimension `n`-element array of 32-bit floats. |

::: info DataVo Extension
`VECTOR(n)` (with `VEC2`, `VEC3`, `VEC4`, `FLOAT[n]`, and `REAL[n]` shorthands) and `GUID` (`UUID`, `UNIQUEIDENTIFIER`) are first-class DataVo extensions beyond standard SQLite. `VECTOR` is a reserved keyword, so a column cannot be named `Vector`.
:::

## The `DATE` Storage & Row Contract

`DATE` stores only a calendar date—no time-of-day or timezone component—as a zero-based 32-bit `DayNumber` (`0` = `0001-01-01`, `3652058` = `9999-12-31`).

- **Query materialization:** Reading a `DATE` column returns a `DataVoDate` struct (`DataVo.Core.DataVoDate`).
- **.NET interoperability:** On `.NET 10`, convert cleanly with `DataVoDate.FromDateOnly(DateOnly)` / `.ToDateOnly()` or `DataVoDate.FromDateTime(DateTime)` / `.ToDateTime()` (midnight `DateTimeKind.Unspecified`).
- **Timestamps:** If you need a point in time with sub-day precision, store Unix epoch milliseconds or ticks in a `BIGINT` column.

## Unsupported Types (`ParserException`)

DataVo throws a `ParserException` at `CREATE TABLE` or `ALTER TABLE` time for types it cannot store faithfully:

| Unsupported Type | Error Guidance / Workaround |
| --- | --- |
| `DECIMAL`, `NUMERIC`, `MONEY` | Use `DOUBLE` for approximate numeric values, or `VARCHAR` to preserve exact decimal digits. |
| `DATETIME`, `TIMESTAMP`, `TIME` | Use `DATE` for calendar dates, or `BIGINT` for Unix timestamps / ticks. |
| `LONG` | Use `BIGINT` for 64-bit integers. |
| `BLOB`, `BINARY`, `VARBINARY`, `JSON`, `JSONB` | Not supported as native column types in `v0.4`; encode as `VARCHAR` (e.g., Base64 or JSON text). |

## See Also
- [DDL Statements](/manual/sql/statements/ddl) — Declaring columns, constraints, and defaults in `CREATE TABLE`
- [Indexes](/manual/sql/statements/indexes) — Choosing B-Tree, HNSW, FLAT, or COLUMNAR indexes by column type
- [SQL Compatibility](/manual/sql/compatibility) — Full dialect comparison against SQLite and PostgreSQL

# SELECT & EXPLAIN

> Source route: /manual/sql/statements/select
> Source file: manual/sql/statements/select.md

`SELECT` retrieves, filters, joins, aggregates, and ranks rows from one or more tables. `EXPLAIN` inspects the query planner's chosen execution path without returning table rows.

```sql
SELECT p.Region, COUNT(*) AS PlayerCount, AVG(p.Score) AS AvgScore
FROM players p
WHERE p.Score >= 100
GROUP BY p.Region
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5
ORDER BY AvgScore DESC
LIMIT 10 OFFSET 0;
```

## Clause Reference

| Clause | Syntax | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SELECT` | `SELECT [DISTINCT] <expr> [AS alias], ...` | Supports `*`, column refs, aliases, aggregates, `RANK()`, scalar functions, arithmetic, and vector distance. |
| `FROM` | `FROM <table> [AS alias]` | Accepts base tables and CTE names. |
| `JOIN` | `INNER \| LEFT \| RIGHT \| FULL [OUTER] \| CROSS JOIN <table> [alias] ON <cond>` | `INNER` and `LEFT` on integer equality keys use typed hash joins; others use the general evaluator. |
| `WHERE` | `WHERE <predicate>` | Supports `AND`, `OR`, `NOT`, comparisons, `IN`, `BETWEEN`, `LIKE`/`NOT LIKE`, `IS [NOT] NULL`, subqueries, and vector distance predicates. |
| `GROUP BY` | `GROUP BY <col>, ...` | Groups rows before applying aggregate functions. |
| `HAVING` | `HAVING <predicate>` | Filters grouped results; also works **without** `GROUP BY` (treats the filtered table as a single group). |
| `ORDER BY` | `ORDER BY <expr> [ASC \| DESC], ...` | Supports multi-column sorting and vector distance ranking. |
| `LIMIT` / `OFFSET` | `LIMIT <n> [OFFSET <m>]` | `ORDER BY ... LIMIT k` uses a bounded top-k heap on typed scans and joins. |

## Joins

```sql
SELECT u.Name, d.Name AS Department
FROM Users u
LEFT JOIN Departments d ON u.DepartmentId = d.Id;
```

`INNER JOIN` and `LEFT JOIN` on integer equality keys run on DataVo's typed hash-join path across any number of tables. `RIGHT JOIN`, `FULL OUTER JOIN`, `CROSS JOIN`, self-joins, text/`GUID` join keys, and cross-table `OR` predicates are fully supported on the general evaluator.

## CTEs (`WITH`), Subqueries, and `UNION`

Non-recursive CTEs are materialized before the main query runs. `WITH RECURSIVE` is supported for [Live Reactive Views](/manual/fundamentals/reactive-views) only.

```sql
WITH HighScorers AS (
    SELECT Id, Name, Region FROM players WHERE Score >= 900
)
SELECT Region, COUNT(*) AS EliteCount
FROM HighScorers
GROUP BY Region;
```

- **Subqueries:** Use `col IN (SELECT ...)`, `EXISTS (SELECT ...)`, and `NOT EXISTS (SELECT ...)` in `WHERE`.
- **Set operations:** Combine compatible `SELECT` branches with `UNION` (deduplicated) or `UNION ALL` (preserves duplicates). Parenthesized `UNION` branches, `INTERSECT`, and `EXCEPT` are not supported in `v0.4`.

## `EXPLAIN`

Prefix any `SELECT` statement with `EXPLAIN` to inspect how the planner executes it:

```sql
EXPLAIN SELECT Id, Name FROM players WHERE Score > 500 ORDER BY Score DESC LIMIT 10;
```

`EXPLAIN` returns a single diagnostic row with four columns:

| Column | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Plan` | High-level logical plan summary |
| `Physical` | Selected physical operator or fast path (e.g., typed scan, columnar aggregate, HNSW search) |
| `EstimatedCost` | Planner's estimated relative execution cost |
| `Reason` | Why the planner chose (or fell back from) a fast path |

## See Also
- [Functions & Operators](/manual/sql/functions) — Aggregates, `RANK()`, `LOWER`/`UPPER`, and vector distance operators
- [Query Planner](/manual/internals/query-planner) — Deep dive into DataVo's typed fast paths and fallback rules
- [Streaming Queries](/manual/fundamentals/streaming-queries) — Lazy `StreamQuery` and zero-allocation `StreamRef` execution

# DML Statements

> Source route: /manual/sql/statements/dml
> Source file: manual/sql/statements/dml.md

Data Manipulation Language (DML) statements add, modify, remove, and compact rows in a table. All DML statements participate in explicit transactions when executed between `BEGIN` and `COMMIT`.

```sql
INSERT INTO players (Id, Name, Score, Region)
VALUES (1, 'Ada', 980, 'EU');

UPDATE players
SET Score = 1050
WHERE Id = 1;

DELETE FROM players WHERE Score < 100;
VACUUM players;
```

## `INSERT INTO`

Insert rows using either a column-targeted list (recommended for schema resilience) or a positional full-row list:

```sql
-- Column-targeted (recommended)
INSERT INTO documents (id, title, category, embedding)
VALUES (1, 'Quickstart', 'guide', '[1.0, 0.0, 0.0]');

-- Positional full-row (must match table column order)
INSERT INTO documents
VALUES (2, 'Vector Search', 'guide', '[0.9, 0.1, 0.0]');
```

- The number of values must match the number of target columns (or all table columns for positional inserts).
- Omitted columns in a column-targeted insert receive their declared `DEFAULT` literal or `NULL` (if nullable).
- Vector columns accept bracketed float array string literals such as `'[0.9, 0.1, 0.0]'` matching the column's fixed dimension.
- `PRIMARY KEY`, `UNIQUE`, `NOT NULL`, and `FOREIGN KEY` constraints are enforced on every insert.

## `UPDATE`

Modify one or more columns on rows matching a `WHERE` predicate:

```sql
UPDATE players
SET Score = Score + 50,
    Region = 'US'
WHERE Id = 1;
```

- Omitting `WHERE` updates every row in the table.
- Updating a `PRIMARY KEY`, `UNIQUE`, or `FOREIGN KEY` column re-validates key constraints and updates secondary indexes atomically.
- Narrow single-row updates on fixed-width schemas can also use compiled fast paths via [Compiled LINQ (`ExecuteUpdate`)](/manual/client-interfaces/compiled-linq) or [Source Generators](/manual/client-interfaces/source-generators).

## `DELETE FROM`

Remove rows matching a `WHERE` predicate:

```sql
DELETE FROM players
WHERE Region = 'Legacy' AND Score = 0;
```

- Omitting `WHERE` deletes all rows in the table.
- Foreign-key `ON DELETE CASCADE` deletes dependent child rows; `ON DELETE RESTRICT` rejects the delete if child rows still reference the target key.

## `VACUUM`

Reclaim space from deleted rows and compact table storage:

```sql
VACUUM players;
```

| Statement | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `INSERT INTO ... VALUES (...)` | Single table | Supports column lists, defaults, and vector literals. No `ON CONFLICT` / `MERGE`. |
| `UPDATE ... SET ... [WHERE ...]` | Single table | Supports multi-column assignments and expressions. No `RETURNING`. |
| `DELETE FROM ... [WHERE ...]` | Single table | Enforces `ON DELETE CASCADE` / `RESTRICT` foreign keys. |
| `VACUUM <table>` | Single table | Compacts deleted slots and storage files after heavy deletes. |

## See Also
- [Transactions](/manual/sql/statements/transactions) — Grouping DML writes with `BEGIN`, `SAVEPOINT`, `COMMIT`, and `ROLLBACK`
- [DataVoContext API](/manual/client-interfaces/datavo-context-api) — High-throughput C# `BulkInsert`, `InsertTypedBatch`, and `ApplyBatch`
- [DDL Statements](/manual/sql/statements/ddl) — Defining primary keys, defaults, and foreign-key delete actions

---

# DDL Statements

> Source route: /manual/sql/statements/ddl
> Source file: manual/sql/statements/ddl.md

Data Definition Language (DDL) statements create, alter, and drop databases and tables. DataVo enforces declared primary keys, unique constraints, nullability, defaults, and foreign-key referential integrity at write time.

```sql
CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS App;
USE App;

CREATE TABLE Departments (
    Id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    Name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL UNIQUE
);

CREATE TABLE Employees (
    Id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    Name VARCHAR(120) NOT NULL,
    DepartmentId INT REFERENCES Departments(Id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
    Active BIT DEFAULT true
);
```

## Database Statements

```sql
CREATE DATABASE [IF NOT EXISTS] <db_name>;
DROP DATABASE [IF EXISTS] <db_name>;
```

Use `USE <db_name>` to switch the active database for the current session.

## `CREATE TABLE`

```sql
CREATE TABLE [IF NOT EXISTS] <table_name> (
    <col_name> <type> [NOT NULL] [DEFAULT <literal>] [PRIMARY KEY] [UNIQUE]
                      [REFERENCES <ref_table>(<ref_col>) [ON DELETE CASCADE | RESTRICT]],
    ...,
    [PRIMARY KEY (<col1>, ...)],
    [UNIQUE (<col>)],
    [FOREIGN KEY (<col>) REFERENCES <ref_table>(<ref_col>) [ON DELETE CASCADE | RESTRICT]]
);
```

### Supported Constraints

| Constraint | Scope | Rules in `v0.4` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PRIMARY KEY` | Column or table | Only one `PRIMARY KEY` per table. Single `INT` or `GUID` primary keys are clustered on `Lsm`. |
| `UNIQUE` | Single column | Enforces uniqueness across non-NULL values; multiple `NULL`s are permitted. Multi-column `UNIQUE (a, b)` is not yet supported. |
| `NOT NULL` | Column | Rejects `NULL` values on `INSERT` and `UPDATE`. |
| `DEFAULT <literal>` | Column | Must be a constant literal (`NULL`, number, quoted string, `true`/`false`). Expressions like `NOW()` are rejected. |
| `FOREIGN KEY ... REFERENCES` | Column or table | Validates parent existence on write. Supports `ON DELETE CASCADE` and `ON DELETE RESTRICT`. |

## `ALTER TABLE`

DataVo supports three `ALTER TABLE` operations:

```sql
ALTER TABLE Employees ADD COLUMN Role VARCHAR(60) DEFAULT 'member';
ALTER TABLE Employees MODIFY COLUMN Name VARCHAR(200);
ALTER TABLE Employees DROP COLUMN Role;
```

| Operation | Behavior & Restrictions |
| --- | --- |
| `ADD COLUMN` | Rewrites existing rows and backfills the new column with its `DEFAULT` literal or `NULL`. |
| `DROP COLUMN` | Rejects columns that belong to a primary key, foreign key, referenced parent key, or index. |
| `MODIFY COLUMN` | Rejects incompatible type changes or modifications to key, foreign-key, referenced, or indexed columns. |

## `DROP TABLE`

```sql
DROP TABLE [IF EXISTS] <table_name>;
```

Drops the table definition, its rows, and its associated indexes from the active database.

## See Also
- [Data Types](/manual/sql/data-types) — Complete list of column types and aliases for `CREATE TABLE`
- [Indexes](/manual/sql/statements/indexes) — Creating `BTREE`, `HNSW`, `FLAT`, and `COLUMNAR` indexes after table creation
- [DML Statements](/manual/sql/statements/dml) — Inserting, updating, and deleting rows

---

# Indexes

> Source route: /manual/sql/statements/indexes
> Source file: manual/sql/statements/indexes.md

DataVo supports four index methods via `CREATE INDEX`: B-Tree for scalar lookups and ranges, `HNSW` and `FLAT` for vector similarity search, and `COLUMNAR` for vectorized analytical aggregations.

```sql
-- Scalar B-Tree index (default)
CREATE INDEX ix_players_score ON players (Score);

-- Approximate vector index
CREATE INDEX ix_documents_emb ON documents (embedding)
USING HNSW WITH (metric = 'cosine', m = 16, ef_construction = 64, ef_search = 64);

-- Analytical columnar index
CREATE INDEX cx_players_stats ON players (Score, Id) USING COLUMNAR;

-- Drop an index
DROP INDEX ix_players_score ON players;
```

## Index Types Overview

| Method | Syntax | Target Columns | Best For |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `BTREE` (default) | `USING BTREE` (or omit `USING`) | Single or composite scalar columns | Point lookups, range scans, and `ORDER BY` on scalar columns. |
| `HNSW` | `USING HNSW [WITH (...)]` | Single `VECTOR(n)` column | Fast approximate nearest-neighbor search on medium/large embedding tables. |
| `FLAT` | `USING FLAT [WITH (metric = ...)]` | Single `VECTOR(n)` column | Exact exhaustive vector search on small tables and recall benchmarks. |
| `COLUMNAR` | `USING COLUMNAR` | Numeric, `BIT`, and `DATE` columns | High-speed `COUNT`, `SUM`, `AVG`, `MIN`, `MAX` without reading full rows. |

::: info DataVo Extension
`USING HNSW`, `USING FLAT`, and `USING COLUMNAR` (along with the `WITH (...)` tuning clause) are DataVo extensions beyond standard SQLite/ANSI SQL.
:::

## Scalar B-Tree Indexes

```sql
CREATE INDEX ix_players_region_score ON players (Region, Score);
```

- A scalar index stores only rows where **all** indexed columns are non-`NULL`. Rows with a `NULL` key receive no index entry, so `IS NULL` predicates scan rows and multiple `NULL`s may coexist in a `UNIQUE` column.

## Vector Indexes (`HNSW` & `FLAT`)

Both `HNSW` and `FLAT` accept `metric` in `WITH (...)`. Passing graph options (`m`, `ef_construction`, `ef_search`, `enable_diversity_heuristic`) to `FLAT` or `BTREE`, or passing out-of-range values, throws an error and creates no index. Option names ignore case and underscores.

| Option | Default | Valid Range | Applies To | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `metric` | `'cosine'` | `'cosine'`, `'euclidean'` (or `'l2'`) | `HNSW`, `FLAT` | Distance metric persisted in the catalog. Use `'euclidean'` for 3D positions. |
| `m` | `16` | `2` – `128` | `HNSW` | Bi-directional links per graph layer (doubled on layer 0). |
| `ef_construction` | `64` | `1` – `4096` | `HNSW` | Candidate beam width during index build. |
| `ef_search` | `64` | `1` – `4096` | `HNSW` | Minimum candidate beam width during search. |
| `enable_diversity_heuristic` | `true` | `true`, `false` | `HNSW` | Keeps cross-cluster links; disable only for faster builds on uniform data. |

For filtered vector searches, DataVo widens the candidate beam automatically and switches to an exact scan when graph traversal would cost more than scanning stored vectors—ensuring filtered `LIMIT k` queries return the full `k` rows when enough rows match.

## Columnar Indexes (`USING COLUMNAR`)

```sql
CREATE INDEX cx_players ON players (Score, Id) USING COLUMNAR;
```

- **Allowed types:** `INT`, `BIGINT`, `FLOAT`, `DOUBLE`, `BIT`, and `DATE` only. Any other type is rejected.
- **Storage modes:** Accelerates `InMemory` (4–8 bytes/row/column in RAM) and `Lsm` (persisted as format-v8 columnar segments inside `.sst` files). Legacy `Disk` mode records the index but falls back to row scans.
- **Query eligibility:** Used for aggregates without `GROUP BY` whose `WHERE` clause is an `AND` of column-to-literal comparisons or `IS NULL` checks over indexed columns. Queries inside explicit transactions, queries with `GROUP BY`, or comparisons where precision could differ (e.g., fractional literal vs. `INT`, `BIT`/`DATE` predicates, or `NaN` floats) fall back to row scans.
- **Scope:** Never serves point lookups and does not replace a B-Tree index. Multiple columnar indexes on the same table are consolidated internally.

## `DROP INDEX`

```sql
DROP INDEX <index_name> ON <table_name>;
```

DataVo requires the `ON <table_name>` clause when dropping an index.

## See Also
- [Vector Search](/manual/fundamentals/vector-search) — End-to-end guide to embeddings, `SearchNearest`, and spatial queries
- [Data Types](/manual/sql/data-types) — `VECTOR(n)`, `VEC2`/`VEC3`/`VEC4`, and `FLOAT[n]` declarations
- [Query Planner](/manual/internals/query-planner) — When the planner selects B-Tree, HNSW, FLAT, or Columnar fast paths

# Transactions & Savepoints

> Source route: /manual/sql/statements/transactions
> Source file: manual/sql/statements/transactions.md

DataVo provides multi-statement atomic transactions with MVCC snapshot isolation and nested savepoints. Transaction boundaries are controlled directly through SQL statements (or `DataVoConnection.BeginTransaction()` when using ADO.NET).

```sql
BEGIN TRANSACTION;

INSERT INTO players (Id, Name, Score, Region) VALUES (10, 'Ada', 900, 'EU');
SAVEPOINT after_insert;

UPDATE players SET Score = 50 WHERE Id = 10;
ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT after_insert;

RELEASE SAVEPOINT after_insert;
COMMIT;
```

## Statement Reference

| Statement | Optional Syntax | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `BEGIN` | `BEGIN TRANSACTION` | Starts an explicit transaction and captures an MVCC read snapshot for the current session. |
| `COMMIT` | — | Atomically publishes all buffered writes in the transaction to the storage engine and WAL (if enabled). |
| `ROLLBACK` | — | Discards all uncommitted writes in the current transaction and closes the transaction. |
| `SAVEPOINT <name>` | — | Marks a named rollback point within the active transaction. |
| `ROLLBACK TO <name>` | `ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT <name>` | Undoes all writes made after `<name>` while keeping the transaction open and earlier writes intact. |
| `RELEASE <name>` | `RELEASE SAVEPOINT <name>` | Removes the named savepoint (and any newer savepoints) without rolling back its changes. |

## MVCC Snapshot Behavior

- **Snapshot isolation (not serializable):** A transaction sees a consistent snapshot of rows committed before it began, plus its own uncommitted writes. Concurrent readers never block writers, and writers never block readers.
- **Autocommit outside `BEGIN`:** Statements executed outside an explicit `BEGIN` ... `COMMIT` block commit automatically.
- **Query path note:** Queries executed inside an explicit transaction evaluate against the transaction's write buffer on the general evaluator rather than bypassing it via storage-only fast paths (such as `COLUMNAR` aggregates).
- **C# usage:** `DataVoContext` does not expose a `BeginTransaction()` C# method—execute `db.Execute("BEGIN")` / `db.Execute("COMMIT")` / `db.Execute("ROLLBACK")` directly. If you use ADO.NET (`DataVo.Data`), `DataVoConnection.BeginTransaction()` wraps these SQL statements for you.

## See Also
- [Transactions & MVCC](/manual/fundamentals/transactions-and-mvcc) — Architecture of MVCC snapshots, write-conflict semantics, and WAL durability
- [DML Statements](/manual/sql/statements/dml) — `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, and `DELETE` statements that participate in transactions
- [ADO.NET Provider](/manual/client-interfaces/ado-net) — Using `DataVoTransaction` with `DataVoConnection`

# Admin & Security Statements

> Source route: /manual/sql/statements/admin-and-security
> Source file: manual/sql/statements/admin-and-security.md

DataVo includes session and schema-inspection commands (`USE`, `GO`, `SHOW`, `DESCRIBE`) alongside a lightweight built-in role-based access control (RBAC) system for managing users, roles, and permissions.

```sql
-- Session & inspection
USE App;
SHOW TABLES;
DESCRIBE players;

-- RBAC setup
CREATE ROLE analyst;
GRANT READ TO ROLE analyst;
CREATE USER alice IDENTIFIED BY 's3cr3t' ROLE analyst;
LOGIN alice IDENTIFIED BY 's3cr3t';
```

## Session & Schema Inspection

| Statement | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `USE <database>` | Switches the active database for the current session. |
| `GO` | Batch separator (no-op statement accepted for SQL script compatibility). |
| `SHOW DATABASES` | Lists all databases registered in the engine catalog. |
| `SHOW TABLES` | Lists all tables in the active database. |
| `DESCRIBE <table>` | Displays column names, types, lengths, keys, and defaults for `<table>`. |

## RBAC & Security Statements

DataVo's security model is a standalone embedded RBAC system (not a PostgreSQL role hierarchy).

| Statement | Syntax |
| --- | --- |
| `CREATE USER` | `CREATE USER <user> IDENTIFIED [BY \| PASSWORD] '<password>' [ROLE <role>]` |
| `DROP USER` | `DROP USER <user>` |
| `CREATE ROLE` | `CREATE ROLE <role>` |
| `DROP ROLE` | `DROP ROLE <role>` |
| `GRANT` (permissions) | `GRANT <perm1> [, <perm2>, ...] TO [ROLE] <user_or_role>` |
| `GRANT` (role) | `GRANT ROLE <role> TO <user>` |
| `REVOKE` (permissions) | `REVOKE <perm1> [, <perm2>, ...] FROM [ROLE] <user_or_role>` |
| `REVOKE` (role) | `REVOKE ROLE <role> FROM <user>` |
| `LOGIN` | `LOGIN <user> IDENTIFIED [BY \| PASSWORD] '<password>'` |
| `LOGOUT` | `LOGOUT` |
| `SHOW USERS` | `SHOW USERS` |
| `SHOW ROLES` | `SHOW ROLES` |
| `SHOW GRANTS` | `SHOW GRANTS [FOR USER <user> \| FOR ROLE <role>]` |

### Supported Permission Tokens

| Permission | Accepted Aliases | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `READ` | `READDATA` | `SELECT`, `EXPLAIN`, and read-only inspection queries |
| `WRITE` | `WRITEDATA` | `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, `VACUUM` |
| `SCHEMA` | `MANAGESCHEMA` | `CREATE`/`ALTER`/`DROP` for databases, tables, and indexes |
| `TRANSACTION` | `TRANSACTIONS`, `MANAGETRANSACTIONS` | `BEGIN`, `COMMIT`, `ROLLBACK`, and savepoints |
| `SECURITY` | `MANAGESECURITY` | User, role, and grant management |
| `ADMIN` | — | Full administrative privileges across all operations |

## See Also
- [DDL Statements](/manual/sql/statements/ddl) — Creating and dropping databases and tables
- [Configuration Reference](/manual/reference/configuration) — Engine authentication and security configuration options
- [Error Handling](/manual/reference/error-handling) — `AuthorizationException` and DataVo error codes

# Functions & Operators

> Source route: /manual/sql/functions
> Source file: manual/sql/functions.md

DataVo v0.4 ships a focused set of SQL aggregates, one window function (`RANK()`), two string scalar functions, standard comparison/logical/arithmetic operators, and native vector distance operators.

```sql
SELECT
    UPPER(Region) AS RegionCode,
    COUNT(*) AS Players,
    AVG(Score) AS AvgScore,
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY Region ORDER BY Score DESC) AS RegionRank
FROM players
WHERE Score BETWEEN 100 AND 1000 AND Name LIKE 'A%';
```

## Aggregate Functions

| Function | Return / Behavior | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `COUNT(*)` / `COUNT(col)` | `BIGINT` (`long`) | `COUNT(*)` counts all rows; `COUNT(col)` ignores `NULL`s. |
| `COUNT(DISTINCT col)` | `BIGINT` (`long`) | Counts distinct non-`NULL` values (general evaluator). `COUNT(DISTINCT *)` is a parse error. |
| `SUM([DISTINCT] col)` | Numeric sum | Ignores `NULL` values. |
| `AVG([DISTINCT] col)` | Floating-point average | Ignores `NULL` values. |
| `MIN([DISTINCT] col)` | Minimum value | Works on numeric, text, and date columns. |
| `MAX([DISTINCT] col)` | Maximum value | Works on numeric, text, and date columns. |

`HAVING` can evaluate aggregates that are not present in the `SELECT` list, and works both with and without `GROUP BY`.

## Window Functions

DataVo v0.4 supports a single window function:

```sql
RANK() OVER ([PARTITION BY <col>, ...] ORDER BY <col> [ASC | DESC], ...)
```

- `ORDER BY` inside `OVER (...)` is required; `PARTITION BY` is optional.
- **Not implemented in v0.4:** `ROW_NUMBER()`, `DENSE_RANK()`, `LAG()`, `LEAD()`, `FIRST_VALUE()`, `LAST_VALUE()`, and window frame clauses (`ROWS BETWEEN ...`) throw a `ParserException`.

## Scalar Functions

| Function | Signature | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `LOWER` | `LOWER(expr)` | Converts text to lowercase. |
| `UPPER` | `UPPER(expr)` | Converts text to uppercase. |

::: warning Not Supported in v0.4
DataVo core SQL does **not** include `CASE WHEN`, `COALESCE`, `CAST`, `LEN`/`LENGTH`, `SUBSTRING`, `TRIM`, date/time functions, math functions, or SQL `COSINE_DISTANCE()`/`L2_DISTANCE()` scalar functions (the latter exist only as EF Core preview shims in `DataVoVectorDbFunctions`).
:::

## Operators

| Category | Operators | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Comparison | `=`, `!=`, `<>`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=` | Text comparisons are ordinal (UTF-8 code-point order). |
| Logical | `AND`, `OR`, `NOT` | Standard three-valued boolean logic. |
| Membership & Range | `IN (v1, v2, ...)`, `IN (SELECT ...)`, `BETWEEN a AND b` | `BETWEEN` on a clustered primary key performs a key-range seek. |
| Pattern & Null | `LIKE`, `NOT LIKE`, `IS NULL`, `IS NOT NULL` | `%` matches any sequence; `_` matches a single character. |
| Arithmetic | `+`, `-`, `*`, `/` | Supported in `SELECT`, `WHERE`, and `UPDATE SET` expressions. |
| Vector Distance | `<->` (L2 / Euclidean), `<=>` (Cosine) | Lower distance means closer. Valid in `SELECT`, `WHERE`, and `ORDER BY`. |

::: info Vector Operator Scope
Only `<->` (L2 / Euclidean) and `<=>` (Cosine) are supported in `v0.4`. There is **no** `<#>` inner-product operator.
:::

## See Also
- [SELECT & EXPLAIN](/manual/sql/statements/select) — Combining operators, aggregates, `GROUP BY`, `HAVING`, and `ORDER BY`
- [Vector Search](/manual/fundamentals/vector-search) — Indexing `<->` and `<=>` queries with `HNSW` and `FLAT`
- [SQL Compatibility](/manual/sql/compatibility) — Full dialect feature matrix

# Query Planner & Fast Paths

> Source route: /manual/internals/query-planner
> Source file: manual/internals/query-planner.md

DataVo does not use a cost-based optimizer. Instead, it pairs one general evaluator that can execute every supported SQL query with a cascade of **typed fast paths** that operate directly on stored bytes without boxing. Whether a query stays on a typed path is the single largest factor in its latency and allocation profile.

```csharp
using var db = new DataVoContext(new DataVoConfig { StorageMode = StorageMode.Lsm, DiskStoragePath = "./app_db" });

// Stays on the Typed Single-Table Path (index lookup or UTF-8 byte scan, ~16–24 KB alloc / 1M rows)
var stmt = db.Prepare("SELECT Id, Name, Score FROM players WHERE Region = @r AND Score >= @min");
var result = stmt.Execute(new DataVoQueryParameter("r", "EU"), new DataVoQueryParameter("min", 500));
```

## Dispatch Cascade

Every `SELECT` is offered to the fast paths in order. A fast path either returns the exact same rows as the general evaluator—in the same order—or declines cleanly; declining is never an error.

<div class="sketch-diagram">
  <img class="light-only" src="/manual/fig-05-planner-fast-paths-light.svg" alt="Query planner dispatch cascade trying Typed Single-Table, Typed Join, and Hybrid Vector paths before the General Evaluator fallback" />
  <img class="dark-only" src="/manual/fig-05-planner-fast-paths-dark.svg" alt="Query planner dispatch cascade trying Typed Single-Table, Typed Join, and Hybrid Vector paths before the General Evaluator fallback" />
</div>

The general evaluator materializes every scanned row as a `Dictionary<string, object?>` (2–4 KB per row read), which turns a 1,000,000-row scan into gigabytes of GC pressure and multi-second latency. Moving `OR`, `LIKE`, and multi-table joins onto typed paths reduced those queries from **1.7–5.0 s** down to **20–100 ms** ([DataVo vs SQLite](/manual/performance/datavo-vs-sqlite)).

## 1. Typed Single-Table Path

Accepts single-table queries whose `WHERE` clause combines `AND`, `OR`, `NOT`, column-vs-value comparisons (`=`, `<>`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`), `IS [NOT] NULL`, and `LIKE` / `NOT LIKE`, with any combination of aggregates, `GROUP BY`, `HAVING`, `ORDER BY`, `LIMIT`, and `OFFSET`.

| Access Method | When Selected | Mechanism |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Index point lookup** | Equality on PK or single-column B-tree index | Reads matching row keys in one index lookup, then fetches those rows by key. |
| **Primary-key range seek** | `BETWEEN` or `>=` / `<` on integer PK | On LSM, seeks SSTables and reads sequentially. On InMemory, binary-searches a lazily built sorted key copy (falls back to scan if range > 25% of table). |
| **SIMD columnar aggregate** | `COUNT`/`SUM`/`AVG`/`MIN`/`MAX` without `GROUP BY` on `[Columnar]` numeric columns | Reads 4,096-row columnar chunks with SIMD kernels; LSM skips chunks via `min`/`max`/`NULL`/`NaN` zone maps. |
| **Index-driven `GROUP BY`** | Whole-table `GROUP BY` on one indexed integer key with `COUNT(*)` / `COUNT(key)` | Streams finished groups in key order from the index without building a hash table. |
| **Full typed scan** | All other accepted predicates | Decodes only referenced columns in storage order; evaluates `WHERE` before materializing matches. |

Key implementation details:

- **Zero-allocation UTF-8 text matching:** On LSM, `=`, `<>`, `LIKE`, `NOT LIKE`, `IS [NOT] NULL`, and single-column text `GROUP BY` compare stored UTF-8 bytes directly without allocating `.NET` strings (falling back to UTF-16 decode only for `_` wildcards against non-ASCII text).
- **Bounded top-k sorting:** `ORDER BY ... LIMIT k` without a usable index compares sort-key cells in place against a bounded list of `k` winners, copying keys only when a row enters the top `k`.
- **Floating-point determinism on LSM:** `SUM` and `AVG` over `FLOAT`/`DOUBLE` columns are intentionally routed to the row scan when an LSM columnar index has an unflushed tail, guaranteeing bit-for-bit identical floating-point addition order. Integer sums, `COUNT`, `MIN`, and `MAX` are always pushed.

## 2. Typed Join Path

Accepts `INNER` and `LEFT` joins of any number of tables on integer equality keys, including per-table `WHERE` predicates (`OR`, `LIKE`), aggregates with or without `GROUP BY`, and top-N projections.

- **Hash join:** Streams the largest table (for all-`INNER` joins) or the `FROM` table (when a `LEFT JOIN` must preserve unmatched rows). Other tables are hashed on their join key, keeping only post-join columns. `INNER` filters apply during build; `LEFT` filters evaluate after NULL padding.
- **Key-only bit sets (`DenseInt64Set`):** When a joined table contributes only its key (such as `LEFT JOIN ... WHERE c.Id IS NULL` or existence checks) and keys are distinct and dense (≤ 64 span per key), DataVo packs them into a compact bit set (12.5 KB for 100,000 keys instead of a 2.9 MB hash table).
- **Index-driven probe:** For all-`INNER` joins where the hashed side is selective, a 32-key sample estimates fan-out; if ≤ 12.5% of the streamed table matches, DataVo probes via its single-column index in key order.

## 3. Hybrid Vector & General Fallback

- **Hybrid Vector Path:** Handles `ORDER BY embedding <=> @q LIMIT k` (and `<->`) with optional `WHERE` filters and joins. Over-fetches candidates by `LIMIT / selectivity`, evaluates typed predicates directly on stored candidate rows, and cost-routes HNSW searches to an exact SIMD Flat scan whenever the widened beam exceeds the graph crossover threshold. See [Vector Search](/manual/fundamentals/vector-search).
- **General Evaluator:** Executes `SELECT DISTINCT`, CTEs, computed select-list expressions, window functions (`RANK() OVER (...)`), `RIGHT`/`FULL`/`CROSS` joins, text/GUID joins, cross-table `OR` predicates, and joins inside explicit transactions. Single-table reads inside an explicit transaction remain on the typed scan over the MVCC snapshot.

## Compiled Queries & Planner Limits

Source-generated `[DataVoQuery]` methods and intercepted `DataVoTable<T>` LINQ queries bypass SQL parsing entirely and compile directly to typed byte-reading kernels (see [Compiled Scan Kernels](/manual/internals/compiled-scan-kernels)).

What the planner does **not** do:

- It does not keep persistent table statistics (index-probe decisions sample keys at runtime).
- It does not reorder arbitrary multi-way joins beyond selecting the streamed table and index probes.
- It does not use secondary indexes to satisfy `ORDER BY` or non-counting `GROUP BY` shapes.

## See Also
- [Zero-Allocation Row Model](/manual/internals/zero-allocation-rows) — Stack-only `RowRef` scans over stored bytes
- [Compiled Scan Kernels](/manual/internals/compiled-scan-kernels) — How Roslyn interceptors compile LINQ predicates into storage loops
- [DataVo vs SQLite](/manual/performance/datavo-vs-sqlite) — Measured latency across 28 SQL shapes and 5 hybrid vector queries

# Zero-Allocation Row Model

> Source route: /manual/internals/zero-allocation-rows
> Source file: manual/internals/zero-allocation-rows.md

DataVo can scan entire tables without allocating a single managed object per row. `RowRef` is a `readonly ref struct` that wraps a `ReadOnlySpan<byte>` over a row's stored bytes, and `RowRefStream` yields `RowRef` values to a `foreach` loop in 1,024-row pages. Once a thread has warmed up on a table's layout, a full scan allocates **0 bytes** on the managed heap.

```csharp
using DataVo.Core;

RowRefStream players = db.Table<Player>().StreamRef();

// Resolve column ordinals once before the loop (ordinal lookup allocates once)
int scoreCol = players.GetOrdinal("Score");

long totalScore = 0;
foreach (RowRef row in players)
{
    if (!row.IsNull(scoreCol))
    {
        totalScore += row.GetInt32(scoreCol);
    }
}
```

The same zero-allocation stream is available without a model type via `db.StreamRef("players")`.

## How `RowRef` Works

Conventional database drivers materialize a dictionary, `object[]`, or POCO for every row—200,000 rows means 200,000 heap allocations that the GC must later collect. `RowRef` avoids materialization entirely by decoding only the cells you read directly from the storage buffer.

<div class="sketch-diagram">
  <img class="light-only" src="/manual/fig-06-zero-alloc-rowref-light.svg" alt="FlatRowStore packed chunk copied in 1,024-row pages into a stack-only RowRef ref struct for zero-allocation column reads" />
  <img class="dark-only" src="/manual/fig-06-zero-alloc-rowref-dark.svg" alt="FlatRowStore packed chunk copied in 1,024-row pages into a stack-only RowRef ref struct for zero-allocation column reads" />
</div>

Because `RowRef` is a `ref struct`, the C# compiler enforces that it lives strictly on the stack—it cannot be boxed, stored on a class field, captured by a lambda, or held across an `await`. That compile-time guarantee makes it memory-safe for `RowRefStream` to reuse the same page buffer for the next 1,024 rows.

## Rules & Safety Guarantees

- **Iteration-scoped lifetime:** A `RowRef` is valid only inside the `foreach` iteration that produced it. Copy any value you need to retain past the loop body.
- **Span views follow the same lifetime:** `GetStringSpan` and `GetStringUtf8` return views directly into the row buffer; call `new string(span)` or copy the bytes if you need the text later.
- **Strict typing with lossless widening:** Accessors must match the column's declared type (with lossless widening: `INT` via `GetInt64`, `FLOAT` via `GetDouble`). Mismatched types throw `InvalidCastException`.
- **Explicit NULL checks:** Reading a NULL cell throws `InvalidOperationException`. Call `row.IsNull(ordinal)` first on nullable columns.
- **Table column order:** Ordinals follow `CREATE TABLE` order or the property declaration order on a `[DataVoTable]` model.

## Concurrency & Page Isolation

- **Non-blocking 1,024-row pages:** The engine acquires a short read lock only while copying a 1,024-row page into the stream buffer, then releases it before your loop body executes—slow consumers never stall writers.
- **Pass semantics:** Every row that exists for the entire pass is visited once; concurrent inserts or deletes may or may not appear. A concurrent schema change aborts the pass with `InvalidOperationException`.
- **Inside explicit transactions:** `StreamRef()` falls back to the query engine so it observes the transaction's own uncommitted writes. **That transactional path allocates.**

## What "Zero Allocation" Covers

Zero allocation applies specifically to `RowRefStream` scans and compiled scan-kernel aggregates—materializing a `Player` class instance still allocates the `Player` object itself.

| Operation | Managed Allocation |
| --- | ---: |
| Full `RowRefStream` pass (after thread warm-up) | **0 B** |
| Compiled LINQ `Count`/`Sum`/`Min`/`Max` over 200,000 rows | **0 B** |
| Compact `InMemory` PK lookup into `Player` (`FlatRowStore`) | **56 B** (the `Player` object itself) |
| `Lsm` PK lookup into `Player` | **144 B** |
| `RowRefStream` pass inside an explicit transaction | Allocates |

Nothing in `RowRef` or `RowRefStream` uses runtime reflection or `System.Reflection.Emit`; `DataVo.Core` compiles cleanly with `IsAotCompatible` and zero trim/AOT warnings.

## See Also
- [Streaming Queries](/manual/fundamentals/streaming-queries) — Comparing `Execute`, `StreamQuery`, and `StreamRef`
- [Compiled Scan Kernels](/manual/internals/compiled-scan-kernels) — Build-time LINQ kernels that run over stored bytes with 0 B allocation
- [Native AOT Deployment](/manual/client-interfaces/native-aot) — Publishing trimmed Native AOT binaries

# Compiled Scan Kernels

> Source route: /manual/internals/compiled-scan-kernels
> Source file: manual/internals/compiled-scan-kernels.md

When you write `db.Table<Player>().Where(static p => p.Score >= 100).Count()`, DataVo does not build an expression tree or invoke a delegate per row. Instead, the `DataVo.Generators` Roslyn source generator inspects the lambda at build time and emits a `[InterceptsLocation]` method with a value-type condition struct that tests stored row bytes directly inside the storage loop.

```csharp
// Intercepted at compile time → 0 B allocated per query, Native AOT safe
int topCount = db.Table<Player>()
    .Where(100, static (p, min) => p.Score >= min)
    .Count();

int totalScore = db.Table<Player>()
    .Where(100, static (p, min) => p.Score >= min)
    .Sum(static p => p.Score);
```

## Build-Time Compilation Pipeline

1. **Analyze:** The incremental Roslyn generator locates `DataVoTable<T>` query chains and validates static lambdas containing comparisons, boolean checks, null tests, `&&`, `||`, and parentheses.
2. **Emit interceptor:** For each qualifying call site, the generator emits an interceptor in the `DataVo.Generated` namespace marked with `[InterceptsLocation]`, routing that exact call to generated C# with zero runtime reflection.
3. **Specialize the condition struct:** When the predicate references only unindexed fixed-width columns (`int`, `long`, `float`, `double`, `bool`, `Guid`, `DataVoDate`, `DateOnly`), the generator emits a `struct` implementing the engine's predicate interface.
4. **Inline into the storage loop:** Because the storage scan is generic over the condition struct across `InMemory`, `Lsm`, and `Disk`, the JIT / Native AOT compiler inlines the predicate directly into the row loop—no virtual dispatch or delegate call per row.

## Fixed-Offset Byte Evaluation

When every column up to the last column referenced by the predicate has a fixed byte width, values sit at constant byte offsets in every row whose leading cells are non-null:

- **Single offset pass:** Byte offsets are computed once per scan; the loop tests leading null flags and reads cells straight from raw row spans without constructing a row view.
- **Automatic safe fallback:** Any row with a NULL in a leading column falls back to the general cell reader so results remain 100% identical.
- **Model layout tip:** Place fixed-width columns (`int`, `long`, `float`, `double`, `bool`, `Guid`) **before** variable-width `string` or `VECTOR` columns in your `[DataVoTable]` class to maximize fixed-offset kernel hits.

## Supported Compiled Aggregates

| Terminal Call | Compiled Kernel Support | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Count()`, `Any()` | Yes (unindexed fixed-width predicates) | Zero model allocations. |
| `Sum(selector)` | Yes (single non-nullable `int`, `long`, `float`, `double` column) | Accumulates in registers; integer overflow throws `OverflowException`. |
| `Min(selector)`, `Max(selector)` | Yes (single `int`, `long`, `float`, `double`, `DataVoDate`, `DateOnly` column) | Skips `NULL`; `NaN` orders below all numbers. |

When target columns are also marked `[Columnar]`, the kernel upgrades automatically to SIMD columnar chunk evaluation—achieving **27.5–90.1 µs** over 200,000 rows with **0 B allocated** (see [Benchmark Results](/manual/performance/benchmarks)).

Inside an explicit transaction, queries stream through the MVCC snapshot path instead of reading raw storage in place, so transactional scans allocate.

## Non-Compilable Shapes & Diagnostics

Any lambda shape the generator cannot compile—such as capturing a local variable instead of passing a state argument, calling an arbitrary C# method, performing arithmetic inside the predicate, or comparing two columns—still executes correctly by streaming and filtering with the original lambda. The compiler emits diagnostic warnings (`DATAVOL001`–`DATAVOL005`) explaining why the call was not intercepted. Predicates on `[PrimaryKey]` or `[Indexed]` columns continue using their index fast paths.

## See Also
- [Compiled LINQ](/manual/client-interfaces/compiled-linq) — Full list of supported LINQ operators and `DATAVOL001`–`DATAVOL005` diagnostics
- [Roslyn Source Generators](/manual/client-interfaces/source-generators) — Setting up `[DataVoTable]`, `[DataVoQuery]`, and `<InterceptorsNamespaces>`
- [Zero-Allocation Row Model](/manual/internals/zero-allocation-rows) — Manual zero-GC table scans with `RowRef`

# DataVo vs SQLite: When Each Engine Wins

> Source route: /manual/performance/datavo-vs-sqlite
> Source file: manual/performance/datavo-vs-sqlite.md

This guide compares DataVo v0.4 (`StorageMode.Lsm` and `StorageMode.InMemory`) against SQLite 3.50.4 (`WAL`, `synchronous=NORMAL`, plus `sqlite-vec` v0.1.9) across **28 relational SQL shapes** over 1,000,000 orders and **5 filtered nearest-neighbour vector queries**, with DuckDB 1.5.3 as an analytical reference. Every query's output is verified bit-for-bit against an independent oracle before timing begins.

**The short version:** DataVo wins on primary-key ranges (**1.4–1.7×**), secondary-index lookups (**2.4×**), low-to-medium cardinality `GROUP BY` (**3.2–4.7×**), integer-key `INNER`/`LEFT` joins (**2.3–10.3×**), SIMD columnar aggregates (**4.8–13.7×**), and filtered vector search (**3.0–71×**). SQLite wins on unindexed full-table scans (**1.05–1.8×**), unindexed `ORDER BY ... LIMIT` (**1.3×**), `LEFT JOIN` anti-joins (**1.07×**), and high-cardinality indexed `GROUP BY` on LSM (**1.4×**). DuckDB beats both on full-table analytical scans (**3–340×**) and trails both on key lookups and ranges.

## Executive Decision Guide

Medians compare DataVo LSM (`LsmStrictFsync = false`) against SQLite (`WAL`, `synchronous=NORMAL`), single-threaded client, 1,000,000 orders (Apple M4 Pro, .NET 10, 17 November 2026 runs).

| Workload Shape | Faster Engine | Speedup | Query IDs |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| Primary-key range read (100–10,000 rows) | **DataVo LSM** | 1.4–1.7× | R1–R4 |
| Primary-key range read (`InMemory` mode) | **SQLite** | 1.1–1.2× | R1–R4 |
| Indexed equality lookup (~1,000 rows) | **DataVo** | 2.4× | W1 |
| Unindexed full-scan filter (`=`, `OR`, `LIKE`) | **SQLite** | 1.05–1.35× | W2–W6 |
| Numeric `COUNT`/`SUM`/`MIN`/`MAX` with `[Columnar]` index | **DataVo** | 4.8–13.7× | C1, C2, C4, C6 |
| Numeric aggregate *without* a columnar index (or LSM `DOUBLE` `SUM`) | **SQLite** | 1.2–1.8× | C1–C4, C6 |
| Full-table `GROUP BY` (4–1,000 groups) | **DataVo** | 3.2–4.7× | G1, G2, C7 |
| High-cardinality indexed `GROUP BY` (~125k groups, `HAVING` + top-100) | **SQLite** (vs LSM) / **DataVo** (InMemory) | 1.4× / 1.8× | G3 |
| Unindexed `ORDER BY ... LIMIT 10` | **SQLite** | 1.3× | C8 |
| 2–3 table `INNER` / `LEFT` joins on integer keys | **DataVo** | 2.3–10.3× | J1–J4, J6, J7 |
| `LEFT JOIN ... WHERE c.Id IS NULL` (anti-join) | **SQLite** | 1.07× | J5 |
| Filtered top-10 vector search (exact, 384 / 1,536 dims) | **DataVo Flat** | 3.0–7.0× / 1.4–5.6× | V1–V4 |
| Filtered top-10 vector search (approximate, 100% recall on test data) | **DataVo HNSW** | 3.6–71× / 2.9–53× | V0–V4 |
| Full-table analytical scans & multi-threaded OLAP | **DuckDB** | 3–340× | All full scans |

## Three Rules Behind the Numbers

1. **Stay on a typed fast path:** DataVo is fast when a query runs on its typed single-table scan, typed integer-key join, SIMD columnar index, or hybrid vector path. Queries that fall back to the general evaluator (`DISTINCT`, CTEs, `RIGHT`/`FULL` joins, text/GUID joins, cross-table `OR`, or joins inside explicit transactions) allocate 2–4 KB per row and are substantially slower than SQLite. See [Query Planner & Fast Paths](/manual/internals/query-planner).
2. **SQLite's row decoder leads slightly on raw full scans:** When both engines touch all 1,000,000 rows without an index advantage, SQLite's record header offset table gives it a 1.05–1.8× edge over DataVo's sequential cell walk. DataVo wins full scans by doing less work—hashing instead of sorting for `GROUP BY`, or scanning 4,096-row columnar chunks with zone maps.
3. **Index coverage decides edge cases:** SQLite uses covering secondary indexes for high-cardinality `GROUP BY` and per-row probes. DataVo uses clustered PKs for ranges, secondary indexes for equality/selective inner joins, and single-column integer indexes for counting `GROUP BY` (nullable keys still require a null-flag pass on LSM).

## 28 Relational SQL Shapes (1,000,000 Orders) {#relational-results}

All relational queries run prepared statements with bound parameters against `Customers` (100k rows), `Products` (1k rows), and `Orders` (1M rows, 25% dangling `CustomerId`, 10% NULL `Discount`, exact multiples of `0.25` for bit-exact `DOUBLE` sums). Raw artifacts: [`2026-11-17-engine-perf-followups/`](https://github.com/ArintonAkos/DataVo-DBMS/tree/master/docs/public/benchmarks/2026-11-17-engine-perf-followups).

::: details Setup & Storage Footprint (1,101,000 rows)
| Metric | DataVo (LSM) | DataVo (InMemory) | SQLite | DuckDB |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Load 1,101,000 rows (ms) | 3,564 | 536 | 4,952 (incl. `ANALYZE`) | 1,014 |
| Close + reopen after load (ms) | 506 | – | 2.2 | 235 |
| Reopen again, nothing to flush (ms) | 8.0 | – | 0.4 | 3.7 |
| Size on disk (MB) | 90.8 | in memory | 83.8 | 54.3 |
| Create columnar index (ms) | 317 | 188 | – | – |

Nearly all of the 506 ms post-load reopen time is flushing trailing MemTables to SSTables on close; a clean reopen with nothing to flush takes 8.0 ms.
:::

::: details Joins (J1–J7)
Median latency per call (p99 in brackets). Ratio = SQLite / DataVo LSM (> 1 means DataVo is faster).

| Query | DataVo (LSM) | DataVo (InMemory) | SQLite | DuckDB | SQLite / DataVo |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| **J1** 3-table inner join, `COUNT`, `SUM`, no filter | 70.2 ms (82.9 ms) | 90.2 ms | 721 ms (740 ms) | 2.11 ms | **10.3×** |
| **J2** J1 + `WHERE c.Region = @r AND p.CategoryId = @cat` (~0.2%) | 21.9 ms (23.4 ms) | 10.8 ms | 84.4 ms | 1.51 ms | **3.85×** |
| **J3** J2 returning rows, `ORDER BY o.Amount DESC, o.Id LIMIT 50` | 16.1 ms (20.0 ms) | 12.8 ms | 84.0 ms | 1.86 ms | **5.22×** |
| **J4** `LEFT JOIN`: `COUNT(*)`, `COUNT(c.Id)`, `SUM` | 68.3 ms (78.9 ms) | 93.1 ms | 238 ms | 3.37 ms | **3.48×** |
| **J5** `LEFT JOIN ... WHERE c.Id IS NULL` (anti-join) | 39.1 ms (39.3 ms) | 81.8 ms | 36.6 ms | 3.30 ms | 0.936× |
| **J6** Orders × Customers, `GROUP BY c.Region` | 130 ms (141 ms) | 195 ms | 764 ms | 3.40 ms | **5.87×** |
| **J7** Products (2%) × Orders, `COUNT`, `SUM` | 6.70 ms (9.62 ms) | 6.20 ms | 15.3 ms | 1.05 ms | **2.29×** |

**Mechanisms:** SQLite executes J1, J4, and J6 as index nested-loop joins (1M B-tree descents). DataVo uses hash joins, index-driven probes (J2, J3, J7), and a 12.5 KB `DenseInt64Set` bit set for key-only tables (J1, J4, J5—cutting per-call allocation to 31–41 KB). SQLite narrowly wins J5 (36.6 ms vs 39.1 ms) because DataVo pays per-row cell walking plus rebuilding the bit set per call.
:::

::: details Filters (W1–W6)
| Query | DataVo (LSM) | DataVo (InMemory) | SQLite | DuckDB | SQLite / DataVo |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| **W1** `WHERE ProductId = @p` (indexed, ~1,000 rows) | 341 µs (658 µs) | 184 µs (479 µs) | 825 µs (920 µs) | 1.13 ms | **2.42×** |
| **W2** `WHERE ProductTag = @p` (no index, ~1,000 rows) | 30.5 ms (33.4 ms) | 66.5 ms | 28.6 ms | 553 µs | 0.941× |
| **W3** `(Status = 'PAID' OR Status = 'SHIPPED') AND Amount >= @lo AND Amount < @hi` | 64.0 ms (66.0 ms) | 76.3 ms | 61.1 ms | 2.11 ms | 0.955× |
| **W4** W3 `AND Discount IS NOT NULL AND Discount < @d` | 74.2 ms (78.1 ms) | 84.7 ms | 63.3 ms | 2.08 ms | 0.853× |
| **W5** `Sku LIKE 'S0042%'` (no index) | 47.6 ms (48.0 ms) | 33.2 ms | 42.2 ms | 2.85 ms | 0.888× |
| **W6** `Sku LIKE '%042-%'` (no index) | 68.7 ms (70.3 ms) | 41.9 ms | 50.7 ms | 4.16 ms | 0.738× |

**Mechanisms:** DataVo compares UTF-8 bytes directly in stored LSM rows without decoding `.NET` strings (16–24 KB allocated per 1M-row scan, down from 36–46 MB). SQLite stays 1.05–1.35× ahead on W2–W6 due to O(1) column-offset headers vs. DataVo's cell walk.
:::

::: details Primary-Key Ranges (R1–R4)
| Query | DataVo (LSM) | DataVo (InMemory) | SQLite | DuckDB | SQLite / DataVo |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| **R1** `Id BETWEEN @lo AND @hi` (100 rows) | 13.6 µs (20.5 µs) | 22.9 µs (45.2 µs) | 18.5 µs (24.6 µs) | 178 µs | **1.36×** |
| **R2** `Id >= @lo AND Id < @hi` (100 rows) | 12.9 µs (19.3 µs) | 23.0 µs (31.6 µs) | 18.2 µs (23.5 µs) | 180 µs | **1.41×** |
| **R3** `BETWEEN` (10,000 rows) | 1.01 ms (12.0 ms) | 2.13 ms (15.2 ms) | 1.76 ms (1.95 ms) | 588 µs | **1.74×** |
| **R4** `>= AND <` (10,000 rows) | 991 µs (11.9 ms) | 1.99 ms (13.7 ms) | 1.74 ms (1.85 ms) | 588 µs | **1.76×** |

LSM seeks clustered SSTables sequentially (1.4–1.7× faster than SQLite). InMemory binary-searches a sorted key copy and performs random slot lookups (1.1–1.2× slower than SQLite). The 10,000-row p99 spike (11–14 ms) is GC from materializing 3.0–3.4 MB of result rows per call.
:::

::: details GROUP BY (G1–G3)
| Query | DataVo (LSM) | DataVo (InMemory) | SQLite | DuckDB | SQLite / DataVo |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| **G1** `GROUP BY Status` (4 groups) | 50.5 ms (50.7 ms) | 67.0 ms | 237 ms | 1.12 ms | **4.70×** |
| **G2** `GROUP BY Bucket` (1,000 groups) | 63.4 ms (65.9 ms) | 51.4 ms | 209 ms | 727 µs | **3.30×** |
| **G3** `GROUP BY CustomerId HAVING COUNT(*) >= @k ORDER BY N DESC, CustomerId LIMIT 100` (~125k groups) | 44.2 ms (48.1 ms) | 16.7 ms | 30.5 ms | 4.40 ms | 0.691× |

**Mechanisms:** DataVo hashes G1/G2 without boxing (UTF-8 byte keys for `Status`, 26.7 KB allocated) while SQLite sorts into a temporary B-tree. On G3, DataVo streams counts from `ix_orders_customer` (InMemory beats SQLite by 1.8×, 929 KB allocated), while LSM still scans nullable `CustomerId` null flags to count the NULL group.
:::

::: details Columnar Index (C1–C8)
`CREATE INDEX cx_orders ON Orders (Amount, Qty, Bucket, Discount, ProductTag) USING COLUMNAR`. Every query allocates 16–48 KB per call on DataVo LSM.

| Query | DataVo (LSM) | DataVo (LSM) + index | DataVo (InMemory) + index | SQLite | DuckDB | SQLite / DataVo + index |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| **C1** `COUNT(*) WHERE Amount >= @lo AND Amount < @hi` | 53.5 ms | **3.18 ms**, pushed | 3.27 ms, pushed | 43.7 ms | 1.13 ms | **13.7×** |
| **C2** `SUM(Qty) WHERE Bucket < @b` | 67.2 ms | **3.44 ms**, pushed | 3.73 ms, pushed | 36.7 ms | 415 µs | **10.7×** |
| **C3** `SUM(Amount) WHERE Qty >= @q` (`DOUBLE` sum) | 65.1 ms | 65.9 ms, row scan | **3.05 ms**, pushed | 39.9 ms | 459 µs | 0.606× |
| **C4** `COUNT(*), SUM(Qty), MIN/MAX(Amount) WHERE Bucket < @b AND Discount IS NOT NULL` | 86.7 ms | **11.9 ms**, pushed | 8.48 ms, pushed | 57.4 ms | 1.38 ms | **4.82×** |
| **C5** `COUNT(*) WHERE Status = @s AND Amount >= @lo` (string col) | 40.0 ms | 39.9 ms, row scan | 45.9 ms, row scan | 42.7 ms | 984 µs | **1.07×** |
| **C6** `COUNT(*) WHERE (Qty = 1 OR Qty = 2) AND Amount >= @lo` | 64.1 ms | **4.77 ms**, pushed | 497 µs, pushed | 35.6 ms | 1.69 ms | **7.45×** |
| **C7** `GROUP BY Bucket`: `COUNT(*)`, `SUM(Qty)` | 63.1 ms | 63.2 ms, row scan | 50.9 ms, row scan | 200 ms | 744 µs | **3.17×** |
| **C8** `ORDER BY Amount DESC, Id LIMIT 10` | 53.0 ms | 52.9 ms, row scan | 46.7 ms, row scan | 41.6 ms | 1.31 ms | 0.786× |

**Why C3 is not pushed on LSM:** When an LSM columnar index has an unflushed tail, floating-point `SUM`/`AVG` falls back to the row scan to preserve bit-identical key-order addition. On InMemory (which is in key order), C3 is pushed at 3.05 ms.
:::

## Hybrid Vector & SQL Search {#hybrid-vector-and-sql}

Measured on `Docs (Id, Category, Price, AuthorId, Emb VECTOR(d))` with 128 normalized clusters, 200 held-out queries, and `Authors` (2,000 rows, 10 countries). DataVo runs prepared `ORDER BY Emb <=> @q LIMIT 10` on LSM (`FLAT` or `HNSW`, default settings) against `sqlite-vec` `vec0` metadata-filtered exact KNN.

- **100% Recall@10** across every shape, engine, and dimension; **0 short results** and **0 filter violations**.
- **384 dims (50,000 rows):** DataVo Flat is **3.0–8.3×** faster than `sqlite-vec`; HNSW is **3.6–70×** faster (`0.26 ms` unfiltered, `0.67–3.62 ms` filtered).
- **1,536 dims (20,000 rows):** DataVo Flat is **1.4–7.0×** faster; HNSW is **2.9–53×** faster (`0.60 ms` unfiltered, `1.40–6.10 ms` filtered).
- **Planner optimizations:** Stored-row candidate filtering cut per-query allocation 20–35× (to 183–232 KB at 384 dims); HNSW automatically cost-routes to an exact SIMD Flat scan when candidate expansion widens the beam past ~9% (384d) or ~20% (1,536d) of the dataset; `enable_diversity_heuristic` is enabled by default for clustered recall.

::: details Full Hybrid Vector Tables (384d & 1,536d) + HNSW Ablation
#### 384 Dimensions, 50,000 Rows
| Shape | DataVo Flat | DataVo HNSW | SQLite + sqlite-vec | sqlite-vec / Flat | sqlite-vec / HNSW |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Load + index build | 442 ms | 1,628 ms | 653 ms | | |
| **V0** Top-10, no filter | 2.19 ms (3.96 ms) | 0.26 ms (0.54 ms) | 18.2 ms (18.5 ms) | **8.3×** | **70×** |
| **V1** `Category = @c AND Price < 50` (~5%) | 2.64 ms (6.87 ms) | 2.48 ms (6.61 ms) | 9.78 ms (10.4 ms) | **3.7×** | **3.9×** |
| **V2** `Price < 50` (~50%) | 2.04 ms (4.15 ms) | 0.67 ms (1.92 ms) | 14.4 ms (15.0 ms) | **7.0×** | **22×** |
| **V3** V1 + `JOIN Authors` | 2.56 ms (6.16 ms) | 2.42 ms (5.63 ms) | 9.76 ms (10.5 ms) | **3.8×** | **4.0×** |
| **V4** `JOIN Authors WHERE a.Country = @k` (~10%) | 4.34 ms (8.13 ms) | 3.62 ms (6.10 ms) | 13.1 ms (16.1 ms) | **3.0×** | **3.6×** |

#### 1,536 Dimensions, 20,000 Rows
| Shape | DataVo Flat | DataVo HNSW | SQLite + sqlite-vec | sqlite-vec / Flat | sqlite-vec / HNSW |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Load + index build | 485 ms | 2,039 ms | 3,952 ms | | |
| **V0** Top-10, no filter | 4.57 ms (5.71 ms) | 0.60 ms (0.95 ms) | 32.0 ms (33.0 ms) | **7.0×** | **53×** |
| **V1** (~5%) | 4.69 ms (10.6 ms) | 4.66 ms (9.49 ms) | 15.4 ms (16.6 ms) | **3.3×** | **3.3×** |
| **V2** (~50%) | 4.16 ms (8.25 ms) | 1.40 ms (3.26 ms) | 23.5 ms (24.5 ms) | **5.6×** | **17×** |
| **V3** V1 + `JOIN Authors` | 4.61 ms (10.4 ms) | 4.52 ms (9.58 ms) | 15.4 ms (18.7 ms) | **3.3×** | **3.4×** |
| **V4** (~10%, author filter) | 12.2 ms (14.6 ms) | 6.10 ms (10.1 ms) | 17.4 ms (18.5 ms) | **1.4×** | **2.9×** |

#### HNSW Diversity Heuristic Ablation (128 Clusters)
| Construction Setting | Dims | Build | Recall@10 | 0%-Recall Queries (default / ef=512) | Median Query |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Nearest neighbours only (old default) | 384 | 1,690 ms | 83.6% | 20 / 19 | 0.158 ms |
| **Diversity heuristic (v0.4 default)** | 384 | 1,592 ms | **100.0%** | **0 / 0** | 0.166 ms |
| Nearest neighbours only (old default) | 1,536 | 1,800 ms | 87.5% | 15 / 12 | 0.284 ms |
| **Diversity heuristic (v0.4 default)** | 1,536 | 1,900 ms | **100.0%** | **0 / 0** | 0.421 ms |

*Note:* Commit `5cbcd14` marks `SimdDistanceKernels` with `[MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveOptimization)]` to eliminate tiered-JIT cold-start jitter on Flat V0 (stabilizing 15 reruns at 2.21–2.28 ms, p99 3.0–4.2 ms).
:::

## Oracle Verification & Caveats {#correctness-findings}

The initial 14 November oracle run caught **5 correctness bugs** (outer-join predicate pushdown `B1`, `COUNT(DISTINCT)` parsing `B2`, aliased vector filter extraction `B3`, multi-join key alignment `B4`, and cross-table vector join filters `B5`), plus two closeout fixes (short filtered vector fallback and `WHERE ... HAVING` without `GROUP BY`). All are fixed with regression tests on both LSM and InMemory engines.

::: details Correctness Findings Log (B1–B5)
| # | Query Shape | Bug Before Fix | Fix Commit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **B1** | `LEFT JOIN ... WHERE c.Id IS NULL` (J5) | Returned `0` instead of `250,395` (filtered before NULL padding) | `bfb1390` — filter after outer join |
| **B2** | `COUNT(DISTINCT CustomerId)` | Returned `2,000` instead of `175` (`DISTINCT` dropped) | `6743521` — parsed & routed to general path |
| **B3** | Vector top-10 + `JOIN` with table alias (V3) | Returned 0–2 rows (alias `d` didn't match table `Docs`) | `8ce4295` — resolve qualifiers via table service |
| **B4** | 3-table join with `AND` across two dimensions (J2/J3) | Returned `0` rows instead of `1,827` (mismatched key order) | `fd81cf8` — canonical table key ordering |
| **B5** | Vector top-10 + `JOIN Authors WHERE a.Country = @k` (V4) | 9/10 rows failed filter (`a.Country` dropped) | `8ce4295` — pre-filter, join, and expand candidates |
:::

**Scope limits:** Single Apple M4 Pro machine, warm OS page cache, read-only timed queries, and ADO.NET client overhead included for SQLite/DuckDB. On x64 Linux/Windows runners, DataVo's scan lead over SQLite is 2–2.8× narrower (see [Benchmark Results](/manual/performance/benchmarks#part-iii-platforms)). Treat differences under ~20% in single-run scenarios as within measurement noise.
