# Benchmark Results & Methodology

> Source route: /manual/performance/benchmarks
> Source file: manual/performance/benchmarks.md

This page summarizes DataVo's performance across **BenchmarkDotNet microbenchmarks**, **systems workloads** (durability, concurrency, reactive IVM, vector search, and 1M-row SQL), and **cross-platform CI runners** (macOS Apple Silicon, Linux x64, Windows x64), along with the methodology and caveats behind every number.

> **Looking for the latest v0.4 SQL & hybrid vector numbers?** See [DataVo vs SQLite: When Each Engine Wins](/manual/performance/datavo-vs-sqlite) for the 28-query 1M-row SQL matrix and 5 filtered vector shapes.

## Executive Summary

| Workload | DataVo Result | Comparison | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **PK point lookup (100k rows)** | **52.1 ns** (InMemory, 56 B) · **236 ns** (LSM, 144 B) | SQLite: 736 ns / 1,609 ns (608 B) · DuckDB 1t: 65–75 µs | M4 Pro, compiled LINQ (`FlatRowStore` compact layout) |
| **Filtered aggregates (200k rows, `[Columnar]`)** | **27.5–90.1 µs** (0 B alloc, InMemory & LSM) | SQLite: 3,915–6,051 µs · DuckDB 1t: 141–740 µs | 2.6–8.9× faster than 1-thread DuckDB; 14–71× faster than row scan |
| **Filtered aggregates (200k rows, row scan)** | **386–526 µs** (InMemory, 0 B) · **2.0–2.3 ms** (LSM) | SQLite: 3.7–5.9 ms · DuckDB 1t: 137–716 µs | 8.8–9.8× faster than SQLite on M4 Pro; 3.5–4.7× on x64 CI |
| **Reactive IVM (3-table join, 50k updates)** | **191.7 ms** (3.1 µs P50) | DuckDB: 34.3 s (179×) · SQLite: 126.1 s (658×) | Incremental Z-set updates vs. full-query polling |
| **Durable commits (`fsync` per update)** | **4.04 ms** P50 (Mac) · **2.42 ms** (Win) · **0.223 ms** (Linux) | SQLite `full+fullfsync`: 4.04 ms (Mac) · 2.51 ms (Win) · 0.097 ms (Linux) | Hardware flush dominates on Mac/Win; SQLite leads 2.3× on fast-flush Linux VM |
| **Relaxed YCSB 80/20 (12 threads)** | **510,695 ops/s** (0.66 ms write P99) | SQLite WAL `NORMAL`: 261,618 ops/s (3.77 ms write P99) | 1.95× throughput, 5.7× lower write tail; neither mode is power-loss durable |
| **Disk footprint (1M rows)** | **27.7 MB** (LSM) | SQLite: 29.1 MB · LiteDB: 154.5 MB | 5% smaller than SQLite; warm reopen in 1.5–4.3 ms |

## Part II: Systems Workloads

Application-shaped scenarios from `demos/Research.Benchmark` (single run per scenario; treat differences under ~20% as not established).

### Streamed Risk Views (Incremental View Maintenance)

Inserting 50,000 orders one-by-one and reading a live dashboard after each insert. DataVo maintains the view incrementally via Z-sets; SQLite and DuckDB re-run indexed queries.

![Streamed risk, complex VIP exposure](/benchmarks/ivm-complex-vip-total-time.png)

![Streamed risk, simple exposure](/benchmarks/ivm-simple-exposure-total-time.png)

- **Complex VIP 3-table join:** DataVo finishes in **191.7 ms** (3.1 µs P50), **179×** faster than DuckDB (`34.3 s`) and **658×** faster than SQLite (`126.1 s`), because incremental work is O(1) per order rather than O(N) re-joining.
- **Simple single-table exposure:** DataVo (`526.9 ms`, 6.4 µs P50) and SQLite (`574.1 ms`, 8.9 µs P50) are closely matched (1.1–1.4× across 4 runs), while DuckDB pays per-query setup overhead (`52.95 s`).

### Durability, Concurrency & Space

![Disk CRUD total time](/benchmarks/disk-crud-wal-time.png)

![Thread scaling](/benchmarks/thread-scaling-throughput.png)

![YCSB write P99](/benchmarks/ycsb-write-p99.png)

- **Strict durability (`fsync` per commit):** DataVo LSM Production (`84.6 s`, `4.04 ms` P50) and SQLite `WAL + full + fullfsync` (`84.9 s`, `4.04 ms` P50) tie on Apple Silicon because both wait on the same SSD cache flush. Group commit scales Production throughput **3.7×** from 1 to 32 threads.
- **Relaxed durability (OS buffer):** DataVo Relaxed beats SQLite WAL `NORMAL` by **1.4×** on serial updates (`113 ms` vs `155 ms`) and **1.95×** on 12-thread YCSB 80/20 (`510.7k` vs `261.6k ops/s`, with **5.7×** lower write P99).

### Vector Search (10,000 × 1,536d)

![Vector search total time](/benchmarks/vector-search-total-time.png)

![HNSW versus Flat](/benchmarks/vector-hnsw-vs-flat.png)

- On **uniform random** 1,536d vectors at 10k scale, exact **Flat** search (`298.7 ms` total, `1.96 ms` P50) beats both `sqlite-vec` (`472.8 ms`) and HNSW (`1,634 ms` total, 63.5% recall) because uniform high-dimensional distances concentrate.
- On **clustered** embeddings (realistic workloads), HNSW is **8×** faster per query at 10k vectors (`0.25 ms`, 95.9% recall) and **15×** faster at 50k (`0.68 ms`, 90.2% recall). Since v0.4, `enable_diversity_heuristic` is enabled by default, raising clustered Recall@10 to 100% on the hybrid benchmark dataset.

::: details Full Part II Raw Tables (IVM, Disk CRUD, Thread Scaling, YCSB, Space, Vector Recall, Flat/Doc/Concurrent)

| Simple Exposure | SQLite | 574.1 | 8.9 µs | 24.6 µs | 200.7 MB |
| Simple Exposure | DuckDB | 52,954.0 | 983 µs | 3,311 µs | 208.3 MB |

| Complex VIP Join | DuckDB | 34,339.1 | 660 µs | 974 µs | 131.3 MB |
| Complex VIP Join | SQLite | 126,064.4 | 2,527 µs | 4,375 µs | 115.6 MB |

#### Other Workloads (Flat CRUD, Deep Document, Concurrent Ops)
- **Flat CRUD (50k insert + 50k lookup, in-memory):** DataVo `63.9 ms` (`0.54 µs` P50) vs SQLite `128.8 ms` (`1.17 µs`) vs LiteDB `1,322.8 ms`.
- **Deep document (5k nested orders):** DataVo `83.6 ms` (`5.0 µs` P50) vs SQLite `140.8 ms` (`7.8 µs`) vs LiteDB `431.2 ms`.
- **Concurrent ops (8 readers + 2 writers, 5 s, M4 Pro):** DataVo `1,852,526 ops/s` (`48 µs` read P99, `0.11 ms` write P99) vs SQLite `372,220 ops/s` (`120 µs` read P99, `5.13 s` write P99).

## SQL over 1,000,000 rows {#sql-over-1-000-000-rows}

The `sql-workload` scenario runs prepared SQL text over 1,000,000 file-backed rows (DataVo LSM Relaxed vs. SQLite WAL `NORMAL`, DuckDB, and LiteDB).

> **v0.4 Update:** Key range scans were upgraded to SSTable seeks (**12.9 µs** for 100 rows vs. SQLite's **18.2 µs**), and `ORDER BY ... LIMIT 10` eliminated per-row sort-key boxing (**48 KB** vs. 84 MB). See [DataVo vs SQLite](/manual/performance/datavo-vs-sqlite) for the latest v0.4 measurements across all 28 SQL shapes.

## Part III: Cross-Platform CI Results {#part-iii-platforms}

To verify portability beyond Apple Silicon, the full suite runs on GitHub Actions (`ubuntu-latest` x64, `windows-latest` x64, and `macos` M1 VM). Latest CI refresh: **20 November 2026** (`master` @ `02fa240f`, run `44748508039`).

![Mean time of a filtered COUNT and of a primary-key lookup across four machines](/benchmarks/ci-bdn-by-platform.png)

![Median latency of one durable update on three platforms](/benchmarks/ci-durable-update-latency.png)

![Total time of the vector scenario on three platforms](/benchmarks/ci-vector-search-time.png)

Key cross-platform findings:

- **Point lookups (20 Nov refresh):** Linux x64 `130.8 ns` (Memory, 56 B) / `288.3 ns` (LSM, 144 B) vs. SQLite `1,398 ns` / `3,643 ns`. Windows x64 `239.6 ns` (Memory) / `666.9 ns` (LSM) vs. SQLite `2,024 ns` / `6,741 ns`.
- **Columnar aggregates (20 Nov refresh, 200k rows):** Linux x64 `9.29 µs` (`COUNT`) and `27.7–40.6 µs` (`SUM`/`MIN`/`MAX`, 0 B alloc); Windows x64 `16.2 µs` and `84.3–102.9 µs`—outperforming both SQLite and 1-thread DuckDB on all platforms.
- **Concurrent ops (20 Nov refresh):** On 4-vCPU runners, DataVo sustains **1.53M ops/s** on both Linux (`302,878` writes, `0.125 ms` write P99) and Windows (`98,696` writes, `1.084 ms` write P99), resolving the earlier writer starvation observed on 4-core VMs.
- **Durability differences:** On Linux VMs with fast virtual-disk flushes (`~0.1 ms`), SQLite's durable update (`0.097 ms`) leads DataVo Production (`0.223 ms`). On Windows (`~2.5 ms`) and macOS (`~4.0 ms`), hardware flush latency dominates and both engines tie.
- **SIMD paths:** `SimdDistanceKernels` auto-dispatches AVX2 (256-bit) on x64, AdvSimd/NEON (128-bit) on Arm64, and `TensorPrimitives` / `Vector<T>` on portable targets.

::: details Cross-Platform CI Tables, Unity IL2CPP Smoke & Historical Audit (July → November)
#### Latest CI Refresh (20 November 2026, `master` @ `02fa240f`, Run `44748508039`)
- **YCSB 80/20 (4 threads):** Linux DataVo Relaxed `230,912 ops/s` (`0.43 ms` write P99) vs SQLite `98,295 ops/s` (`3.20 ms`). Windows DataVo Relaxed `70,735 ops/s` (`1.05 ms` write P99) vs SQLite `33,256 ops/s` (`7.49 ms`).
- **Space & recovery (1M rows):** `28.15 MB` on disk vs SQLite `29.08 MB`; Relaxed warm reopen `1.65 ms` (Linux) / `3.86 ms` (Windows).

#### Platform Scaling Summary (12 November CI Run `43189115522`)
| Scenario | Engine | Linux x64 | Windows x64 | Apple M4 Pro (local) |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Complex VIP (50k insert + read) | DataVo | 532 ms | 506 ms | 192 ms |
| | DuckDB | 116,020 ms | 134,356 ms | 34,339 ms |
| | SQLite | 234,852 ms | 249,796 ms | 126,064 ms |
| Vector search (10k × 1,536d) | DataVo Flat | 552 ms | 812 ms | 299 ms |
| | SQLite + `sqlite-vec` | 2,276 ms | 2,681 ms | 473 ms |
| Durable update P50 (50k updates) | DataVo Production | 0.223 ms | 2.42 ms | 4.04 ms (20k) |
| | SQLite (`full`) | 0.097 ms | 2.51 ms | 4.04 ms (20k) |

#### Unity IL2CPP Smoke (macOS Standalone, Aggressive Stripping)
`scripts/run-unity-macos-il2cpp-player-smoke.sh` passed on Unity `6000.5.4f1` (universal arm64/x86_64, `UnityLinker --rule-set=Aggressive`, 0 AOT/linker warnings), verifying Unity `Vector2`/`Vector3`/`Vector4`/`Quaternion` storage plus `Lsm` and `Disk` persistence. This is a correctness proof, not a timing benchmark.

#### What Changed Since July 2026 (v0.1 Alpha Audit) {#what-changed-since-july}
- **Strict durability:** July's `502 ms` ("417× faster than SQLite") did not wait for stable storage and was withdrawn; commit `befede4` enforced durable visibility (`84.6 s`, matching SQLite's `84.9 s`).
- **Flat vector allocation:** July's `10.3 MB` was not reproducible; current `61.7 MB` reflects one copy of the 10,000 × 6,144 B input vectors during insert.
- **Disk footprint (1M rows):** Dropped from `66.4 MB` to `27.7 MB` (5% smaller than SQLite) after clustered primary keys landed.
:::

## Methodology & Known Limits

All benchmarks use deterministic seeded datasets, Release builds on .NET 10, and pre-timing answer verification against either DataVo (Part I) or an independent mathematical oracle (`sql-matrix` / `hybrid-vector`).

| Durability Label | What a Commit Waits For | Power-Loss Durable |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **DataVo LSM Production** (`LsmStrictFsync = true`) | WAL reaches stable storage (`fsync`) | Yes |
| **SQLite WAL `full` + `fullfsync=1`** | WAL reaches stable storage (`fsync`) | Yes |
| **DataVo LSM Relaxed** (`LsmStrictFsync = false`) | OS page-cache write only | No |
| **SQLite WAL `NORMAL`** | OS page-cache write only | No |

Only configurations with matching durability should be compared. Key caveats:

- **Managed vs. native memory:** `GC.GetAllocatedBytesForCurrentThread` and `GC.GetTotalAllocatedBytes(precise: true)` measure .NET managed allocations only; SQLite's page cache and DuckDB's native buffers are excluded.
- **Warm OS page cache:** Reopen benchmarks run immediately after writing in the same process; they verify zero-scan open time, not cold-disk boot or crash replay.
- **Single-run variance:** Part I (BenchmarkDotNet) provides 99.9% confidence intervals; Part II and CI scenarios run once per workload, so treat margins under ~20% as noise.
- **API overhead:** SQLite and DuckDB are measured through ADO.NET (the standard .NET client path), while DataVo uses its native compiled LINQ and prepared-statement APIs.

## See Also
- [DataVo vs SQLite](/manual/performance/datavo-vs-sqlite) — Detailed v0.4 28-query SQL matrix and hybrid vector guide
- [Reproducing Benchmarks](/manual/performance/reproducing-benchmarks) — CLI cookbook to run every benchmark suite locally
- [LSM Storage & Durability](/manual/fundamentals/lsm-and-durability) — Configuring `LsmStrictFsync`, compaction, and WAL recovery

# Reproducing Benchmarks

> Source route: /manual/performance/reproducing-benchmarks
> Source file: manual/performance/reproducing-benchmarks.md

Every chart and table in the performance documentation can be reproduced from the repository root using Release builds on .NET 10. Run scenarios **serially** on an idle machine—parallel runs contend on CPU and storage flushes and invalidate latency tails.

```bash
# 1. Capture environment metadata first
git rev-parse HEAD && dotnet --info && uname -a

# 2. Build the research benchmark host once
dotnet build demos/Research.Benchmark/src/Research.Benchmark.Host -c Release
DLL=demos/Research.Benchmark/src/Research.Benchmark.Host/bin/Release/net10.0/Research.Benchmark.Host.dll
```

## 1. SQL Matrix & Hybrid Vector (`DataVo vs SQLite`)

Reproduces the 28-query 1,000,000-row SQL comparison and 5 filtered nearest-neighbour shapes in [DataVo vs SQLite](/manual/performance/datavo-vs-sqlite).

```bash
# 28 relational SQL shapes over 1,000,000 orders (~2 min, ~1.2 GB peak RAM)
dotnet "$DLL" --scenario sql-matrix > sql-matrix.md 2> sql-matrix.log

# Filtered vector search (50k × 384d and 20k × 1,536d; requires SQLITE_VEC_PATH)
SQLITE_VEC_PATH=$PWD/vec0.dylib dotnet "$DLL" --scenario hybrid-vector > hybrid-vector.md
SQLITE_VEC_PATH=$PWD/vec0.dylib dotnet "$DLL" --scenario hybrid-vector --vectors 20000 --dimensions 1536 > hybrid-vector-1536.md
```

Useful filters: `--records 100000` (fast 1-minute smoke), `--queries J5,C8` (specific shapes), `--engine datavo,datavo-mem,sqlite,duckdb` (or `datavo-flat,datavo-hnsw,sqlite`).

::: details Installing `sqlite-vec` v0.1.9 (`SQLITE_VEC_PATH`)
**macOS arm64:**
```bash
curl -sL -o /tmp/svec.tgz https://github.com/asg017/sqlite-vec/releases/download/v0.1.9/sqlite-vec-0.1.9-loadable-macos-aarch64.tar.gz
tar xzf /tmp/svec.tgz -C /tmp && export SQLITE_VEC_PATH=/tmp/vec0.dylib
```

**Linux x64:**
```bash
curl -sL -o /tmp/svec.tgz https://github.com/asg017/sqlite-vec/releases/download/v0.1.9/sqlite-vec-0.1.9-loadable-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
tar xzf /tmp/svec.tgz -C /tmp && export SQLITE_VEC_PATH=/tmp/vec0.so
```

**Windows x64 (PowerShell):**
```powershell
curl.exe -L -o $env:TEMP\svec.tgz https://github.com/asg017/sqlite-vec/releases/download/v0.1.9/sqlite-vec-0.1.9-loadable-windows-x86_64.tar.gz
tar -xzf $env:TEMP\svec.tgz -C $env:TEMP
$env:SQLITE_VEC_PATH = "$env:TEMP\vec0.dll"
```
:::

## 2. BenchmarkDotNet Microbenchmarks (Part I)

Runs the statistical microbenchmark suite (`benchmarks/DataVo.Benchmarks`, ~15 minutes) comparing DataVo, SQLite, and DuckDB on identical data. Outputs Markdown, CSV, and HTML reports to `BenchmarkDotNet.Artifacts/results/`.

```bash
dotnet run -c Release --project benchmarks/DataVo.Benchmarks -- --filter '*'
```

## 3. Systems Workloads (Part II)

| Scenario | Command | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Flat CRUD** | `dotnet "$DLL" --scenario flat-crud --format markdown` | 50k inserts + 50k in-memory lookups |
| **Disk CRUD WAL** | `dotnet "$DLL" --scenario disk-crud-wal --records 20000 --format markdown` | ~3 min (20k strict `fsync` commits) |
| **Thread Scaling** | `dotnet "$DLL" --scenario thread-scaling --engine datavo-lsm-relaxed --format markdown` | Use `--engine all` to include strict mode |
| **YCSB Mixed 80/20** | `dotnet "$DLL" --scenario ycsb-mixed --records 100000 --format markdown` | Multi-threaded read/write tail latency |
| **Space & Recovery** | `dotnet "$DLL" --scenario space-and-recovery --records 1000000 --format markdown` | 1M rows, disk size & warm reopen |
| **Vector Search** | `dotnet "$DLL" --scenario vector-search --vectors 10000 --dimensions 1536 --queries 100 --topk 10 --format markdown` | Requires `SQLITE_VEC_PATH` |
| **HNSW vs. Flat Recall** | `dotnet run -c Release --project demos/Research.Benchmark/tools/VectorRecall` | Held-out recall@10 (~1 min) |
| **Reactive IVM** | `dotnet "$DLL" --scenario simple-exposure --format markdown` and `--scenario complex-vip` | Single-table & 3-table Z-set IVM |
| **Other Workloads** | `--scenario deep-document`, `--scenario concurrent-ops`, `--scenario sql-workload` | App-shaped & 1M-row SQL workloads |

Always keep durability settings explicit when comparing strict vs. relaxed LSM:

```csharp
var strict  = new DataVoConfig { StorageMode = StorageMode.Lsm, DiskStoragePath = "./bench_strict",  LsmStrictFsync = true };
var relaxed = new DataVoConfig { StorageMode = StorageMode.Lsm, DiskStoragePath = "./bench_relaxed", LsmStrictFsync = false };
```

## 4. Arena Live Views, Unity IL2CPP & Charts

```bash
dotnet "$DLL" --scenario arena-live-views --profile gameplay --engine all --repetitions 7 --output /private/tmp/datavo-arena-gameplay --format markdown
```

```bash
bash scripts/run-unity-macos-il2cpp-arena-cross-engine.sh
bash scripts/run-unity-arena-editor-tests.sh
bash scripts/run-unity-macos-il2cpp-arena.sh
```
*Do not compare Unity IL2CPP timings directly with desktop .NET timings; evaluate each lane independently with its canonical checksums.*
:::

::: details Regenerating Charts & CI Workflow Artifacts
**Regenerate PNG charts** (requires Python 3, `matplotlib`, `numpy`; IVM plots also require `rsvg-convert`):

# Configuration Reference

> Source route: /manual/reference/configuration
> Source file: manual/reference/configuration.md

`DataVoConfig` configures every aspect of an embedded `DataVoContext`. Most applications only set `StorageMode`, `DiskStoragePath`, and `LsmStrictFsync`; every other property ships with production-ready defaults.

```csharp
using DataVo.Core;
using DataVo.Core.StorageEngine.Config;

using var db = new DataVoContext(new DataVoConfig
{
    StorageMode = StorageMode.Lsm,
    DiskStoragePath = "./game_data",
    LsmStrictFsync = true
});
```

## Storage & Durability

| Property | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `StorageMode` | `StorageMode.InMemory` | Storage backend: `InMemory`, `Lsm`, `Disk` (legacy), `Wasm` (browser playground), or `Custom`. |
| `DiskStoragePath` | `null` | Directory for persisted `Lsm` and `Disk` files. Guarded by a single-process `datavo.lock`. |
| `CustomStorageEngine` | `null` | Custom `IStorageEngine` instance when `StorageMode = StorageMode.Custom`. |
| `WasmStorageEngine` | `null` | Browser storage engine when `StorageMode = StorageMode.Wasm`. |
| `LockAcquireTimeoutMs` | `30000` | Maximum milliseconds to wait for a lock before failing (`-1` waits indefinitely). |
| `WalEnabled` | `true` (`Disk`), `false` (other) | Enables WAL in legacy `Disk` mode. |
| `SyncDiskWrites` | `false` | Forces fsync on legacy `Disk` mode writes. |
| `WalFilePath` | `"datavo.wal"` | Legacy `Disk` WAL file name or path. |
| `WalCheckpointThreshold` | `1000` | Legacy `Disk` WAL entry threshold before checkpointing. |
| `WalCheckpointIntervalMs` | `1000` | Background WAL checkpoint interval (ms) for `IoSchedulerMode.GroupCommit`. |
| `TransactionIdStateFilePath` | `"datavo.txid"` | Persisted MVCC transaction ID watermark file. |
| `CheckpointStateFilePath` | `"datavo.ckpt"` | Persisted binary WAL checkpoint LSN watermark file. |

## LSM & I/O

| Property | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `LsmStrictFsync` | `true` | `true` flushes the LSM commit log to stable storage before acknowledging writes; `false` (Relaxed) acknowledges in OS page cache. |
| `LsmReadMode` | `LsmReadMode.Auto` | `Auto` memory-maps SSTables on 64-bit platforms; `PositionalRead` uses standard file reads. |
| `ClusteredPrimaryKeys` | `true` | Stores new LSM tables with single-column `INT` or `GUID` primary keys clustered under that key. |
| `IoSchedulerMode` | `IoSchedulerMode.Off` | Disk I/O scheduler mode (`Off`, pooled positioned I/O, or `GroupCommit`). |
| `EnableZeroAllocCompiledUpdate` | `true` | Allows eligible fixed-width single-row compiled `UPDATE`s to byte-patch stored rows in place. |

The LSM MemTable flush threshold (32 MB) is an internal engine constant rather than a `DataVoConfig` property.

## Execution & Planner

### Vector & Hybrid Query Routing

| Property | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `EnableVectorPredicateFastPath` | `true` | Uses the vector index for `WHERE v <=> @q < threshold` and filtered distance `ORDER BY`. |
| `VectorPredicateFastPathMinRows` | `128` | Minimum table row count before invoking the vector index fast path. |
| `VectorPredicateFastPathCandidateMultiplier` | `3` | Multiplier from estimated qualifying rows to initial index candidates. |
| `VectorPredicateFastPathMaxTopKRatio` | `0.6` | Falls back to plain filtering when candidate requests exceed this share of the table. |
| `VectorPredicateFastPathMaxTopK` | `20000` | Hard cap on candidates requested from the vector index. |
| `VectorPredicateFastPathMaxExpansionPasses` | `2` | Maximum candidate-expansion retries before switching to a filter-first exact scan. |
| `VectorPredicateFastPathExpansionFactor` | `2` | Candidate growth multiplier per expansion pass. |
| `EnableHybridOrderByAdaptiveInitialTopK` | `true` | Sizes the initial candidate request from estimated filter selectivity (`LIMIT / selectivity`). |

HNSW graph parameters (`m`, `ef_construction`, `ef_search`) are configured per index in SQL. See [Vector Search](/manual/fundamentals/vector-search).

### Experimental Volcano & Telemetry Switches

`EnableVolcanoExecution` (default `false`) and its `Volcano*` spill, external-sort, aggregate-partitioning, and join-feedback properties control an experimental operator pipeline used for planner testing; leave `EnableVolcanoExecution = false` in production.

Telemetry flags (`EnableVectorPredicateFastPathTelemetry`, `EnableHybridRoutingTelemetryCounters`, `EnableHybridRoutingPerQueryTelemetry`, `HybridRoutingTelemetrySnapshotIntervalQueries`) record hybrid vector routing diagnostics for benchmarks.

## Security & Auth

| Property | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `EnableAuthorization` | `false` | Enforces users, roles, and SQL `GRANT`/`REVOKE` checks. |
| `Username`, `Password` | `""` | Credentials for the default session principal (or supply `PasswordHash` + `PasswordSalt`). |
| `Role`, `Roles` | `ReadWrite`, `[]` | Built-in role and custom role names assigned to the session principal. |
| `AllowAnonymousSession` | `true` | Permits unauthenticated sessions when `EnableAuthorization` is `true`. |
| `AnonymousRole` | `DatabaseRole.ReadOnly` | Role granted to anonymous sessions. |
| `AuthorizationUsers` | `[]` | List of `DataVoAuthUser` principals provisioned at startup. |

## See Also

- [Storage Modes](/manual/fundamentals/storage-modes) — Comparing `InMemory`, `Lsm`, and legacy `Disk`
- [LSM & Durability](/manual/fundamentals/lsm-and-durability) — `LsmStrictFsync` trade-offs and recovery guarantees
- [ADO.NET Provider](/manual/client-interfaces/ado-net) — Connection string keys (`StorageMode`, `DataSource`, `WalEnabled`)

# Error Handling

> Source route: /manual/reference/error-handling
> Source file: manual/reference/error-handling.md

Every failed SQL statement in `DataVoContext.Execute` returns a `QueryResult` with `IsError = true`, a human-readable message in `Messages`, and a stable `ErrorCode` from `DataVoErrorCodes`. Syntax errors also populate `ErrorLine` and `ErrorColumn`. Always branch on `ErrorCode` rather than message text.

```csharp
using DataVo.Core.Contracts.Results;

QueryResult result = db.Execute(
    "INSERT INTO players (id, name, score) VALUES (1, 'Ada', 1200)")[0];

if (result.IsError && result.ErrorCode == DataVoErrorCodes.PrimaryKeyViolation)
{
    Console.WriteLine("Player 1 already exists.");
}
```

## Error Surfaces by API

Every DML statement and bulk insert is all-or-nothing: if any row violates a constraint, nothing from that statement is written.

| API Layer | Failure Surface | Error Code Property |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DataVoContext.Execute` / `Prepare` | `QueryResult` (`IsError = true`) | `result.ErrorCode`, `ErrorLine`, `ErrorColumn` |
| `Insert<T>`, `InsertTyped`, `InsertTypedBatch`, `BulkInsert` | `ConstraintViolationException` | `ex.ErrorCode` |
| `DataVo.Data` (ADO.NET / Dapper) | `DataVo.Data.DataVoException` | `ex.ErrorCode`, `ex.Line`, `ex.Column` |
| `DataVo.EntityFrameworkCore` | `DataVoEfException` | `ex.ErrorCode` (propagated from the engine or EF bridge) |

```csharp
try
{
    cmd.ExecuteNonQuery();
}
catch (DataVo.Data.DataVoException ex) when (ex.ErrorCode == DataVoErrorCodes.Deadlock)
{
    // Retry transaction after deadlock victim selection
}
```

## Error Code Catalog (`DataVoErrorCodes`)

### Syntax & Input (`DV1xxx`)

| Code | Constant | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DV1001_SYNTAX` | `Syntax` | Invalid or incomplete SQL. Check `ErrorLine` and `ErrorColumn`. |
| `DV1002_EMPTY_STATEMENT` | `EmptyStatement` | The input string contained no executable statement. |

### Binding & Catalog (`DV2xxx`)

| Code | Constant | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DV2001_NO_DATABASE_SELECTED` | `NoDatabaseSelected` | No active database; run `USE <database>` first. |
| `DV2002_UNKNOWN_DATABASE` | `UnknownDatabase` | Referenced database does not exist (`USE` keeps the prior selection). |
| `DV2003_UNKNOWN_TABLE` | `UnknownTable` | Table does not exist in the active database. |
| `DV2004_UNKNOWN_COLUMN` | `UnknownColumn` | Column does not exist on the target table. |
| `DV2005_UNKNOWN_INDEX` | `UnknownIndex` | Index does not exist. |
| `DV2006_AMBIGUOUS_COLUMN` | `AmbiguousColumn` | Unqualified column matches multiple joined tables; qualify with table/alias. |
| `DV2007_UNKNOWN_TABLE_ALIAS` | `UnknownTableAlias` | Qualified reference names a table or alias not in the query. |
| `DV2101_DATABASE_EXISTS` | `DatabaseExists` | Database already exists. |
| `DV2102_TABLE_EXISTS` | `TableExists` | Table already exists. |
| `DV2103_INDEX_EXISTS` | `IndexExists` | Index already exists on the table. |
| `DV2900_BINDING` | `Binding` | Uncategorized binding error. |
| `DV2901_CATALOG` | `Catalog` | Uncategorized catalog error. |
| `DV2902_INDEX` | `Index` | Uncategorized index error. |

### Constraints (`DV3xxx`)

| Code | Constant | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DV3001_PRIMARY_KEY_VIOLATION` | `PrimaryKeyViolation` | Duplicate primary key value. |
| `DV3002_NULL_PRIMARY_KEY` | `NullPrimaryKey` | Primary key column received `NULL`. |
| `DV3003_UNIQUE_VIOLATION` | `UniqueViolation` | Duplicate value in a `UNIQUE` column. |
| `DV3004_FOREIGN_KEY_VIOLATION` | `ForeignKeyViolation` | Missing parent row or blocked parent delete. |
| `DV3005_NOT_NULL_VIOLATION` | `NotNullViolation` | `NOT NULL` column received `NULL`. |

### Type & Evaluation (`DV4xxx`)

| Code | Constant | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DV4001_TYPE_MISMATCH` | `TypeMismatch` | Value does not match column type (e.g., `'abc'` for `INT`). |
| `DV4002_VALUE_TOO_LONG` | `ValueTooLong` | String exceeds `VARCHAR(n)` length (values are never silently truncated). |
| `DV4003_VALUE_COUNT_MISMATCH` | `ValueCountMismatch` | `VALUES` count does not match target column count. |
| `DV4004_DIVISION_BY_ZERO` | `DivisionByZero` | Division by zero during expression evaluation. |
| `DV4900_EVALUATION` | `Evaluation` | Uncategorized expression evaluation error. |

### Transactions, Auth, Storage & Internal (`DV5xxx`–`DV9xxx`)

| Code | Constant | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DV5001_NO_ACTIVE_TRANSACTION` | `NoActiveTransaction` | `COMMIT` or `ROLLBACK` called without an active `BEGIN`. |
| `DV5002_TRANSACTION_ALREADY_ACTIVE` | `TransactionAlreadyActive` | `BEGIN` called while a transaction is already active in the session. |
| `DV5003_DEADLOCK` | `Deadlock` | Transaction selected as deadlock victim; safe to retry. |
| `DV6001_PERMISSION_DENIED` | `PermissionDenied` | Active session lacks required privileges. |
| `DV7001_DATABASE_IN_USE` | `DatabaseInUse` | Data directory is locked by another process or opened with incompatible settings. |
| `DV7900_STORAGE` | `Storage` | Uncategorized storage I/O or engine failure. |
| `DV9000_ERROR` | `General` | General unclassified error. |
| `DV9001_INTERNAL` | `Internal` | Unexpected internal failure; please file a bug report with the offending statement. |

## See Also

- [DataVoContext API](/manual/client-interfaces/datavo-context-api) — Checking `QueryResult` on SQL execution
- [ADO.NET Provider](/manual/client-interfaces/ado-net) — Catching `DataVoException`

# Limits & Unsupported Features

> Source route: /manual/reference/limits
> Source file: manual/reference/limits.md

This page documents the explicit architectural boundaries and unsupported features of DataVo `v0.4` (`0.4.0-rc.1`) so you can evaluate fit without guessing from source code or roadmap notes.

## Architectural & Storage Limits

| Boundary | Behavior in `v0.4` (`0.4.0-rc.1`) |
| --- | --- |
| **Process ownership** | Single-process write ownership enforced via `datavo.lock`. Multiple contexts/connections inside one process share one engine; a second process opening the same directory fails with `DV7001_DATABASE_IN_USE`. |
| **Deployment model** | Embedded in-process only. No wire protocol server, replication daemon, or HA clustering (`DataVo.Server` for PostgreSQL-wire GUI clients like DBeaver/DataGrip is unscheduled). |
| **Prerelease storage format** | On-disk structures may evolve before `1.0`. Maintain seed or export/import scripts across prerelease upgrades. |
| **Vector dimensions** | Fixed per column at `CREATE TABLE` (`VECTOR(n)`). Inserted vectors must match the declared dimension. |
| **LSM MemTable flush size** | Fixed internal constant of 32 MB (not a `DataVoConfig` setting). |
| **Transaction isolation** | Snapshot isolation with first-committer-wins conflict detection. Full serializable isolation and predicate-range phantom prevention are **not** provided (write skew is possible). |
| **HNSW vector recall** | HNSW is approximate; measure recall on your own embeddings or use `USING FLAT` / `exact: true` when exact nearest neighbors are required. |

## Query-Shape Performance Limits

Correctness does not depend on query shape, but allocation and latency do. Queries outside the compiled/typed fast paths execute on the general dictionary evaluator, which allocates a dictionary per row read (seconds and gigabytes on million-row tables):

- `SELECT DISTINCT`
- `RIGHT`, `FULL`, and `CROSS` joins
- Joins on text (`VARCHAR`) or `GUID` keys
- `OR` predicates spanning two joined tables
- Computed expressions in the `SELECT` list
- Window functions (`RANK()`) and common table expressions (CTEs)
- Any SQL query executed inside an explicit `BEGIN ... COMMIT` transaction

See [Query Planner](/manual/internals/query-planner) for how to stay on zero-allocation fast paths.

## SQL `DATE` Contract

DataVo provides a calendar `DATE` type (`YYYY-MM-DD`) and has **no** `DATETIME` or `TIMESTAMP` column type:

- Store timestamps or points in time as `BIGINT` (UTC ticks or Unix milliseconds).
- In C# models and source-generated projections, SQL `DATE` maps to `DataVo.Core.DataVoDate` across all targets, and additionally supports `System.DateOnly` on `.NET 10`.
- `System.DateTime` properties are not mapped to SQL `DATE`.

## Unsupported Features

| Category | Not Supported in `v0.4` (`0.4.0-rc.1`) |
| --- | --- |
| **PostgreSQL compatibility** | Not PostgreSQL-compatible. No PostgreSQL wire protocol, no `pg_class`/`pg_attribute` system catalogs, and no PostgreSQL role catalog. |
| **SQL clauses & expressions** | No views (`CREATE VIEW`), `INTERSECT`, `EXCEPT`, `CASE WHEN`, `CAST`, `COALESCE`, `PRAGMA`, date/math SQL functions, or window functions other than `RANK()`. |
| **Procedural SQL** | No stored procedures, functions, or triggers. |
| **Text collation** | Ordinal comparison only; `LIKE` is case-sensitive. |
| **Vector operators & functions** | No `<#>` inner-product operator; no core SQL `COSINE_DISTANCE()`/`L2_DISTANCE()` functions (only `<->` L2 and `<=>` Cosine operators; function shims exist only in EF Core preview). |
| **EF Core bridge** | No EF migrations, shadow properties, complex LINQ joins, broad `GroupBy` translation, or Native AOT support. |
| **ADO.NET** | No `DbProviderFactory`, no connection pooling, no async cancellation via `CommandTimeout`/`Cancel()`. |
| **WebAssembly / npm** | `DataVo.Browser` is an experimental playground runtime for documentation only; no production npm package is published. |

## See Also

- [SQL Compatibility](/manual/sql/compatibility) — Full SQL dialect support matrix
- [SQL Data Types](/manual/sql/data-types) — Supported column types and C# mappings
- [Transactions & MVCC](/manual/fundamentals/transactions-and-mvcc) — Snapshot isolation contract and write-conflict behavior
- [Query Planner](/manual/internals/query-planner) — Fast paths vs. general evaluator

# AI Access & MCP

> Source route: /manual/reference/ai-access
> Source file: manual/reference/ai-access.md

DataVo publishes a curated, AI-readable Markdown export of the `v0.4.0-rc.1` manual alongside the VitePress site. Only public manual pages are exported — internal architecture notes, audits, and raw source directories are excluded.

## Static AI Endpoints

| Endpoint | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `/llms.txt` | Concise entry point listing all 38 public manual pages |
| `/llms-full.txt` | Complete public manual concatenated into a single Markdown file |
| `/ai/index.json` | Structured JSON index mapping routes to Markdown export paths |
| `/ai/pages/<route>.md` | Canonical Markdown export for an individual page (e.g., `/ai/pages/manual/getting-started/quickstart.md`) |
| `/mcp/datavo-docs.json` | Local stdio MCP server discovery config |
| `/mcp/remote-docs.json` | HTTP-retrievable page index for remote AI tools |

Every manual page also displays a **Copy page for AI** button at the top that copies the canonical Markdown export directly to your clipboard.

## Local Stdio MCP Server

GitHub Pages hosts the static Markdown and discovery JSON files, while local coding assistants can run the stdio MCP server directly from the `docs` directory:

```bash
cd docs
npm run docs:ai
npm run mcp
```

The MCP server restricts access strictly to the curated public manual:

```text
get_doc("/manual/getting-started/quickstart")  -> public Markdown
get_doc("architecture/index-manager.md")       -> Access Denied
```

::: details MCP Client Configuration Example
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "datavo-docs": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["./mcp/datavo-docs-server.cjs"],
      "cwd": "./docs"
    }
  }
}
```
:::

- [Quickstart](/manual/getting-started/quickstart) — Get started in C# in 60 seconds.
